news.Title: Why Arm Holdings Stock Plummeted by Nearly 10% Today
news.Content:
If Friday's stock trading session goes down in history, it will be due to the heavy sell-off of semiconductor stocks. One company caught in the downpour was U.K.-based Arm Holdings , which fell by almost 10% on that gloomy day for its industry.

The big rout

The chip stock rout can be traced to one major factor -- Intel 's (NASDAQ:INTC) third-quarter earnings release , published just after market close on Thursday. It wasn't that this was chock-full of bad news, as the company reported double-digit revenue growth and substantial gains in its data center and artificial intelligence (AI) reporting unit.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Rather, it was the unexpectedly weak guidance it proffered for its current (fourth) quarter. Not only is the bellwether semiconductor company predicting sequential and substantial declines in revenue, gross margin, and non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share, but its projections came in well under analyst estimates.

The following day, investor panic was palpable, with a wide range of chip stocks taking heavy losses, including Arm. Although Intel isn't quite the leading benchmark in the semiconductor industry it once was, such weak guidance is being seen as a canary in the coal mine for the sector.

Sinking as a group

When developments like this happen, markets tend to overreact by overselling. I feel that's the case for most of the chip stocks suffering collateral damage from Intel's guidance.

That said, like Intel, Arm is vulnerable to the current contraction in PC shipments, not to mention rising component costs. The factors impacting the chip giant will also affect Arm.

I've always found the company's asset-light business model appealing -- it licenses its advanced chip technology and isn't a manufacturer, so it might be less exposed than Intel. But I'd hold off on snapping up its beaten-down shares until we get the company's update in the form of its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results, slated for publication next Wednesday, Nov. 4, after market close.

news.Title: Wall Street's Next Blockbuster Stock Split Has Arrived -- The Stock Has Gained 3,050% Since Its 2025 Debut and Still More Upside Ahead, According to Wall Street
news.Content:
Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have shifted the tech landscape, minting a string of stock winners along the way. One of those is Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK). It's been less than a year since it was spun off from Western Digital in early 2025. In the short time since its debut, Sandisk has become a Wall Street darling, as it supplies memory chips used to underpin AI.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The company's impressive business performance has fueled a surge in its stock price. Sandisk shares have surged 378% thus far in 2026 (as of this writing), and are up 4553% over the past year and 3,050% since its spin-off.

In conjunction with its fiscal 2027 first-quarter financial report, Sandisk announced plans to split its stock for the first time since its debut. This long-rumored announcement has sparked a wave of interest in the semiconductor stock .

Let's take a look at the details, the company's recent results, and why Wall Street thinks there is still upside ahead.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The details

After the market close on Thursday, Sandisk announced that its board of directors had approved an 8-for-1 stock split. "The stock split will be effected through an amendment to Sandisk's Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation," the company noted in its earnings report.

Shareholders of record as of Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, will receive an additional seven shares of stock for each share they own. Those shares will be distributed after the close of business on Thursday, Nov. 19. The stock is expected to begin split-adjusted trading when the market opens on Friday, Nov. 20.

As is typically the case, shareholders won't need to take any action to participate in the stock split. The brokerage or investment bank will handle the details behind the scenes, and shares will be deposited directly into investors' brokerage accounts once the stock split has taken effect.

The process is complex, so the additional shares may not show up immediately after the market close on Nov. 19. The schedule may vary slightly from brokerage to brokerage, and it may take several days for the newly minted shares to appear.

Actual numbers help provide context. For each share of Sandisk stock an investor holds -- currently trading for roughly $1,200 per share (as of this writing) -- post-split, shareholders will own 8 shares worth $150 each.

Story Continues

What's driving the gains?

Sandisk's financial results help illustrate the surging demand for its memory chips. For its fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Oct. 2), the company generated revenue of $11 billion, which surged 378% year over year and 23% quarter over quarter. This drove adjusted earnings per share (EPS) that soared more than 40-fold to $49.51.

For context, analysts' consensus estimates were calling for revenue of $10.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $46.67, so the company cleared both hurdles with ease.

Management's commentary was equally revealing. CEO David Goeckeler noted, "We're hearing from our customers that they have underestimated the amount of NAND they need to run their infrastructure." He went on to say that multiple customers have revised their contracts to increase the amount of supply. CFO Luis Visoso went further, noting that "Our [memory] pipeline exceeds our supply throughout the end of the decade."

Investors have expressed concerns about the durability of AI demand and the emerging potential for competition from China, but Sandisk has taken steps to ensure its windfall continues. The company has shifted to long-term supply agreements with major customers, locking them into minimum prices, with the average duration of the contract lasting four years or longer.

Is Sandisk stock a buy?

Wall Street is bullish about Sandisk's future prospects. Of the 25 analysts who offered an opinion in October, 84% rate it a buy or strong buy. Furthermore, Wall Street's average price target for the stock is about $2,143, implying additional upside of 85%.

Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes is far more bullish than his Wall Street colleagues, with a buy rating and $3,600 price target -- the highest on Wall Street -- suggesting the stock could triple from here.

He cites strong demand for High-Bandwidth Flash memory, firm NAND pricing, and strong free cash flow as the basis for his bullish thesis. Reitzes believes Sandisk can buy back as much as $100 billion in stock over the next three years.

The stock has fallen more than 50% from its peak in late June, fueled by concerns about the resilience of AI demand and the potential for emerging competition from China. However, Sandisk now trades for less than 16 times earnings and 5 times forward earnings.

For investors who believe, as I do, that this is just the beginning for AI, Sandisk stock is a compelling buy.

news.Title: FORM Drops 12% Post Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
news.Content:
FormFactor FORM shares dropped 11.65% on Thursday following third-quarter 2026 results despite reporting better-than-expected earnings and revenues. The selloff appears to reflect investor concerns about slowing near-term revenue growth, capacity constraints, normalization of unusually strong gross margins and earnings, and temporary profitability pressures associated with the company's new Farmers Branch manufacturing facility. Nevertheless, we believe the dip offers an investing opportunity due to rising demand for AI semiconductor testing, expanding opportunities in GPUs and custom ASICs, growing high-bandwidth memory (HBM) complexity, and accelerating adoption of co-packaged optics. So, what should investors do with the stock? Let's dig deep to find out.

FORM to Remain Under Pressure Due to Weak Q4 Guidance

FormFactor expects fourth-quarter revenues of $285 million, plus or minus $10 million, indicating just 1.6% sequential growth at the midpoint compared with 8.6% growth in the third quarter. The company projects non-GAAP earnings of 95 cents per share, down 8.7% sequentially from $1.04. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to decline from 56.5% to 54%, while operating expenses are projected to rise from $64.4 million to approximately $69 million. The combination of slower revenue growth, higher operating expenses and declining profitability likely weighed on investor sentiment despite the company's impressive third-quarter performance.

FormFactor also acknowledged that its existing manufacturing footprint is approaching maximum production capacity after achieving nearly 40% year-over-year revenue growth without significant facility expansion. Although manufacturing efficiency improvements have increased output, opportunities for further productivity gains are diminishing. The new Farmers Branch facility is expected to provide additional capacity, but its production capability will ramp gradually throughout 2027.

The Farmers Branch manufacturing expansion presents near-term execution and profitability challenges. FormFactor expects its 2027 non-GAAP gross margin to remain near the current normalized baseline of 53%, as higher production volumes and operational improvements offset temporary inefficiencies associated with the factory ramp. Moreover, the company expects approximately $25-$30 million in preproduction expenses in 2026, with certain costs shifting from operating expenses to cost of revenues as production begins.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at 80 cents per share, unchanged over the past 60 days and indicating 74% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure. The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 revenues is pegged at $278.8 million, suggesting 29.6% growth from the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

Story Continues

FormFactor, Inc. Price and Consensus

FormFactor, Inc. price-consensus-chart | FormFactor, Inc. Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.05 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days and indicating 134.6% growth over 2025's reported figure. The consensus mark for 2026 revenues is pegged at $1.03 billion, suggesting 31.7% growth from 2025's reported figure.

FORM Shares Are Trading at a Premium

FormFactor shares are trading at a premium, as suggested by a Value Score of F.

In terms of the forward 12-month price-to-sales (P/S), the company is trading at 6.46X compared with the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 5.6X. Peers, including Cohu COHU, Teradyne TER and KLA KLAC trade at 3.50X, 7.79X and 11.50X, respectively.

FORM Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Facility Expansion & Strong HBM Demand Aids FORM's Prospect

FormFactor's nearly 300,000-square-foot Farmers Branch manufacturing facility is a major long-term growth catalyst. The company has completed initial assembly and testing qualifications and shipped its first production probe card to a leading customer. FORM expects the facility to reach approximately $400 million in annualized probe-card production capacity by the end of 2027. The expansion should alleviate existing production constraints and enable FormFactor to address growing opportunities across GPUs, advanced CPUs and custom ASICs. The facility's modular design also provides flexibility for additional capacity expansion beyond 2027.

The company is positioned to capitalize on rising demand for advanced semiconductor testing as AI workloads drive adoption of high-performance GPUs and hyperscaler-developed custom ASICs. Increasing chip complexity, higher-speed interfaces, rising power density and advanced chiplet packaging architectures are expanding the need for high-performance MEMS probe-card technologies. As Farmers Branch adds capacity, FormFactor expects to gain meaningful market share across GPU and custom ASIC applications in 2027.

Increasing HBM complexity represents another compelling long-term opportunity for FormFactor. Although HBM probe-card revenues declined sequentially in the third quarter because of customer product-mix adjustments, FORM expects continued strong growth supported by development programs for next-generation HBM4E and HBM5 architectures. Higher memory speeds, increasingly complex stacked designs and demanding production-test requirements should support demand for advanced probing solutions. FormFactor's SmartMatrix DRAM probe-card architecture provides differentiated high-speed testing capabilities with improved productivity and parallelism. The company's strength in final-stack testing also positions it to benefit from evolving HBM architectures, potentially offsetting concerns related to specification changes

These factors are expected to strengthen FORM's competitive position against broader semiconductor competitors, including Teradyne, Cohu and KLA on a trailing 12-month basis. Shares of Cohu, KLA and Teradyne have returned 124.5%, 38.5% and 63%, respectively, compared with FORM's 77.4% return.

FORM Stock's Price Performance

Meanwhile, FormFactor's expanding relationships with leading semiconductor test equipment providers like Teradyne and Advantest strengthen its competitive advantages. Improving operating model provides another reason for long-term optimism. FormFactor expects Farmers Branch to become gross-margin accretive after its initial ramp is completed. The company continues to target a longer-term operating model of $1.6 billion in revenues, 55% gross margin and $5 in non-GAAP earnings per share.

Conclusion

FormFactor's sharp post-earnings decline appears to be primarily due to near-term earnings normalization and manufacturing capacity limitations rather than a deterioration in underlying semiconductor testing demand. The company's expanding exposure to AI processors, custom ASICs, advanced HBM architectures and optical interconnect technologies provides multiple avenues for sustained growth. Moreover, the Farmers Branch expansion and improving manufacturing efficiencies strengthen its long-term competitive positioning.

FormFactor currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which implies that investors should accumulate the stock on the dip. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold AEIS Stock Before Q3 Earnings Release?
news.Content:
Advanced Energy AEIS is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 2.

For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million. Non-GAAP earnings are projected to be $3 per share, plus or minus 25 cents.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter revenues is currently pegged at $646.39 million, indicating growth of 39.52% from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $3.06 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. The figure indicates a 75.86% increase from the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. Quote

Advanced Energy beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in the trailing four quarters, delivering an average surprise of 14.79%.

Let's see how things have shaped up for the upcoming announcement.

Factors Likely to Have Influenced AEIS's Q3 2026 Performance

Advanced Energy's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from robust demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) data center infrastructure, improving industrial and medical market conditions and increasing adoption of next-generation power solutions. Higher production volumes, favorable product mix and improved manufacturing efficiencies are also likely to have supported profitability in the to-be-reported quarter.

The Semiconductor business is likely to have benefited from strong demand for leading-edge memory and logic manufacturing, driven by increasing investments in advanced semiconductor technologies. Rising etch and deposition intensity, particularly in advanced DRAM, NAND and logic processes, is expected to have supported demand for Advanced Energy's precision power solutions. The company's eVerest and eVoS plasma power platforms are gaining traction due to their improved yield and throughput capabilities. Production ramps of existing products and new design wins in plasma and system power applications are expected to have supported growth in the quarter to be reported. Management anticipates semiconductor revenues to increase nearly 50% year over year in the second half of 2026.

The Data Center Computing business is expected to have benefited from accelerating hyperscaler investments in AI infrastructure and growing demand for high-efficiency, high-density power solutions. Resolution of downstream supply-chain constraints, increasing deployments of next-generation AI computing platforms and expanding engagements with existing hyperscale customers are likely to have driven sequential revenue growth.

The Industrial & Medical business is likely to have benefited from recovering market conditions, improving distributor demand and production ramps of previously secured design wins. Strength in test and measurement, factory automation, robotics, aerospace and defense, medical imaging and electrosurgery applications is expected to have supported sequential revenue growth. Increased factory output and improving order trends are additional positives.

However, customer concentration, inventory and capex execution, tariffs, currency swings and convertible debt complexity remain risks.

Story Continues

AEIS Shares Outperformed Sector, YTD

Advanced Energy shares have returned 14.5% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's rise of 14.1%.

However, the company's shares have also underperformed its peers, which include Lam Research LRCX, KLA Corporation KLAC and MKS Instruments MKSI. All three companies, Lam Research, KLA, and MKS Instruments, are expanding their footprint in the semiconductor equipment and technology sector. Shares of Lam Research, KLA and MKS Instruments have rallied 48.6%, 37.8% and 35.3%, respectively, in the year-to-date period.

AEIS Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Advanced Energy shares are currently overvalued, as suggested by its Value Score of F.

In terms of the forward 12-month Price/Earnings ratio, AEIS is trading at 20.25X, higher than the Computer & Technology sector's 18.67X.

AEIS Valuation

AEIS Rides On AI Power Demand and Semiconductor Strength

Advanced Energy's strong AI Infrastructure demand has been a major growth driver. Strong hyperscaler spending, expanding customer engagements, and rising power requirements in AI data centers are strengthening the company's long-term growth prospects. Advanced Energy expects its Data Center Computing revenues to grow at least 50% in 2026, supported by next-generation program ramps. Expanding relationships with second-wave data center customers are expected to accelerate growth in 2027 and beyond.

The transition toward 800-volt data center architectures presents another significant opportunity. Advanced Energy's modular AC-DC and DC-DC power solutions offer high power density, approximately 98% efficiency, and improved reliability. These products are expected to generate initial production revenues in late 2027, followed by a meaningful ramp in 2028, potentially increasing power content per rack.

In semiconductor, rising investments in advanced logic, DRAM and NAND manufacturing, alongside increasing etch and deposition intensity, are creating opportunities for market share gains. Strong customer acceptance of the eVerest and eVoS plasma power platforms, coupled with system power design wins, is expected to accelerate new product revenues in 2027 and beyond.

The manufacturing expansion in Malaysia and Thailand, favorable product mix and operational efficiencies should support profitable growth. Advanced Energy expects its expanded manufacturing network to eventually provide approximately $5 billion in revenue-generating capacity, while targeting gross margins exceeding 43% over the long term.

What Should Investors Do With AEIS Stock?

Advanced Energy's robust and diversified portfolio to meet the rising demand for AI-driven technologies, particularly in data center computing and semiconductor markets, is contributing to its growth prospects continuously, driving top-line growth. Expanding hyperscaler relationships, next-generation power solutions, and strong design-win momentum further strengthen its long-term prospects. These factors have justified its premium valuation.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold ALAB Stock Before Q3 Earnings Release?
news.Content:
Astera Labs ALAB is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 3.

For the third quarter of 2026, revenues are expected to be between $540 million and $560 million. The midpoint implies sequential growth of approximately 40%. Management projects non-GAAP earnings between $1.16 and $1.21 per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 revenues is currently pegged at $550.39 million, indicating an increase of 138.71% from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $1.19 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This implies 142.86% year-over-year growth.

Astera Labs, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Astera Labs, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Astera Labs, Inc. Quote

ALAB's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters, with an average earnings surprise of 17.07%.

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Factors to Note for ALAB's Q3 Earnings

Astera Labs is expected to have benefited from accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, growing demand for high-speed connectivity solutions and increasing adoption of its Scorpio AI Fabric Switches in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Expanding hyperscaler investments in AI training and inference infrastructure, coupled with increasing accelerator cluster sizes and bandwidth requirements, are likely to have supported demand for the company's intelligent connectivity portfolio.

The transition of Scorpio X-Series high-radix AI Fabric Switches into volume production is expected to have been a major growth catalyst in the to-be-reported quarter. Strong demand from a leading hyperscaler customer, particularly for its 320-lane switching solutions, is likely to have accelerated revenue growth. Scorpio is expected to become Astera Labs' largest product family by revenues in the third quarter, surpassing Aries. Growing adoption of Scorpio P-Series across AI networking, storage and scale-out applications is likely to have contributed to top-line expansion.

The Aries signal conditioning portfolio is expected to have benefited from accelerating adoption of PCIe 6 retimers and gearboxes across AI servers, GPUs and general-purpose computing platforms. Increasing AI accelerator cluster sizes, higher retimer attach rates, and improved average selling prices associated with PCIe 6 adoption are likely to have strengthened Aries revenues. Continued demand for PCIe 5 solutions across inference applications is also expected to have supported growth.

The Taurus portfolio is likely to have benefited from increasing demand for high-speed Ethernet connectivity across AI and general-purpose computing platforms. Strong adoption of 400G solutions, alongside initial preproduction shipments of 100-gigabit-per-lane Taurus Smart Cable Modules supporting 800G Ethernet connectivity, is expected to have boosted revenues. Expanding 800G deployments are likely to have supported improved attach rates and higher average selling prices.

However, Astera Labs' third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to have faced pressure from declining gross margins due to an evolving product mix and rising operating expenses associated with continued investments in product development.

Story Continues

ALAB Shares Outperform Sector, Industry

Astera Labs shares have risen 74.6% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 14.2% and the Zacks Internet Software industry's rise of 0.2%.

ALAB Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Astera Labs stock is not so cheap, as the Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation at this moment.

In terms of the forward 12-month Price/Sales, ALAB is trading at 17.79X, higher than the Zacks Internet Software industry's 3.98X.

ALAB Valuation

ALAB Faces Stiff Competition

Despite an expanding portfolio and strong partner base, ALAB is facing stiff competition from other industry players like Marvell Technology MRVL, Credo Technology CRDO and Cisco Systems CSCO. These companies are all expanding their footprints in the AI infrastructure space.

Marvell Technology has expanded its AI connectivity portfolio with the introduction of the Alaska E 3.2T protocol-aware retimer and second-generation Alaska A 1.6T active electrical cable DSP. Built on advanced 3nm technology, these solutions address growing bandwidth, latency and power-efficiency requirements in AI infrastructure. The Alaska E delivers 3.2 Tbps bandwidth across 16 lanes, supporting Ethernet, UALink and ESUN protocols. The Alaska A offers 1.6T throughput, more than six meters of copper reach and improved power efficiency. Both products are currently sampling to customers, strengthening Marvell Technology's position in next-generation AI scale-up networking.

Credo Technology's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In August 2026, the company announced that it is developing a new open interconnect standard within the Open Compute Project (OCP). It has established the OCP Open Chiplet Economy Lightweight Serial Interconnect (LSI) Workstream, aimed at developing efficient interconnect solutions for AI infrastructure. As part of the initiative, Credo Technology plans to contribute its OmniConnect lightweight AXI framer specification to OCP. The OCP LSI initiative is designed to support an open, interoperable ecosystem where compute, memory and other resources can be combined more efficiently. This could allow data-center operators and AI developers to tailor systems to specific workloads rather than relying on fixed architectures.

Cisco's AI infrastructure business continues to gain momentum. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the company secured $4 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders, bringing fiscal 2026 orders to $9.3 billion, approximately 4.5 times the previous year's level. The company's Silicon One architecture, particularly its P200 and G200-powered systems and Acacia optical solutions, is strengthening its competitive position. Cisco expects hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenues to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027 compared with approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026.

Conclusion

Astera Labs' expanding AI connectivity portfolio and accelerating Scorpio adoption are likely to drive strong third-quarter growth. However, stretched valuation, intensifying competition and margin pressures remain risks.

Astera Labs currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting that it may be wise to wait for a more favorable entry point to accumulate the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Why Micron Stock Dove Today
news.Content:
Shares of Micron (NASDAQ:MU) stumbled out of the gate Friday morning, falling as much as 5.9%. As of 11:28 a.m. ET, the stock was still down 4.7%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist lower was a competitor's bullish financial report, which wasn't enough to ease investor concerns about the future of artificial intelligence (AI).

Image source: The Motley Fool.

You want chips with that?

Rival memory chipmaker Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) released its financial results, which were by all accounts bullish. For its fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Oct. 2), the company delivered revenue that soared 378% year over year and 23% quarter over quarter to $11 billion. This fueled adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $49.51, which grew more than 40-fold.

For context, analysts' consensus estimates were for revenue of $10.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $46.67, so the company cleared both hurdles by a wide margin.

Unrelenting demand for the memory chips that underpin AI continued. Data center revenue was the highlight, surging 1,682% year over year to $4.8 billion, while edge computing revenue of $5.8 billion jumped 320%.

Sandisk even provided a robust second-quarter forecast that surpassed Wall Street's expectations, guiding for revenue of $12.4 billion and adjusted gross margin of 85%, both at the midpoint of its guidance.

On the heels of its stellar financial report, Sandisk stock plunged as much as 11% on Friday, dragging other memory chipmakers down with it.

So what does this have to do with Micron?

The reason for the stalling stock prices is complex. Sandisk and Micron stocks have gained 488% and 293%, respectively, over the past year, driven higher by surging demand for the memory chips used for AI. After runs of this magnitude, investors are increasingly concerned that the good times can't last -- particularly when it comes to AI.

Moreover, the Big Three memory chipmakers -- Sandisk, Micron, and SK Hynix -- tend to move together, and that phenomenon held true today.

Finally, Micron stock is selling for just 12 times earnings. For investors who believe that AI still has room to run, this represents an attractive buying opportunity.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Plunged Today
news.Content:
Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) were trading sharply lower on Friday, tumbling as much as 11%. As of 10:49 a.m. ET, the stock was still down 9.6%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist lower was the company's financial results. While they were better than expected, investors wanted more.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Chip shot

For its fiscal 2027 first quarter (ended Oct. 2), Sandisk generated revenue that surged 378% year over year and 23% quarter over quarter to $11 billion. This drove adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $49.51, up more than 40-fold.

Given the falling stock price, you'd be excused for thinking that Sandisk missed the mark, but nothing could be further from the truth. Analysts' consensus estimates were calling for revenue of $10.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $46.67, so the company sailed past expectations with room to spare.

The catalyst that drove the results was no secret. Soaring demand for the memory chips critical to artificial intelligence (AI) processing continued. Data center revenue of $4.8 billion soared 1,682% year over year, also surpassing expectations of $4 billion. At the same time, edge computing revenue of $5.8 billion jumped 320% year over year and 7% sequentially.

Sandisk raised its second-quarter outlook above Wall Street's expectations and is now calling for revenue of $12.4 billion and adjusted gross margin of 85%, both at the midpoint of its guidance.

Management also announced a long-rumored 8-for-1 stock split "to make the stock more accessible, including to employees." Shareholders of record as of market close on Nov. 9, 2026 will receive seven additional shares for each share owned, which will be issued after market close on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Post-split trading is expected to begin when the market opens on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026.

From all appearances, it was a stellar quarter, so why is the stock falling? Frankly, the magnitude of Sandisk's growth is the stuff of legend, but investors fear it simply can't last. Concerns about the continuing demand for all things AI, the resilience of consumer spending, and a ceiling on memory prices are all weighing on the stock -- despite the company's stellar performance.

If you believe -- like I do -- that we're still in the early innings of artificial intelligence adoption, Sandisk stock is a steal at 16 times earnings.
