news.Title: Okta Surges 158% YTD: Should Investors Hold the Stock Now?
news.Content:
Okta OKTA shares have jumped 157.5% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's return of 17.4%. The company is benefiting from growing demand for identity security, artificial intelligence (AI) agent governance, enterprise modernization and expanding adoption of its newer products. However, intense competition, uncertainty surrounding AI adoption, slowing customer growth and near-term revenue headwinds remain concerns. What should investors do with OKTA stock? Let's find out.

Okta Rides on Strong Enterprise Demand & New Products

Okta is well-positioned to benefit from increasing enterprise investments in identity security as organizations accelerate AI adoption and modernize their cybersecurity infrastructure. The proliferation of autonomous AI agents across applications, cloud platforms and enterprise systems is creating demand for identity discovery, authentication, access controls and governance. Okta for AI Agents enables enterprises to discover, secure and govern AI agents while enforcing access policies across heterogeneous environments. Growing adoption of agentic AI is expected to expand the company's addressable market and create additional cross-selling opportunities across its identity security portfolio.

Okta's newer offerings, including Okta Identity Governance, Okta Privileged Access, Identity Security Posture Management, Identity Threat Protection and Okta for AI Agents, are helping customers address increasingly complex security requirements. Deals involving newer products generated an average annual contract value (ACV) uplift of approximately 40%, highlighting significant cross-selling and upselling opportunities. Increasing adoption of these solutions is likely to strengthen Okta's competitive positioning, deepen customer relationships and support subscription revenue growth.

Okta is benefiting from solid demand among large enterprises, improving sales productivity and strong customer expansion activity. During the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the number of customers generating more than $1 million in ACV increased more than 20%, bringing the total to more than 600. Strong pipeline conversion and deal expansions contributed to record bookings for a quarter outside the fiscal fourth quarter. The company is strengthening collaborations with Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Cisco, OpenAI, Databricks and Snowflake to expand identity controls across AI applications and enterprise systems.

Intense Competition & Moderating Revenue Growth Hurts OKTA

Story Continues

OKTA is facing stiff competition from the likes of Microsoft MSFT, CrowdStrike CRWD and Cisco Systems CSCO. YTD, CrowdStrike, Cisco and Microsoft have returned 114.6%, 42.2% and 9.4%, respectively.

OKTA Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Per OKTA management estimates, Microsoft's workforce access management market share is at approximately 40% compared with Okta's 30%. Competition is also intensifying as cybersecurity vendors, enterprise software providers and AI infrastructure companies expand into identity governance and AI agent security.

Okta continues to face challenges in accelerating overall revenue growth despite improving bookings and subscription demand. For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, the company expects revenues of $813-$817 million, indicating approximately 10% year-over-year growth. Current Remaining Performance Obligation growth is projected at 11-12%, below the 14% growth recorded in the second quarter. Okta expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 10-11%, including an approximately one-percentage-point headwind from shifting more professional services business to global system integrator partners.

OKTA's Earnings Estimate Revision Reflects Steady Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Okta's fiscal 2027 earnings has remained steady at $3.93 per share over the past 30 days. The earnings estimate suggests 12.3% growth over the figure reported in fiscal 2026. The consensus estimate for revenues is currently pegged at $3.22 billion, suggesting 10.4% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2026.

Okta, Inc. Price and Consensus

Okta, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Okta, Inc. Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Okta's third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings has been steady at 93 cents per share over the past 30 days. The earnings estimate suggests 13.41% growth over the figure reported in the year-ago quarter. The consensus estimate for revenues is currently pegged at $815.5 million, suggesting 9.9% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Here's Why OKTA is a Hold

OKTA shares are trading at a premium, as suggested by the Value Score of F.

In terms of forward 12-month price/sales (P/S), Okta is trading at 11.23X, higher than the median of 5.08X, the broader sector's 5.60X, Cisco's 5.94X and Microsoft's 9.52X. However, OKTA is cheaper than CrowdStrike, shares of which are trading at 38.93X.

OKTA Stock's Valuation

Okta's near-term prospects are supported by resilient subscription demand, growing adoption of identity governance solutions, expanding enterprise relationships and early momentum in AI agent security. Its independent platform architecture, improving sales execution and robust cash generation provide additional strengths. Nevertheless, competitive pressure from Microsoft and other platform vendors, AI monetization uncertainty and moderating revenue growth remain significant concerns. The company's ability to translate its early AI security leadership into sustained subscription growth while maintaining profitability will be critical to its long-term performance.

Okta currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), which implies that investors should wait for a more favorable point before accumulating stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Arista Networks (ANET) vs. CSCO and AVGO: Is AI Data Center Expansion Creating a Long-Term Networking Winner?
news.Content:
Is ANET a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Arista Networks, Inc. on TradersPro's Substack. Since the thesis was published on August 29th, ANET shares have pulled back amid profit-taking and valuation concerns after a strong rally, creating a near-term pause while AI networking demand continues to support the longer-term growth case. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ANET. Arista Networks, Inc.'s share was trading at $186.72 as of October 28th 2026. ANET's trailing and forward P/E were 55.91 and 33.82 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a networking equipment company pitched as a great investment. ANET shares gained 42.50% year to date. Comparable technology stocks like Cisco Systems and NVIDIA gained 43.18% and 15.49%, respectively, during the same period. Why are AI infrastructure stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

In May, we published an article about the 10 Stocks That Will Make You Rich Over the Next Decade and ANET ranked #4 in that article. ANET returned 31.76% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ANET. This article highlights ANET among the 12 Best NYSE Stocks to Buy for Long-Term Investment. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Arista Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:ANET) makes the networking equipment that connects servers, data centers, and enterprise systems, using high-speed switches, routers, and its EOS software. Its biggest growth opportunity right now is AI infrastructure, where massive AI computing clusters need faster, more reliable connections between chips, making Arista Networks, Inc. a key supplier of the "plumbing" behind the AI boom.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

The company is also benefiting from steady spending by large cloud providers, growing demand for office and campus networking, expansion into routers, and a large existing customer base that keeps generating repeat business. Investors are watching closely because AI infrastructure still can't keep up with AI demand, and that gap is where Arista Networks, Inc. sees its opportunity ( see how Arista's $6.9 billion in deferred revenue relates to its cash flow ).

The bullish argument is simple: as AI systems get more powerful, they need more bandwidth and faster connections. This lets Arista Networks, Inc. grow along two paths at once — more AI clusters being built overall, and each cluster needing better networking gear than the last. Its core switching business is well placed for this, while its newer push into routers and campus networks adds growth beyond just AI data centers.

Story Continues

A key part of the long-term story is the shift toward liquid-cooled AI infrastructure, which changes how high-density data centers are built. As AI servers use more power and generate more heat, traditional cooling starts to fall short, forcing new approaches to layout, power delivery, and system design. If this shift continues, Arista Networks, Inc. could play a bigger role in connecting these next-generation systems, though it still has to prove it can turn this opportunity into consistent growth.

The main risk is a slowdown in AI spending or delays in data center buildouts by large customers. Networking demand depends heavily on this spending, and factors like component shortages, tariffs, power limits, and the sheer complexity of liquid-cooled builds could all slow things down. The market already expects a lot from Arista Networks, Inc., so continuing to win AI networking deals matters more than ever — any stumble in adoption of its newer platforms could weigh on the stock.

Another risk for the stock is that AI networking growth benefits competing technologies more than Arista's Ethernet platforms. Rising spending on AI clusters does not guarantee that customers will choose Arista's equipment. Its annual report identifies InfiniBand and NVLink as competing technologies, often sold alongside NVIDIA's graphics processors as integrated solutions. Customers choosing these packages could leave less networking business available to independent suppliers. Arista might then need to offer lower prices or spend more on development to win deployments. That would put pressure on margins even if overall AI infrastructure investment remains strong. In our opinion, the stock's premium becomes harder to justify if the networking market expands faster than Arista's ability to capture profitable orders.

Beyond AI, growth in campus networking, routing products, and support revenue from its installed base gives the company other ways to grow, so it isn't fully dependent on one market. Still, how fast AI-related demand keeps growing will be the biggest factor in whether the stock's current optimism is justified.

The stock's momentum has picked up recently, with trading volume rising and the stock moving into a stronger technical position — a sign of growing investor confidence. But the longer-term outlook still hinges on whether AI spending keeps converting into real networking orders, and whether growth holds up as expectations climb. A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending or delays from big customers could pressure the stock even if the broader industry keeps growing.

AI remains the main reason investors are bullish, but there's a risk that demand stays concentrated among just a handful of large cloud customers. If those customers keep expanding their AI clusters and adopting newer, denser computing setups, Arista Networks, Inc. should keep benefiting. The real test is whether this turns into lasting earnings growth rather than a short-term spending wave.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed but generally constructive signal. As per our database, 91 hedge fund portfolios held Arista Networks, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, up from 85 in the previous quarter. This increase suggests institutional interest in the stock strengthened, supporting its appeal as an AI infrastructure investment. By comparison, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) was held by 101 hedge funds, up from 97, NVIDIA was held by 285 hedge funds, up from 275, and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) was held by 170 hedge funds, down from 173. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) stood out with the strongest increase in hedge fund interest by number of funds, followed by Arista Networks and Cisco Systems, while Broadcom saw a modest pullback, suggesting institutional enthusiasm remained broadly positive across the group.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for Arista Networks, Inc. relative to its peers. About 1.17% of Arista Networks, Inc.'s float is sold short, almost identical to Broadcom Inc. at 1.14%, but below NVIDIA Corporation at 1.30% and Cisco Systems, Inc. at 1.53%. This suggests Arista Networks, Inc. is drawing similarly limited skepticism to Broadcom Inc., with bearish bets remaining low across all four AI infrastructure companies.

Valuation Analysis

ANET's forward P/E is 33.82x. Broadcom Inc., Cisco Systems, Inc., and NVIDIA Corporation trade at forward P/Es of 18.25x, 20.53x, and 13.79x, respectively. ANET's own forward P/E was 32.75x on December 31, 2025, making its current multiple approximately 3% higher. We believe the current valuation reflects strong investor expectations for AI networking demand, continued cloud spending, and expansion into campus networking and routing. However, the premium appears demanding despite Arista's strong profitability and earnings growth, as its multiple exceeds all three peers. Arista's revenue increased 37.7% to $3.04 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while net income rose approximately 36% to $1.21 billion, demonstrating that increased demand is translating into substantial earnings. We believe ANET can justify its current valuation without accelerating beyond this growth rate if strong earnings growth persists and margins remain resilient. If Arista maintains its Ethernet leadership and successfully converts AI investment into sustained earnings growth, its premium could remain justified, but we would wait for a lower entry price given the limited room for disappointment.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Arista Networks Inc (ANET) by Charly AI in April 2025, which highlighted the AI and cloud networking growth, strong margins, balance sheet strength, and long-term upside despite near-term pressures. ANET's stock price has appreciated by approximately 168.66% since our coverage. We believe ANET could offer an attractive entry point at a lower valuation if AI networking demand sustains earnings growth and Arista preserves its margins, despite its premium multiple and competition from integrated alternatives.

Arista Networks is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While ANET could offer long-term upside if it converts AI networking demand into sustained earnings growth, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential at more attractive valuations, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than ANET and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: KLAC Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise on AI Demand
news.Content:
KLA KLAC reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $1.22 per share, up 38.6% year over year. Earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.39%.

Revenues increased 28.9% year over year to $4.14 billion and surpassed the consensus mark by 2.20%. Results benefited from AI infrastructure investments, leading-edge foundry/logic demand and rising process control intensity. Wafer Inspection revenues surged 37% year over year, reflecting robust demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

KLAC Segment Revenues Show Broad-Based Growth

Semiconductor Process Control revenues reached $3.75 billion, accounting for 91% of total revenues. The segment grew 29% year over year and 15% sequentially, supported by increasing investments in advanced logic, memory and packaging technologies.

Specialty Semiconductor Process revenues rose 16% year over year to $140 million but declined 13% sequentially. PCB and Component Inspection revenues increased 28% year over year to $242 million and remained flat sequentially, benefiting from technology transitions and stringent performance requirements in high-performance computing.

KLA Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

KLA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | KLA Corporation Quote

KLA Product Mix Highlights Wafer Inspection Strength

Wafer Inspection remained the largest product category, generating $2.11 billion, or 51% of revenues. Sales increased 37% year over year and 19% sequentially, reflecting strong demand for inspection capabilities in increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing processes.

Patterning revenues grew 29% year over year and 18% sequentially to $862 million, representing 21% of the top line. Services revenues advanced 14% year over year and 4% sequentially to $850 million, contributing 20% of revenues. Growth reflected an expanding installed base, longer equipment lifecycles and customers' increasing focus on equipment productivity and availability.

KLAC End Markets Reflect Foundry and Logic Leadership

Foundry and logic represented 72% of Semiconductor Process Control systems revenues to semiconductor customers. Memory accounted for the remaining 28%, supported by growing demand for advanced DRAM and high-bandwidth memory technologies.

Geographically, China contributed 34% of total revenues, followed by Taiwan at 25% and North America at 15%. Korea accounted for 12%, while Europe, Japan and the Rest of Asia represented 5%, 4% and 5%, respectively.

The company highlighted strengthening process control requirements in advanced packaging. KLA expects advanced packaging process control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing more than 70% year-over-year growth.

Story Continues

KLA Margins Expand Despite Component Cost Pressures

Non-GAAP gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint of KLA's guidance.

Non-GAAP operating expenses totaled $688 million, including $395 million in research and development and $293 million in selling, general and administrative expenses. Management cited elevated memory component costs as a continuing margin headwind. Product cost reductions, improved memory efficiency and pricing initiatives are expected to help offset these pressures over time.

Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 240 basis points sequentially to a record 46.1%, reflecting revenue growth and operating leverage.

KLAC Cash Flow Supports Strong Shareholder Returns

KLAC ended the quarter with $4.74 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, compared with $5.72 billion in carrying-value debt.

Cash flow from operations reached $1.53 billion, while free cash flow totaled $1.34 billion, representing a 32% margin. Capital expenditures were approximately $195 million, including investments supporting future capacity expansion.

The company returned $1.24 billion to shareholders during the quarter, comprising $936 million in share repurchases and $305 million in dividends. Over the trailing 12 months, capital returns totaled $3.79 billion, while free cash flow reached $4.04 billion.

KLA Issues Strong Second-Quarter Fiscal 2027 Outlook

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, KLA expects revenues of $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million. Non-GAAP earnings are projected at $1.44 per share, plus or minus 11 cents, while non-GAAP gross margin is forecast at 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point.

Foundry/logic is expected to account for approximately 60% of Semiconductor Process Control systems revenues to semiconductor customers, with memory contributing 40%. Within memory, DRAM is projected to represent 84% and NAND the remaining 16%. Non-GAAP operating expenses are anticipated at approximately $710 million.

The company raised its calendar 2026 wafer equipment market outlook, including advanced packaging, to the mid-$150 billion range and expects the market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. KLA anticipates second-half calendar 2026 revenues to grow approximately 25% over the first half, supported by improving supply capacity, expanding backlog and sustained AI-related investments.

news.Title: DELL Expands AI Security Capabilities: Can It Challenge CSCO & HPE?
news.Content:
Dell Technologies DELL is benefiting from growing enterprise demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, cybersecurity and data protection solutions. The company recently expanded its cybersecurity and resilience portfolio to strengthen protection across AI environments, identity systems and enterprise infrastructure. These enhancements strengthen DELL's competitive position against Cisco Systems CSCO and Hewlett Packard HPE.

The company introduced Security Hardening for Dell AI Factory and Resilience Operations for AI services to enhance workload protection and recovery. Expanded PowerProtect AI Assistant capabilities simplify cyber resilience management, while new identity resilience solutions support recovery across Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID and Okta. Dell Technologies also enhanced PowerProtect and PowerScale integration for faster data recovery. The company also introduced quantum-safe encryption in PowerStore and Post-Quantum Readiness Assessment services to help enterprises address emerging cybersecurity threats.

Dell Technologies' growing AI infrastructure business has been a major growth driver. In second-quarter fiscal 2027, AI server revenues reached $16.4 billion, while the AI backlog surged to $95 billion. Strong enterprise adoption creates opportunities for the company to cross-sell security, storage and data protection solutions.

Dell Technologies' expanding cybersecurity capabilities, integrated infrastructure portfolio and robust AI demand strengthen its competitive position against Cisco Systems and Hewlett Packard. The company expects third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues of approximately $49 billion, including $19 billion in AI server revenues.

How Competitors Fare against DELL

Dell Technologies suffers from stiff competition from companies like Cisco Systems and Hewlett Packard. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the security space.

Cisco Systems is benefiting from its expanding security portfolio, growing adoption of AI-driven cybersecurity solutions and strengthening Splunk momentum. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Security revenues increased 14% year over year to $2.23 billion. The entire security portfolio, including Splunk, recorded double-digit order growth.

Hewlett Packard is expanding its security capabilities by integrating Juniper Networks with its Aruba-based networking portfolio, strengthening its position in AI-native networking and converged network security. The company has also introduced server innovations designed to accelerate secure 5G and AI deployments, enhance security and automate operations from the edge to the core.

news.Title: Cisco Gains From AI Networking Boom: Can It Outpace HPE & ANET?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO is benefiting from accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, hyperscaler demand and enterprise network modernization. The growing adoption of agentic AI is driving demand for high-bandwidth, low-latency networking solutions, strengthening Cisco's competitive position against Hewlett Packard HPE and Arista Networks ANET.

Cisco's AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers reached $9.3 billion in fiscal 2026, approximately 4.5 times the fiscal 2025 level. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027. Its Silicon One architecture, Acacia optical technologies and next-generation switching platforms are helping capture opportunities across scale-out and scale-across AI networking deployments.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, networking revenues increased 28% year over year, supported by triple-digit AI infrastructure growth. Networking orders surged 40%, while data-center networking orders increased more than 35%. Strong campus networking demand, Wi-Fi 7 adoption and enterprise infrastructure refreshes further strengthen its prospects.

The company's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. CSCO recently expanded its Cisco 360 Partner Program with new incentives, Ecosystem Deal Registration and AI-powered tools to strengthen partner profitability and customer engagement. The company announced the general availability of Cisco IQ for Partners, enabling resellers and managed service providers to leverage real-time intelligence, automate operations and identify modernization opportunities. Cisco also enhanced its Cloud Control platform with AgenticOps capabilities, including Model Foundry, ThousandEyes integration and Model Context Protocol servers. The company also introduced quantum-resilient Wi-Fi 7 access points and expanded Live Protect capabilities to strengthen enterprise security and support AI-ready infrastructure.

Cisco's expanding AI networking portfolio, strong hyperscaler traction and partner ecosystem position it favorably to capitalize on emerging opportunities and compete effectively with Hewlett Packard and Arista Networks. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Cisco expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion.

How Competitors Fare Against CSCO

Cisco is facing stiff competition from Arista Networks and Hewlett Packard in the AI networking domain.

Arista strengthens its position in AI networking as enterprises and hyperscale customers expand Ethernet-based AI infrastructure. During the second quarter of 2026, the company exceeded 100 cumulative AI fabric customers using Etherlink switches compared with only a handful of early adopters in 2024. Management also expects AI revenues to reach at least $3.6 billion in 2026, supported by scale-up, scale-out and scale-across deployments.

Hewlett Packard is benefiting from a broader shift toward AI infrastructure, networking modernization and hybrid cloud, with Juniper expanding its addressable market and integration synergies supporting earnings growth. The Juniper acquisition is broadening HPE's reach across campus and branch, data center switching, routing and security, while integration remains ahead of schedule.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Networking revenues were $2.9 billion, up 10% on a normalized basis, and operating margin was 22%. Networks for AI orders reached $700 million in the quarter and $2.2 billion cumulatively, prompting HPE to raise its fiscal 2026 year-end target to $2.5 billion-$3.0 billion. HPE now expects fiscal 2026 Networking revenue growth of 73% to 74%.
