news.Title: Microsoft Q1 Earnings Beat Estimates as Cloud Accelerates
news.Content:
Microsoft MSFT reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings of $4.89 per share on a non-GAAP basis (excluding OpenAI investment impacts), which increased 18% on a year-over-year basis (up 19% in constant currency). The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.82%. On a GAAP basis, earnings per share were $4.92, up 32% year over year.

Revenues of $92.3 billion increased 19% year over year (up 19% in constant currency) and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.88%. The top line came above management's guided range of $89.85-$90.95 billion, with results exceeding the company's expectations across revenues, operating income and earnings per share.

Microsoft Cloud revenues totaled $63.9 billion, up 30% year over year (31% in cc), accelerating from 27% growth in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Commercial remaining performance obligation reached $677 billion, up 73% year over year, with a weighted average duration of 2.3 years. Roughly 30% of this is expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 12 months, up 29% year over year, while the portion recognized beyond 12 months increased 98%. Commercial bookings declined 12% (down 11% in cc), reflecting large Azure commitments in the prior-year quarter, partly offset by a large Azure commitment signed this quarter.

Beginning fiscal 2027, Microsoft reports results under two segments, Agents and Infra and Devices and Consumer, replacing the earlier three-segment structure. The change was announced in September 2026, and prior-period figures have been recast to conform to the new structure.

Microsoft Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Microsoft Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Microsoft Corporation Quote

MSFT's Q1 Segment Performance

Agents and Infra

The Agents and Infra segment generated $76.8 billion in revenue, which grew 25% year over year (25% in cc).

Azure revenues surged 48% year over year (48% in cc) to $33.2 billion, accelerating from 42% growth in the prior quarter and ahead of the company's expectations, despite delays in some third-party capacity deliveries. Growth was driven by Foundry and improved CPU monetization. Foundry revenues more than tripled year over year, aided by efficiency gains across the GPU fleet that freed up additional capacity for customers, as well as higher revenue per token.

Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenues increased 17% on a reported basis (18% in cc), or 18% (19% in cc) when adjusted for a prior-year comparable that had benefited from one point of in-period revenue recognition. Results were ahead of expectations on stronger GitHub Copilot adoption and usage, partially offset by weaker sales execution in Microsoft 365 E3 and stand-alone SKUs. Paid Microsoft 365 commercial seats grew 5%. Average revenue per user growth was led by premium offerings, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, E5 and E7, the latter of which has already reached millions of paid seats.

Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenues rose 17% (16% in cc), as the business began lapping the benefit of the prior-year price increase. Total Microsoft 365 cloud revenues were $27.8 billion, up 17%.

Productivity and server licensing revenues declined 3% (down 2% in cc) to $8.4 billion. Industry solutions cloud revenues grew 10%, driven by Dynamics 365 and LinkedIn Talent Solutions, although booking trends continued to moderate. Frontier and support services revenues rose 4% (5% in cc) to $2.1 billion.

Operating income for the segment rose to $40.6 billion from $32.7 billion a year earlier, representing an increase of 24% (25% in cc). Operating margin decreased slightly to 53% as sales mix shifted toward Azure. Microsoft Cloud gross margin was 66%, down year over year.

Devices and Consumer

The Devices and Consumer segment generated $15.5 billion in revenues, down 3% year over year (down 3% in cc), pressured by a steep decline in Windows OEM and devices revenues, partly offset by growth in search and advertising.

Search and advertising revenues, excluding traffic acquisition costs, rose 12%, ahead of expectations on higher volume and rate across LinkedIn, Edge and Bing. Xbox content and services revenues fell 2% (down 1% in cc), as declines in third-party content and Xbox Game Pass were partially offset by growth in first-party content. Windows OEM and devices revenues declined 22%, with Windows OEM revenues down 27% (down 28% in cc) due to a prior-year comparable that benefited from Windows 10 end of support, inventory drawdowns by OEM and channel partners, and weaker PC market demand.

Operating income for the segment increased to $5.4 billion from $5.2 billion a year earlier, up 2% (3% in cc). Operating margin expanded to 35%, aided by lower amortization of intangible assets from the Activision acquisition.

Story Continues

MSFT's Notable Developments in Q1

Microsoft announced its biggest Copilot update to date, combining Chat, Cowork, Autopilot and Code into a single unified experience across commercial and consumer users. Copilot daily users increased nearly 50% sequentially and more than five-fold year over year, while the number of customers with more than 50,000 Copilot seats rose more than eight-fold. Customers consuming Copilot credits through usage-based billing grew more than 75% in the quarter. The company did not provide an updated paid Copilot seat count this quarter.

Foundry crossed 120,000 customers, and revenues from open-source models on Foundry increased 10-fold. Microsoft completed pre-training of MAI Base 2, its next first-party base model, and released DecisionOne, a structured decision-making model used by more than 4,000 customers in its first month. Paid Fabric customers reached 44,000, up more than 50% year over year, while more than 50 million agents are now registered in Agent 365, up over 30% sequentially.

On GitHub, agent-generated pull requests increased six-fold over the past six months, and GitHub Advanced Security revenues grew more than 50% year over year. At GitHub Universe, the company announced broad availability of Copilot Fusion, which brings multi-model orchestration to software development.

Microsoft added 24 new data centers across five continents during the quarter, cut dock-to-live times for new GB300 systems in its largest regions by about 20% sequentially and docked its first NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs. Its in-house Maia 200 chip is delivering up to 1.7 times more tokens per watt across Teams and Copilot workloads.

LinkedIn surpassed 1.4 billion members, with time spent viewing feed content up 15% year over year. In gaming, Minecraft delivered a record quarter for engagement and revenues. The company also announced an employee voluntary exit offer, the estimated cost of which is included in its second-quarter guidance.

MSFT's Financial Performance in Q1

Gross margin reached $62.6 billion, up 17% year over year, with gross margin percentage at 68%.

Total operating expenses increased to $16.6 billion from $15.7 billion, up 6%, driven by continued investments in research and development, compute capacity and talent. Research and development expenses were $9 billion, sales and marketing were $5.7 billion, and general and administrative expenses were $1.9 billion.

Operating income increased 21% year over year (22% in cc) to $45.9 billion, while operating margin expanded slightly to 50%. Net income reached $36.6 billion, up 32% on a GAAP basis. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding OpenAI-related impacts, net income was $36.4 billion, up 18% (19% in cc).

Other income and expense, net, was a positive $38 million in the quarter compared with a negative $3.7 billion a year earlier. Excluding the impact of OpenAI investments, other income and expense was a negative $234 million.

MSFT's Q1 Capital Expenditure and Infrastructure

Capital expenditures, including finance leases, were $45.2 billion, below expectations as some anticipated third-party capacity deliveries were delayed. Roughly three-quarters of spending went toward short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs, including higher memory and storage costs. Finance leases were $7.4 billion, while cash paid for property and equipment was $39.4 billion.

Cash flow from operations totaled $58 billion, up 29% year over year, driven by strong cloud billings and collections. Free cash flow was $18.6 billion, down from $25.7 billion a year ago, reflecting higher capital spending.

As of Sept. 30, 2026, Microsoft had total cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $64.5 billion compared with $76.8 billion as of June 30, 2026. Long-term debt was $31.1 billion, with an additional $4.4 billion in the current portion of long-term debt.

Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the fiscal first quarter.

MSFT's OpenAI Partnership Update

The fiscal first quarter reflected net gains from investments in OpenAI of $207 million, adding 3 cents to earnings per share. This compares with the first quarter of fiscal 2026, when net losses from OpenAI investments decreased net income and earnings per share by $3.1 billion and 41 cents, respectively.

These OpenAI-related impacts have historically created volatility in reported GAAP results, leading the company to provide non-GAAP measures excluding these effects to help investors better understand operational performance.

MSFT's Q2 2027 Outlook

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Microsoft expects total revenues between $96 billion and $97.1 billion, indicating growth of 18% to 19%. Based on current rates, foreign currency is not expected to have a meaningful impact on revenues, cost of revenues or operating expense growth.

The Agents and Infra segment is expected to generate revenues between $80.1 billion and $80.7 billion, indicating growth of 24% to 25%. Azure revenue growth is projected at 49% to 50% in cc, with demand continuing to exceed available supply and some third-party GPU capacity contracts delayed to the second half of the fiscal year. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenues are expected to grow approximately 19% in cc, while Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenues are expected to grow in the low teens. Microsoft Cloud gross margin is expected to be roughly 65%.

The Devices and Consumer segment is expected to generate revenues between $15.9 billion and $16.4 billion. Search and advertising revenue growth, excluding traffic acquisition costs, is expected in the low double digits, and Xbox content and services revenues are expected to grow in the mid-to-high single digits depending on the timing of first- and third-party content launches. Windows OEM and devices revenues are expected to decline in the mid-30s percentage range.

Cost of revenues is projected between $32.7 billion and $32.9 billion, up 26% to 27%, while operating expenses are expected between $18.5 billion and $18.6 billion, up 9%. Operating margin is expected to decline slightly year over year. Excluding any impact from OpenAI investments, other income and expense is expected to be roughly negative $300 million, and the effective tax rate is projected at approximately 20%.

Capital expenditures are expected to exceed $50 billion in the second quarter. Given the third-party capacity delays, Microsoft now expects calendar 2026 capital spending of approximately $170 billion, with spending expected to accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027. The company expects to remain free cash flow positive in fiscal 2027.

MSFT's Zacks Rank and Stocks to Consider

Currently, Microsoft carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Analog Devices ADI, Applied Materials AMAT and Cisco Systems CSCO, each carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Shares of Analog Devices have rallied 54.4% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $13.00 per share, up by a penny over the past seven days, indicating an increase of 66.9% year over year.

Shares of Applied Materials have jumped 54.5% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMAT's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.79 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating a rise of 35.8% year over year.

Cisco Systems shares have surged 45.3% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $5.11 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 18% year over year.

news.Title: UMC Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates Despite Higher Wafer Shipments
news.Content:
United Microelectronics Corporation UMC reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, wherein both earnings and revenues missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate. The company reported earnings of 21 cents per ADS, up from 20 cents in the year-ago quarter. The figure missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.7%.

Revenues increased 19.6% year over year to $2.32 billion but missed the consensus mark by 1.3%. Higher wafer shipments, improved factory utilization and strong demand for specialty technologies supported growth. Capacity utilization reached 92%, while wafer shipments hit a record high.

UMC's Wafer Shipments Hit Record High

Wafer shipments increased 7.3% sequentially to 1.212 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers, reflecting healthy demand across market segments. Quarterly manufacturing capacity increased to 1.325 million wafers from 1.305 million in the preceding quarter.

Capacity utilization improved to 92% from 85% in the second quarter and 78% in the year-ago period. Several 12-inch fabrication facilities operated at full capacity, while 8-inch operations witnessed a strong recovery. Blended average selling prices remained firm sequentially.

United Microelectronics Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

United Microelectronics Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | United Microelectronics Corporation Quote

United Microelectronics Sees Stable Revenue Mix

The communication segment contributed 39% of wafer revenues, while consumer applications accounted for 32%. Computer applications represented 13%, and other applications contributed the remaining 16%. The revenue distribution remained unchanged sequentially.

Asia Pacific accounted for 67% of wafer revenues, up from 66% in the preceding quarter. North America contributed 22%, while Europe represented 8% and Japan accounted for 3%. Fabless customers generated 86% of wafer revenues, with integrated device manufacturers contributing 14%.

UMC Benefits From Advanced Technology Demand

Revenues from 22/28-nanometer technologies represented 35% of wafer sales compared with 37% in the preceding quarter. However, the 22-nanometer business reached a record high, accounting for 18.3% of wafer revenues, supported by demand for display drivers, automotive radar and Wi-Fi integrated circuits.

Technologies at 40 nanometers and below contributed 51% of wafer revenues. The 40-nanometer node accounted for 16%, while 65-nanometer technologies represented 19%. Management highlighted continued customer engagement in silicon photonics and advanced packaging, supporting opportunities in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Story Continues

United Microelectronics' Operating Margins Expand

Gross profit increased 43% year over year and 12.9% sequentially. Gross margin expanded 420 basis points year over year and 150 basis points sequentially to 34%, benefiting from improved manufacturing utilization.

Operating expenses increased 4.3% year over year but declined 8% sequentially. Research and development expenses decreased 2.3% year over year. Operating income surged 67.7% year over year, while operating margin expanded 630 basis points to 25.1%.

UMC's Cash Position Strengthens

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalent balances were $4.48 billion, up from $3.92 billion as of June 30, 2026.

Cash flow from operating activities amounted to NT$30.02 billion during the quarter. Capital expenditures totaled NT$11.93 billion, resulting in free cash flow of NT$18.09 billion. The company's debt-to-equity ratio declined to 44% from 50% in the preceding quarter.

United Microelectronics Expects Steady Q4 Demand

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects wafer shipments to increase by a low-single-digit percentage sequentially. U.S. dollar average selling prices are projected to remain firm, while gross margin should be comparable to the third quarter. Capacity utilization is expected to remain in the low-90% range.

UMC maintained its 2026 cash-based capital expenditure budget at $2 billion. Separately, its board approved an additional capital expenditure budget of approximately $3.2 billion to accelerate expansion in Singapore and Tainan, supporting silicon photonics and advanced packaging.

Management expects positive demand momentum to continue into 2027, with blended average selling prices increasing approximately 10% year over year, supported by improved pricing and a richer product mix. AI-related revenues are expected to approach $300 million in 2026, with AI exposure potentially exceeding one-quarter of total revenues within three years.

news.Title: TYL Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on SaaS Growth and Margin Expansion
news.Content:
Tyler Technologies, Inc. TYL reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $3.52 per share, which increased 18.5% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.03%.

Tyler Technologies' revenues increased 8.7% year over year to $647.6 million but missed the consensus mark by 0.55%. The performance was supported by strong SaaS demand, transaction revenue growth and improved operating efficiency. Annualized recurring revenue (ARR) increased 11% to $2.28 billion, highlighting the strength of Tyler's recurring revenue model.

TYL's Recurring Revenue Base Strengthens in Q3

Recurring revenues increased 11% year over year to $568.8 million and accounted for 87.8% of total revenues. Excluding the impact of the Texas payments contract, recurring revenues grew 12.8%, reflecting healthy underlying demand.

Subscription revenues rose 15.3% to $462.6 million, supported by continued cloud adoption and transaction growth. Maintenance revenues declined 4.6% to $106.2 million as on-premises customers continued migrating to SaaS offerings.

Tyler Technologies, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Tyler Technologies, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tyler Technologies, Inc. Quote

Tyler's SaaS Momentum Drives Subscription Growth

SaaS revenues jumped 21.2% year over year to $242.2 million, reflecting sustained demand for cloud-based government solutions. Transaction revenues increased 9.5% to $220.4 million despite the discontinuation of revenues under the Texas payments contract in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Excluding the Texas contract impact, transaction revenues grew 14.2%, subscription revenues increased 17.8%, and total revenues rose 10.2%. These adjusted growth rates highlight the strength of Tyler's underlying business.

Management also highlighted progress in cloud modernization. Wasco County, OR, became the first Enterprise ERP customer to go live on Tyler's multi-tenant Cloud Living platform, with broader rollouts targeted for 2027.

TYL's Bookings Growth Signals Healthy Public Sector Demand

Total bookings increased 7.3% year over year to $646 million. Total SaaS bookings grew 14% to approximately $262 million in total contract value, supported by new contracts, customer expansions, renewals and cloud migrations.

New SaaS deals contributed approximately $22 million in annual contract value, while on-premises migrations added $18.6 million. Total SaaS ARR added 32.1% to approximately $40.6 million.

Management highlighted healthy government budgets, robust request-for-proposal activity and strong sales demonstrations. New SaaS annual contract value bookings increased 75%, underscoring customer demand for digital modernization.

Story Continues

Tyler's AI Adoption Expands Across Government Agencies

Tyler continued advancing its government-focused artificial intelligence strategy, closing approximately 300 deals containing AI solutions year to date, including roughly 130 during the third quarter.

The company made 11 AI agents and assistants generally available and expects to expand AI functionality to 25 agents by year-end. Its Resident AI Assistant now supports deployments across 11 states.

Notable wins included Nebraska's statewide Resident AI Assistant deployment and multiple contracts for AI-powered Priority Based Budgeting. These developments reflect growing opportunities to commercialize AI across Tyler's existing government customer base.

TYL Expands Profitability on Favorable Revenue Mix

Non-GAAP operating income increased 14.8% year over year to $182.1 million, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded 150 basis points to 28.1%. The improvement reflected a favorable shift toward higher-margin SaaS and transaction revenues, cloud efficiencies and disciplined expense management.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 13.4% to $192.7 million. GAAP operating income rose 19.5% to $117 million, while GAAP operating margin improved to 18.1% from 16.4% a year earlier.

Research and development expenses increased to $63.3 million from $51.8 million, reflecting continued investment in product development and innovation.

Tyler Generates Record Quarterly Free Cash Flow

Cash flows from operations increased 10.7% year over year to $282.5 million. Free cash flow rose 11.9% to a quarterly record of $277 million, supported by earnings growth and improved working capital performance.

Free cash flow margin expanded to 42.8% from 41.5% in the prior-year quarter, demonstrating improved cash generation.

Tyler ended the quarter with approximately $905 million in cash and investments and $1.4 billion in debt.

The company repurchased approximately 1.1 million shares for $379 million during the quarter. Year-to-date repurchases represented approximately 8.5% of outstanding shares, with roughly $1.37 billion remaining under its authorization.

TYL Provides Updated 2026 Earnings and Revenue Outlook

For full-year 2026, Tyler expects revenues between $2.535 billion and $2.565 billion. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 revenues is pegged at $2.55 billion, within management's projected range.

Non-GAAP earnings per share are projected between $12.95 and $13.20. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $13.10 per share, also within the company's guidance range.

Tyler expects a free cash flow margin of 26-28%, research and development expenses of $245-$250 million and capital expenditures of $20-$22 million.

The outlook incorporates continued investment in cloud and AI initiatives, alongside strategic acquisitions, including CODY Systems, acquired in July for approximately $27.7 million to strengthen Tyler's public safety software portfolio.

news.Title: Silicon Motion (SIMO) Is Considered a Good Investment by Brokers: Is That True?
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Silicon Motion (SIMO) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Silicon Motion currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.25, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 12 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.25 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 12 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 10 are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 83.3% and 8.3% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for SIMO

While the ABR calls for buying Silicon Motion, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns.

Another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a company's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements.

Is SIMO a Good Investment?

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for Silicon Motion, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has remained unchanged over the past month at $11.16.

Analysts' steady views regarding the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by an unchanged consensus estimate, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: What STMicroelectronics (STM) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Strong third-quarter performance: STMicroelectronics reported $3.76 billion in revenue, above the midpoint of its outlook, with non-U.S. GAAP EPS of $0.37. Industrial revenue rose 40% year over year, while communication equipment and computer peripherals surged 64%, driven by AI data centers and low-earth-orbit satellites.

AI and satellite demand are accelerating: ST expects about $1.3 billion in AI data-center revenue in 2026 and projects data-center revenue to more than double in 2027. Satellite communications revenue is also expected to reach or exceed 2026's record level, with capacity potentially limiting growth.

Positive outlook and margin plans: The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint and expects approximately $14.5 billion in full-year 2026 revenue. Manufacturing restructuring is expected to deliver more than 400 basis points of structural gross-margin improvement by late 2027 or early 2028.

Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue above the midpoint of its outlook, citing strengthening demand across industrial markets and continued growth in artificial intelligence data centers and low-earth-orbit satellite communications.

Revenue totaled $3.76 billion, with gross margin of 37.3% and non-U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.37. Chief Executive Officer Jean-Marc Chery said revenue outperformance was driven principally by communication equipment and computer peripherals, including AI data-center and satellite-related products, as well as communications and personal electronics.

→ Apple's Foldable iPhone Sold Out in Minutes, But Wall Street Has Questions

Industrial Chips Are in Rally Mode—5 Ways to Play

The company generated $351 million in free cash flow during the quarter. Inventory increased modestly to support expected fourth-quarter revenue growth, while distributor inventory declined and remained below STMicroelectronics' standard target, management said.

Demand, bookings and end-market performance

Chery said the recovery in the company's served markets continued to gain momentum in the third quarter. Sequential bookings increased and the overall book-to-bill ratio remained "well above two," with ratios above one across all end markets. Communication equipment and computer peripherals, as well as industrial, each had book-to-bill ratios well above three, according to management.

Story Continues

→ Coca-Cola Stock Is Everything AI Isn't—And That's Its Biggest Strength

STMicronelectronics Sends Industrial Chips Into Overdrive

The company's backlog stood at more than $20 billion at the end of the quarter, representing roughly five quarters of revenue at the midpoint of its fourth-quarter guidance. Chery said this level of backlog provided "appropriate visibility" for operations, although it remained below the peaks seen in 2022 and 2023.

Automotive: Revenue was flat sequentially and rose 5% year over year. ST cited demand for application-specific ICs and sensors used in core automotive systems, electric powertrains and advanced driver-assistance systems.

Industrial: Revenue increased 12% sequentially and 40% from a year earlier, supported by general-purpose microcontrollers, analog products and power-conversion devices.

Personal electronics: Revenue rose 12% sequentially but declined 4% year over year. Management said the stronger-than-expected third quarter did not reflect a customer pull-in.

Communication equipment and computer peripherals: Revenue climbed 14% sequentially and 64% year over year, primarily reflecting AI data-center and low-earth-orbit satellite communications demand.

By reportable segment, year-over-year revenue rose 8.8% in Analog Products, MEMS and Sensors; 11.3% in Power and Discrete Products; 24.1% in Embedded Processing; and 46.2% in RF & Optical Communications.

AI data-center and satellite growth drivers

→ Off-Price, High-Yield: Why Ross Stores Is Defying the Retail Slump

Management said AI data-center products remain a major company-specific growth driver. STMicroelectronics expects approximately $1.3 billion in AI data-center revenue during 2026, with more than 85% coming from RF-related products, including microcontrollers, silicon photonics and electronic ICs based on BiCMOS technology.

Chery said the company expects data-center revenue to more than double in 2027, with further growth anticipated in 2028. Rémy El-Ouazzane, president of the company's Microcontrollers, Digital ICs and RF Products Group, said microcontroller revenue in data centers is expected to double year over year in 2027. He added that silicon photonics is expected to become a meaningful portion of revenue next year, while BiCMOS contributions should become more visible in 2028.

El-Ouazzane said ST plans to increase silicon-photonics capacity by more than four times year over year, describing customer electro-optical yields as strong. In low-earth-orbit satellite communications, he said 2027 revenue should be at least as high as, and potentially higher than, the record level expected in 2026. The business could be constrained by capacity rather than demand, he said.

Margins and manufacturing restructuring

Third-quarter gross profit was $1.40 billion, up 32.2% year over year. Gross margin improved 410 basis points from a year earlier and 250 basis points sequentially, aided by lower unused-capacity charges and a better product mix.

However, third-quarter gross margin included roughly 60 basis points of unused-capacity charges and 40 basis points of nonrecurring costs tied to the company's manufacturing reshaping program. CFO Lorenzo Grandi said the company remains committed to an intermediate gross-margin model of 44% to 46% after completing the manufacturing transition.

The company expects more than 400 basis points of structural gross-margin improvement from reshaping its manufacturing footprint. Grandi said the benefit is expected to emerge toward the end of 2027 or in early 2028, subject in part to customer qualification timing as ST closes four legacy fabs and transfers production to newer facilities.

ST reported third-quarter operating income of $367 million, including $55 million in impairment, restructuring and related phase-out costs, plus $7 million in purchase-price-allocation effects from the acquisition of NXP's MEMS sensor business. Non-U.S. GAAP operating income was $429 million, representing an 11.4% margin.

Fourth-quarter and full-year outlook

For the fourth quarter, STMicroelectronics forecast revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint, plus or minus 350 basis points. That would represent sequential growth of 10.5% and year-over-year growth of 24.7%. The company expects gross margin of about 39%, plus or minus 200 basis points, including approximately 40 basis points of unused-capacity charges.

The outlook excludes potential effects from further changes in global trade tariffs. At the midpoint of its fourth-quarter outlook, ST expects full-year 2026 revenue of about $14.5 billion, up 22.8% year over year, with gross margin of roughly 36.4% and non-U.S. GAAP gross margin of approximately 36.6%.

Management also said it was comfortable delivering at least current consensus estimates for first-quarter 2027 revenue and gross margin, despite the quarter having 86 calendar days. The company expects 2027 operating expenses to rise, though Grandi said the increase should be accompanied by an improved expense-to-sales ratio as savings programs and lower startup costs partly offset investment in new opportunities and wage inflation.

Separately, Chery said the supervisory board requested that he be reappointed for an additional year as chairman of the managing board, president and CEO, subject to shareholder approval at the 2027 annual meeting. ST also announced organizational changes effective Jan. 1, 2027, including the appointment of El-Ouazzane as chief technology officer and Marco Cassis as chief strategic officer.

About STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM)

STMicroelectronics N.V. (NYSE: STM) is a global semiconductor company that designs, develops, manufactures and markets a broad range of integrated circuits and other semiconductor products. Its offerings support applications in automotive, industrial, personal electronics, communications equipment and computer systems.

The company's product portfolio includes microcontrollers, analog and power semiconductors, sensors, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), connectivity products and automotive chips.

news.Title: Lam Research Corporation (LRCX) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Lam Research (LRCX) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this semiconductor equipment maker have returned -22.7%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.9% change. During this period, the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, which Lam Research falls in, has lost 6.9%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Lam Research is expected to post earnings of $2.34 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +84.3%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +4%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $9.59 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +65.1%. This estimate has changed +2.8% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $11.88 indicates a change of +23.9% from what Lam Research is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +4.8%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Lam Research.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

In the case of Lam Research, the consensus sales estimate of $8.61 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +61.1%. The $34.78 billion and $41.38 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +49.7% and +19%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Lam Research reported revenues of $8.22 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +54.4%. EPS of $2.2 for the same period compares with $1.26 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $8.14 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +0.99%. The EPS surprise was +1.38%.

The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Lam Research is graded D on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Lam Research. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: STMicroelectronics forecasts higher Q4 revenue on AI chip demand
news.Content:
Investing.com-- STMicroelectronics (EPA:STMPA) forecast higher fourth-quarter revenue on Thursday after reporting a stronger-than-expected recovery in third-quarter sales and margins, supported by improving demand and growth in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The Franco-Italian chipmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $3.76 billion, up 17.9% from a year earlier and above its guidance midpoint of $3.70 billion.

Operating income excluding restructuring and other special items rose 98% to $429 million.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Gross margin increased to 37.3% from 33.2% a year earlier, helped by lower unused-capacity charges and a better product mix.

STMicro forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion at the midpoint, representing sequential growth of 10.5% and a 24.7% increase from a year earlier. It expects gross margin of 39.0%.

The company projected full-year 2026 revenue of about $14.5 billion, up 22.8% from 2025, citing a cyclical recovery across its end markets and growth opportunities in AI data centres and low-Earth-orbit satellite communications.

Chief Executive Jean-Marc Chery said stronger bookings and improving demand visibility supported the recovery, while distribution inventories remained below the company's standard target.

STMicro said it would continue expanding capacity while restructuring its manufacturing footprint and reducing its global cost base to improve profitability.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Cisco’s Report
news.Content:
Headquartered in San Jose, California, Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO) has built a global business around networking, cybersecurity and communications, keeping businesses connected in an increasingly digital world.

With a market cap of nearly $431.8 billion, the company offers network infrastructure, cloud and wireless technologies, data center solutions, collaboration tools, security software, technical support, and managed services, giving it a broad foothold across the technology landscape.

Dear Chevron Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 30

Jensen Huang Goes to Bat for Neoclouds, Citing Funding Gap. What This Means for Hard-Hit CoreWeave Stock.

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

The extensive reach sets the stage for Cisco's upcoming Q1 FY2027 earnings report, with Wall Street expecting diluted EPS of $1.15, a 42% increase from the year-ago quarter. Cisco has also beaten EPS estimates in each of the past four quarters, setting a strong precedent ahead of its latest results.

The earnings outlook beyond the current quarter looks equally encouraging, with analysts projecting diluted EPS of $4.42 for full-year FY2027, representing year-over-year (YOY) growth of 21.4%. Analysts also expect the bottom line to reach $8.6 for FY2027, marking a 4.8% increase from the previous year.

The market has already taken notice, sending CSCO stock up 51.9% over the past 52 weeks, far ahead of the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), which gained 12.4%. Cisco has carried that momentum into 2026, with shares advancing 43.2% year-to-date (YTD), compared with a 13.1% rise for the broader benchmark.

Cisco's performance looks even more impressive against the technology sector, where the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) has gained 26.5% over the past 52 weeks and advanced 32.7% YTD. Although those returns reflect a strong run for technology stocks, Cisco has comfortably outpaced the sector.

At the heart of that transformation lies Cisco's push into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, which has breathed new life into its established networking business. The company reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $17.3 billion, up 17.6% YOY, while hyperscaler AI orders reached $4 billion. These orders lifted FY2026 orders to $9.3 billion, roughly 4.5 times the previous year's total.

Story Continues

Cisco's momentum also extends beyond hyperscalers, broadening its market reach. Networking orders climbed 40%, Silicon One chips secured new design wins, and enterprise and sovereign customers continued upgrading their infrastructure. Looking ahead, management expects hyperscaler AI revenue to reach $7.5 billion in FY2027, nearly double this year's roughly $4 billion.

Wall Street's ratings reflect this improving outlook, with the 27 analysts covering Cisco arriving at an overall "Moderate Buy" rating. 16 analysts recommend a "Strong Buy," one assigns a "Moderate Buy," and 10 rate the stock "Hold."

Price targets provide another measure of Wall Street's expectations, with the average target of $133.08 indicating potential upside of 20.7%. Meanwhile, the Street-High target of $165 points to a possible gain of 49.6% from current levels.

news.Title: KLA (KLAC) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Wed, Oct. 28, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Vice President of Investor Relations and Market Analytics - Kevin Kessel

Chief Executive Officer - Rick Wallace

Chief Financial Officer - Bren D. Higgins

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Thank you for your continued patience. Your meeting will begin shortly. If you need assistance at any time, please press 0 and a member of our team will be happy to help you. Good afternoon. My name is Stephanie, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to the KLA Corporation September Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call and Webcast. All participant lines have been placed in a listen only mode to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question and answer session. Thank you. I will now turn the call over to Kevin Kessel, Vice President of Investor Relations and Market Analytics. Please go ahead.

Kevin Kessel: Welcome to the September 26 quarterly earnings call. Joining me are our CEO, Rick Wallace; and our CFO, Bren D. Higgins. We will discuss today's results as well as our outlook. Which we released after the market closed it is available on our website. Along with supplemental materials. We are presenting today's discussion and metrics on a non GAAP financial basis unless otherwise specified. All full year references we make always refer to calendar years. The earnings material contains a detailed reconciliation of GAAP to non GAAP results. Our comments today are subject to risks and uncertainties. Uncertainties reflected in the disclosure of the risk factors in our SEC filings.

Any forward looking statements, including those we make on the call today, are also subject to those risks. And KLA cannot guarantee those forward looking statements will come through. Our actual results may differ significantly from those projected in our forward looking statements. For any subsequent updates, please refer to KLA's IR website which also contains investor events, presentations, corporate governance information and links to our SEC filings. We will begin the call with Rick providing commentary on the quarter and our overall business environment. Followed by Bren, with financial highlights and our outlook. I will pass the call now to Rick. Rick?

Richard Wallace: Thanks, Kevin. KLA's September quarter beat the midpoint of our guidance ranges, across all key metrics. Revenue was another record at $4.14 billion This, coupled with our December quarter revenue guidance of approximately $4.7 billion demonstrates the growth acceleration we plan for the second half of 26. KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments, and increasing process control intensity across leading edge devices and advanced packaging. Other highlights for the quarter include KLA delivering operating margins above 46% for the first time ever.

Story Continues

Gross margin was 62.7%, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion Over the course of calendar 2026, the AI demand environment has continued to strengthen as reflected in our performance. Additionally, our strong customer engagement has provided visibility into a more favorable outlook for wafer equipment investment for calendar 2026 and 2027. We see this reflected in our growing backlog and sales funnel forecast. We expect momentum across our business to continue into the December quarter, and we are positioned to deliver significant growth in calendar 2027. We have been proactively working with our strategic supply chain partners over the past year to increase their capacity in order to keep up with our demand.

Advanced packaging remains increasingly critical to AI infrastructure expansion. And advanced packaging roadmaps continue to incorporate more wafer front end process, which drive additional process control requirements, KLA's leading process control portfolio enables the company to address these requirements across a growing range of applications. For calendar 2026, Advanced Packaging Process Control Systems revenue remains on track to hit $1.1 billion or more than 70% year over year growth. Nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market. The growing complexity of KLA's installed base and lengthening tool life cycles continues to increase demand for services.

KLA services revenue was $850 million in the quarter, up 14% year over year supported by a growing installed base and continued customer focus on tool performance, productivity, and availability in this tight system utilization environment. Finally, KLA's process, PCB, and component inspection businesses are also benefiting from technology transitions and the rigorous performance requirements of high performance computing. In summary, KLA is experiencing strengthening momentum driven by growth across the semiconductor ecosystem. Pace of our backlog growth is a key signal of accelerating momentum and provides confidence in our visibility into calendar 2027. Our September quarter results demonstrate the strength KLA's market position and operating model execution. Semiconductors continue to play an increasingly important role across global industries.

With growth driven by investment in AI infrastructure and expanded demand across a broader range of applications and end markets. Together, these trends are supporting stronger, more durable, and more diversified long term growth for the industry. Additionally, the growing complexity of AI enabled semiconductors is increasing process control intensity throughout the manufacturing flow. Reinforcing KLA's long term growth opportunity. KLA's differentiated portfolio is uniquely positioned to address these requirements. While sustained AI data center investment and broader adoption of advanced packaging architectures continue to expand the company's addressable market. As we look ahead, we remain focused on supporting customer roadmaps, investing in innovation and scaling our global capabilities to meet expected demand growth through calendar 2027.

As we progress toward our 2030 target model, we remain committed to disciplined execution, technology leadership, and our proven capital allocation strategy, which will allow us to create durable shareholder value. With that, I will turn the call over to Bren to discuss the quarter's financial highlights.

Bren D. Higgins: Thank you, Rick. KLA delivered strong sequential and year over year growth in the September quarter. For the first time in our company history, KLA delivered operating margins of over 46%. These results reflect our market leadership and disciplined execution. Supported by our global team's dedication and focus on customer success. Revenue of $4.14 billion was above the midpoint of guidance and rose 13% sequentially and 29% year over year. Non GAAP diluted EPS was $1.22 and GAAP diluted EPS was $1.18 each above the midpoint of the respective guidance ranges. Gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint of the guidance range. Operating expenses were $688 million including $395 million in R&D, and $293 million in SG&A.

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to 46.1%. Net income was 1.6 billion GAAP net income was 1.55 billion Cash flow from operations was 1.53 billion and free cash flow was $1.34 billion The company had 1.31 billion diluted weighted average shares outstanding. For the quarter, a breakdown of revenue by reportable segments and markets, major products, and regions, can be found within the shareholder letter and slides. Moving to the balance sheet. KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in total cash equivalents and marketable securities, and $5.95 billion of debt. The company maintains a flexible and attractive bond maturity profile supported by investment grade ratings from all 3 major rating agencies.

The industry outlook continues to strengthen, with visibility improving as customers increase long term investment plans. Despite these fast pace limitations, customers have been very resourceful and are accelerating delivery expectations across all segments. We are therefore raising our expectation for the wafer equipment market including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range in calendar 2026. KLA backlog continues to grow, and our sales funnel visibility is unprecedented. Supported by new fab investments by a broad base of customers. We continue to plan for significant growth in calendar 2027.

While we will have more to say about market and customer segment expectations for next year in our earnings call in late January, We currently expect the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. Customer engagement remains robust with numerous new fab projects and greenfield facilities. Scheduled to come online in the quarters ahead. The primary area of focus for our customers is on delivery urgency aligned with new project plans. Against this backdrop, KLA's business momentum and critical role in leading edge process control positions us to deliver accelerating growth for the remainder of calendar 2026 and continuing into 2027.

Our expectations of revenue growth acceleration in the second half of 26 are playing out as more capacity comes online in our long lead time supply chain areas. This is resulting in growth in the second half of calendar year 26 over the first half of approximately 25%. And positions the company for continued sequential growth into calendar 2027. KLA's December quarter guidance is for revenue of $4.7 billion plus or minus $200 million Foundry/logic revenue for semiconductor customers is forecasted to be approximately 60% and memory is expected to be about 40% of semiconductor process control systems revenue to semiconductor customers. Within memory, DRAM is expected to account for approximately 84% with NAND representing the remaining 16%.

As a reminder, these business mix approximations pertain solely to our semiconductor customers and do not fully reflect our total semiconductor process control systems revenue. Gross margin for the December quarter is forecasted to be 62.5% plus or minus 1 percentage point. While the company is demonstrating expected operating leverage across the business as it grows, This is being offset by persistently high memory costs for our system image processing requirements as we have discussed in prior quarters. We are actively engaged across the portfolio to optimize memory efficiency in our systems. Along with other product cost reduction initiatives. These efforts coupled with driving our usual returns based value sharing with our customers, should offset this headwind over time.

Operating expenses are forecasted to be approximately $710 million in the December quarter. We will continue to prioritize next generation product development scaling our business execution and company infrastructure investments to support expected revenue growth over the next several years. And we anticipate these expenses to grow sequentially through 2027 but at a much slower pace than revenue growth and consistent with our business model for operating margin leverage. As a reminder, our business model is designed to deliver 40% to 50% incremental operating margin leverage on revenue growth over the long run. Other model assumptions include other income and net of approximately $25 million expense for December quarter and we expect it to remain at approximately this quarterly level.

Planning tax rate is 14.5%. Our tax rate will vary quarter to quarter due to the geographic distribution of profit and various discrete items. In the December quarter, non GAAP diluted EPS is expected to be $1.44 plus or minus $0.11 and GAAP diluted EPS is expected to be $1.41 plus or minus $0.11 EPS guidance is based on a fully diluted share count of approximately 1.31 billion shares. In conclusion, process control and KLA in particular remain critical to the AI ecosystem build out and benefits from numerous ongoing relevance inflections including increases in leading edge designs across foundry and logic, device size and value, rising complexity and performance requirements, and the growing importance of advanced packaging.

KLA is experiencing strengthening momentum and a broader set of growth drivers across the semiconductor ecosystem. The rate and pace of our backlog growth is a key signal of our accelerating momentum and increased confidence in our visibility leading into calendar 2027. Our September quarter results demonstrate the strength of KLA's market position and operating model execution and support continued confidence in our performance moving forward. These recent results also illustrate the strength of KLA's market leading portfolio, disciplined operating model execution, and continued confidence in improving our performance moving forward. Looking ahead, remain focused on supporting customer roadmaps investing in innovation, and scaling our global capabilities to meet expected demand growth throughout calendar 2027 and beyond.

As we progress towards our 2030 target model, remain committed to disciplined execution, technology leadership our proven capital allocation strategy and creating durable shareholder value. That concludes my prepared remarks. Kevin, please begin the Q and A.

Kevin Kessel: Thank you. At this time, can you please give the instructions? Can you just give the instructions and we will get started?

Operator: Thank you, Kevin. We will now take our first question from Jim Schneider with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

James Schneider: Good afternoon. Thanks for taking my question. Good to see the accelerated growth in the back half Relative to calendar 2027 in your view of $100 billion in WFE, obviously, you have some good things going for you with advanced packaging growth and so on. So can you maybe kind of articulate how you are thinking about the way calendar 2027 shapes up and your level of confidence that you will be able ability to outgrow that 30% rough market number for 2027?

Bren D. Higgins: Jim, thanks for the question. When we look at 2027 and we been saying this for quite some time, as we think the construct for 2027 sets up pretty favorably for us. First, feel very good about our supply situation, right? We have been working at it for the last 12 months. We indicated we see an acceleration in the second half, certain components that have very long lead times. And so getting that to come online was a bit of a challenge in the first half, and we are seeing that play through. And that certainly informs our confidence in the December quarter, but also our views into 2027.

The setup for 2027 around the leading edge, both in terms of the breadth of investment the leading edge, new node investment, we think that sets up very well for the company. Greenfield investment in DRAM, the HBM dynamics and how that is affecting process control intensity, We are also seeing an uplift in process control intensity and conventional memory. Advanced packaging has been a nice growth driver. I do not see any reason why, as we look at next year that part of our business would not continue to grow faster than the market. So we feel overall that the setup is very leading edge centric.

Packaging is augmenting the growth and we think we are well positioned and our supply should be there to be able to enable us to meet the demand. Their demand is strong. I would say that we are I am still behind in supply, but I still I think that the trajectory is good, and we feel pretty confident about the guidance we have given.

James Schneider:

Operator: We will take our next question from Yes.

James Schneider: Sorry. And sorry, just 1 quick follow-up. As you think about the way the shape of 2027 starts to materialize, anything to call out in terms of back half of 2026 was certainly much stronger than the first half. Do you think it is going to be more ratable through 2027? Or you see again maybe being a little more back half loaded?

Bren D. Higgins: Right now, would say, for the next several quarters, given the backlog growth and the visibility in the funnel that we will see sequential growth for the next several quarters. Sort of implies second half stronger. I think it is more linear. I do not think it will have the same, as of now, the same significant uptick in half to half growth that looks a little more linear to us, but we would expect sequential growth moving forward.

Operator: Thank you. We will take our next question from Harlan Sur with JPMorgan.

Harlan Sur: Good afternoon. Thanks for taking my question. On the gross margin front, I know the team had some cost headwinds this year. Memory pricing headwinds, maybe GPUs, CPU pricing headwinds as well? Moving into next year, I know the team has benefit of new platforms, which carry higher pricing. Obviously, you are going to be driving higher volumes. Maybe you have got other value pricing initiatives taking place. Can we expect the team to drive back into that sort of 63%-plus range on a strong WFE outlook in 2027?

Positive Points

KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) reported record revenue of $4.14 billion, up 29% year-over-year, and guided December quarter revenue to approximately $4.7 billion, demonstrating accelerating growth.

Operating margin exceeded 46% for the first time in company history, reflecting strong operating leverage and disciplined execution.

Advanced packaging process control revenue is on track to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, growing over 70% year-over-year, nearly twice the market growth rate.

Services revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $850 million, driven by a growing installed base and increasing demand for tool performance and productivity.

KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC ) expects to outgrow the wafer equipment market in calendar 2027, with a strong backlog and sales funnel visibility, and anticipates the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in 2027.

Negative Points

Gross margin was 62.7%, slightly above the midpoint, but persistently high memory costs for system image processing continue to pressure margins.

Supply chain constraints, particularly for long lead time optical components, have limited KLA Corp ( NASDAQ:KLAC )'s ability to fully meet demand, with lead times averaging around 12 months and extending for some products.

China revenue as a percentage of total is expected to decline to the low 20th percentile in 2027, growing at a slower rate than the overall business.

Operating expenses are forecasted to grow sequentially through 2027, which could impact operating margin leverage if revenue growth slows.

The company faces potential delays in customer fab readiness, which could affect equipment delivery schedules and revenue recognition.

Q & A Highlights

Q : With WFE expected to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027, how confident are you that KLA can outgrow the roughly 30% market growth, and how does 2027 shape up? A : CEO Rick Wallace said the 2027 setup is "very leading-edge-centric," with breadth of leading-edge node investment, greenfield DRAM, HVM dynamics lifting process control intensity, and advanced packaging growing faster than the market. He noted supply is much improved after 12 months of work, though he is "still behind in supply," with the trajectory nonetheless supporting guidance.

Q : Will 2027 be more linear or back-half loaded, given the strong second-half 2026 ramp? A : CEO Rick Wallace said backlog growth and funnel visibility imply sequential growth for the next several quarters, which suggests a stronger second half, but he expects 2027 to be "more linear" than 2026, without the same significant half-to-half uptick.

Q : Given memory and other cost headwinds, can gross margin return to the 63%+ range in 2027? A : CEO Rick Wallace said the 63%64% target range remains the goal, but advanced packaging and non-semi PC growth are a mix headwind, offset by scale and value-based pricing on new capabilities. He expects improvement as the company moves through 2027, particularly in the middle-to-back half and into 2028, consistent with the March Investor Day model.

Q : When could process control gross margin, which was above 65% in June 2025, return to the mid-60s as DRAM contracts roll off? A : CFO Bren Higgins said on a consistent mix he can see it trending back there in the second half of 2027, since it is difficult to raise prices on existing backlog but new product deals should help. CEO Rick Wallace added that engineering work to use less memory in systems will lower memory content over time, though it takes time to implement.

Q : What are you seeing on lead times, and how are you preparing hiring and the supply chain for a multi-year growth cycle? A : CFO Bren Higgins said lead times average around 12 months, with some products such as Gen4 and Gen5 extending further. KLA is adding headcount in manufacturing, service, applications and engineering, and investing in every factory and with key suppliers, particularly in long lead-time optics, to support a multi-year investment cycle.

Q : Will KLA gain WFE share in 2027 given 12-plus month lead times and low-to-mid-30s market growth? A : CFO Bren Higgins said 2026's first-half weakness was a supply issue rather than demand, and the company remains short on supply today. He feels good about maintaining and growing KLA's relevant share, noting the inflecting parts of the market uniquely benefit process control. CEO Rick Wallace added, "We think we can outgrow next year."

Q : DRAM systems revenue is stepping up sharply in December is this driven by new fabs or rising inspection intensity? A : CEO Rick Wallace said intensity is definitely rising as customers appreciate the incremental value of yield on advanced devices with higher performance requirements. CFO Bren Higgins added that greenfield fabs are driving retooling, yield is "equivalent to printing money," and HBM, I/O counts and logic base die requirements are pushing DRAM intensity in some products toward leading-edge logic levels. Memory is expected to be about 60% of the business in 2027.

Q : How high can WFE grow, and is $300 billion a plausible peak? A : CFO Bren Higgins said the Investor Day view of $220 billion plus or minus $20 billion for 2030 now "looks like a very conservative one," and KLA is more optimistic about higher industry investment levels. The company is having deep conversations with key suppliers about 2029 and 2030 needs to support higher-end scenarios.

Q : Why shouldn't the 2030 model revenue be achievable in 2027 given current WFE levels? A : CFO Bren Higgins said the model assumed service growth tied to installed base expansion, non-semi PC growth, and a few points of semi process control share gain lifting overall share from about 7.5% of wafer equipment in 2025 toward 9%. Those assumptions are not yet met, but he sees no reason the financial model would not perform as laid out as growth comes from the same customers for the same products.

Q : Is the 40%50% incremental operating margin range structurally higher given current performance? A : CFO Bren Higgins said it depends on growth rates: in a normalized environment KLA performs near the midpoint, but with roughly 25% revenue growth it is slightly above the top end, and he expects to be beyond that in 2030. At company growth rates closer to 20%, he would expect performance at the top end of the model or better.

Q : What drove the record CapEx this quarter, and how should we think about CapEx and services growth going forward? A : CFO Bren Higgins said a significant land purchase in India for a new campus drove the quarter. He expects CapEx of roughly 2%3% of revenue, trending to $600$800 million per year as KLA invests at every site. On services, he sees no reason it would not operate at the high end of the long-term growth range in 2027 given installed base growth and high utilization.

news.Title: 聯電法說變法會「股價打跌停」 智原連拉2漲停
news.Content:
聯電（2303）28日公布第3季財報，營收創單季歷史次高、晶圓出貨量刷新紀錄，還預告2027年平均售價有望成長約10％，並追加32億美元，要布局先進封裝與矽光子。怎料「法說變法會」29日股價開低走低，股價一度打跌停。另一方面，集團旗下智原（3035）股價延續強勢，連拉2根漲停。

第3季營收742億元

聯電第3季合併營收達742.4億元，季增8％、年增25.6％，創單季歷史次高；毛利率34％，營業利益186.4億元，季增24.7％，歸屬母公司淨利164.3億元，每股純益（EPS）1.32元。第3季晶圓出貨量季增7.3％，突破120萬片12吋約當晶圓，創下歷史新高，產能利用率也從第2季的85％提升至92％，部分12吋晶圓廠產能已滿載，8吋晶圓廠營運亦明顯復甦。

展望第4季，聯電預估晶圓出貨量季增1％至3％，美元計價平均售價維持穩健，毛利率約34％，產能利用率則可望維持在91％至93％。執行長王石指出，高階智慧手機、工業應用需求強勁，車用市場也持續復甦，但電腦市場需求相對疲軟。隨著AI基礎建設持續發展，電源管理晶片（PMIC）、現場可程式化邏輯陣列（FPGA）及連接應用需求可望成長。

明年ASP喊漲1成

聯電看好2027年晶圓代工定價環境改善，預期平均售價將較2026年成長約10％，並從明年第1季開始呈現正向成長。然而，財務長劉啟東坦言，晶圓報價調升不代表毛利率就能同步大幅改善，因為原物料成本也在增加，加上未來數年折舊費用將持續上升，預期2027年折舊費用至少呈低個位數成長，2028年增幅可能進一步擴大。

聯電指出，未來至少3年，折舊與原物料成本都將對毛利率形成壓力，即使平均售價上漲，毛利率仍不容易回到過去景氣高峰水準。這也成為市場評估聯電後續獲利的重要變數，投資人關注漲價效益能否抵銷成本增加，以及產能受限後，營收與獲利還能有多少成長空間。

聯電重挫、智原連2根漲停

儘管營運展望不乏亮點，聯電股價仍遭賣壓襲擊。29日盤中最低殺到跌停價115.5元。相較之下，集團旗下智原受惠明年AI營收可望大幅成長，以及成功接獲美系雲端AI應用之大型專案，採用2奈米GAA製程，股價延續強勢，已連續第2個交易日攻上漲停，來到231.5元。

news.Content:
Key Points

KLA reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion , up 13% sequentially and 29% year over year, with a company-record 46.1% operating margin and earnings above guidance.

3 AI Winners, 3 Very Different Paths to Higher Margins

KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion, exceeding the midpoint of its guidance range as demand for process-control equipment remained strong across leading-edge foundry, logic, memory and advanced-packaging applications tied to artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

President and Chief Executive Officer Rick Wallace said revenue rose on continued investment in AI-related semiconductor capacity and growing process-control requirements for advanced devices and packaging. The company also projected December-quarter revenue of approximately $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, signaling an acceleration in growth during the second half of calendar 2026.

"KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading-edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments and increasing process control intensity across leading-edge devices and advanced packaging," Wallace said.

September-quarter results

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to a company-record 46.1%.

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash equivalents and marketable securities and $5.95 billion in debt.

Services revenue reached $850 million, up 14% from a year earlier. Wallace said the increase reflected a larger installed base, more complex systems and customer focus on tool performance, productivity and availability amid high system utilization.

Advanced packaging and AI demand

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

The company said advanced packaging is becoming more important to AI infrastructure expansion as packaging roadmaps incorporate more sophisticated wafer-front-end processes. KLA expects revenue from advanced-packaging process-control systems to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year.

Wallace said that growth rate would be nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced-packaging market. In response to analyst questions, Chief Financial Officer Bren Higgins said KLA expects its packaging business to continue growing faster than the market in 2027, with demand increasingly moving toward higher-sensitivity inspection systems as hybrid bonding and other advanced packaging processes expand.

KLA also expects strong memory-related demand. For the December quarter, foundry and logic are forecast to account for about 60% of Semiconductor Process Control Systems revenue from semiconductor customers, while memory is expected to account for approximately 40%. Within memory, DRAM is expected to represent about 84% and NAND about 16%.

Wallace said process-control intensity is rising in DRAM as customers seek higher yields and meet more stringent performance expectations, particularly for advanced memory products. Higgins added that some DRAM products now have process-control intensity comparable with leading-edge logic, aided by greenfield fab investment and demand for high-bandwidth memory.

Industry outlook and capacity investments

KLA raised its estimate for the calendar 2026 wafer-equipment market, including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range. Higgins said customers are increasing long-term investment plans despite fab-space limitations and that KLA's sales funnel visibility is "unprecedented," supported by new fab investments from a broad customer base.

For calendar 2027, the company expects the wafer-equipment market to exceed $200 billion. Higgins said KLA anticipates sequential revenue growth over the next several quarters, with a more linear progression than the sharp second-half increase anticipated in 2026.

The company said it has been working with supply-chain partners for the past year to expand capacity, particularly for long-lead-time components such as optics. Higgins said average lead times are about 12 months, with some Gen4 and Gen5 product lines taking longer.

KLA is investing in manufacturing, service, engineering and applications staffing, as well as factory capacity. Higgins said capital expenditures should trend higher over the next several years, estimating annual spending of roughly $600 million to $800 million. He noted that a significant land purchase in India for a new campus was a major contributor to the quarter's capital spending.

Management said supply availability had constrained shipments during the first half of 2026, but incremental capacity is now coming online. Wallace also noted that customers can face their own constraints, including delays in clean-room construction, materials and power availability.

Margins, China and December outlook

KLA forecast December-quarter gross margin of 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point, and operating expenses of approximately $710 million. Higgins said persistently elevated memory costs for system image-processing requirements remain a margin headwind, though the company is working to reduce memory usage in its systems, lower product costs and capture value-based pricing on new capabilities.

For the December quarter, KLA expects non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.44, plus or minus $0.11, and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.41, plus or minus $0.11. The company's forecast assumes approximately 1.306 billion fully diluted shares, other expense of about $25 million and a planning tax rate of 14.5%.

On China, Higgins said the country's revenue contribution is expected to decline as a percentage of total sales despite modest growth in absolute terms. He expects China to represent roughly 27% to 29% of revenue in the fourth quarter and to fall to the low-20% range in calendar 2027, as wafer-equipment spending outside China grows more rapidly.

About KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC)

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ: KLAC) develops process control, inspection and yield management solutions for the semiconductor and other advanced manufacturing industries. Its technologies help manufacturers identify defects, measure critical dimensions and monitor production processes to improve quality, reliability and manufacturing efficiency.

The company's product portfolio includes wafer and reticle inspection systems, metrology and measurement tools, defect review and classification systems, and software for analyzing manufacturing data.

The next quarter looks less punchy: management's $5.80 billion$6.30 billion revenue forecast puts the midpoint at $6.05 billion, essentially level with the third quarter. That leaves investors watching whether the recovery can keep building after a strong jump.
