news.Title: Why Arm’s Q2 Earnings Could Spur a Recovery in Its Stock
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (ARM) will release its fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings on Nov. 4. While profit booking following a significant rally has led to a correction in its stock price, its solid Q2 performance and strong Arm AGI CPU demand could spur a recovery.

Arm continues to see strong customer demand across its business, which indicates solid growth ahead. Moreover, it has signed multiple high-value agreements that will support long-term growth.

More News from Barchart

Micron Just Unveiled a New Bonus Plan. What That Means for MU Stock.

PLTR Stock Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Palantir's Q3 Report

'U.S Has the Best Healthcare in the World. It's Not Even Close' Says Mark Cuban — But the Problem Is Most Americans Can't Afford It

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Arm's Q2 Outlook

Arm entered fiscal 2027 on a strong footing, led by solid momentum across its business. Strong demand for ARM-based computing architectures across cloud infrastructure, consumer electronics, automotive systems, and emerging AI applications positions it well to deliver solid growth in Q2 and beyond.

Arm reported first-quarter revenue of $1.29 billion, up 22% year-over-year (YoY). The top line benefited from solid performance in the royalty business. Its royalty revenue increased 22% YoY to $715 million, with cloud AI and data center infrastructure emerging as the primary growth engines. Data center royalty revenue more than doubled from the previous year, supported by the expanding adoption of ARM-based server processors among major hyperscalers.

In addition, the growing deployment of data processing units (DPUs) and SmartNICs is providing another growth source, as Arm technology is incorporated into a broad range of leading data center networking products.

In the consumer segment, Edge AI royalties continued to expand despite weakness in the smartphone market. Higher royalty rates, driven by growing adoption of Armv9 architectures and compute subsystems, helped offset softer smartphone sales and the pressure from elevated memory prices. Physical AI also contributed positively, with continued adoption of ARM-based technologies in advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous applications supporting demand across the automotive ecosystem.

Licensing revenue is another key growth driver. License and other revenue reached $574 million, up 23% YoY, reflecting strong customer demand for next-generation architectures and deeper strategic relationships with major technology companies. Arm also secured multiple high-value agreements as existing customers renewed long-term licenses. These arrangements, involving hyperscalers, automotive and robotics companies, and handset manufacturers, strengthen Arm's competitive position.

Story Continues

Demand for Arm's AGI CPU offering is also gaining traction, with reported demand exceeding $2 billion. The addition of customers across the U.S. and China, alongside an expanding overall pipeline, points to strong growth ahead.

Looking ahead, management expects the growth trajectory to remain strong in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Arm forecasts revenue of $1.38 billion, representing approximately 22% YoY growth. Licensing and other revenue are projected to rise about 30%, while royalty revenue is expected to grow at a low-teens rate.

The earnings outlook is also solid, with management projecting adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.47 for Q2, up 21% YoY.

Why ARM Stock Appears Compelling Ahead of Q2

Arm's upcoming Q2 earnings could be a key catalyst for a stock-price recovery, supported by strong customer demand, expanding data center adoption, and growing traction for its AGI CPU offering.

Arm is expected to deliver solid revenue and earnings growth, driven by strength in royalty revenue. Higher licensing revenue and long-term agreements with major technology companies also highlight its solid growth prospects. Moreover, rising adoption of ARM-based architectures across AI infrastructure, automotive systems, and consumer electronics provides multiple avenues for sustained growth.

Although ARM stock still trades at a high valuation, the 49% decline from its 52-week high has eased some of these concerns ahead of the earnings announcement.

Analysts currently have a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating on ARM stock and a mean price target of $292.72.

news.Title: AEIS Rides on Strong Data Center Demand: Can It Outpace KLA & MKS?
news.Content:
Advanced Energy AEIS is benefiting from robust demand for precision power solutions, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and hyperscale data centers. The company's expanding relationships with hyperscale customers, growing design-win pipeline and next-generation power technologies are strengthening its competitive position against KLA KLAC and MKS MKSI in the rapidly evolving data center market.

In the second quarter of 2026, Data Center Computing revenues increased 35.2% year over year to $191.5 million, driven by strong hyperscale demand. Advanced Energy expects data center revenues to increase more than 50% in 2026. Accelerating hyperscale investments and the ramp-up of next-generation programs are expected to sustain this momentum.

Advanced Energy's investments in 800-volt power architectures represent another significant growth opportunity. Its modular AC-DC and DC-DC solutions offer approximately 98% efficiency, high power density and reliability. Initial production revenues are expected in late 2027, followed by a more meaningful ramp in 2028. This transition could expand Advanced Energy's power content per rack and create additional long-term revenue opportunities.

The company's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. AEIS recently introduced three new M-CRPS power supplies offering 3200W and 3600W output capacities for AI data centers, networking and telecommunications applications. The OCP-compliant solutions deliver power densities exceeding 100 W per cubic inch, supporting increasingly demanding AI infrastructure requirements. Featuring advanced cybersecurity capabilities, high efficiency and improved thermal performance, the new products are designed to support next-generation CPU and GPU workloads while simplifying system integration and accelerating deployment.

AEIS's expanding portfolio and strong growth across the data center computing market are expected to boost top-line growth and position it favorably against KLA and MKS. For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million.

AEIS Faces Stiff Competition

The company is facing stiff competition from companies like KLA and MKS. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the data center space.

KLAC is benefiting from robust data center demand, driven by accelerating AI infrastructure investments and growing adoption of high-performance computing. Increasing demand for advanced logic chips, high-bandwidth memory and sophisticated semiconductor packaging is driving higher process control intensity, strengthening KLA's growth prospects.

MKS is benefiting from rising AI-related investment across semiconductor and advanced packaging markets, with demand broadening through memory, logic, advanced PCBs, photonics, and chemistry equipment. Strong demand for datacom testing solutions and expanding manufacturing capacity further strengthens MKSI's long-term growth prospects. In second-quarter 2026, photonics and optics gained momentum in lithography, metrology and inspection, while datacom benefited from communications testing for AI data centers.

Story Continues

AEIS Share Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Advanced Energy shares have gained 11.2% in the year-to-date period compared with the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's increase of 14.9% and the Zacks Semiconductor Equipment - Wafer Fabrication industry's growth of 47.2%.

news.Title: Vicor Stock is Overvalued at 16.52X EV/Sales: Should You Still Buy it?
news.Content:
Vicor VICR shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F. In terms of the trailing 12-month EV/Sales, VICR is trading at 16.52X, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 8.19X. The company is trading at a higher multiple compared with peers, including Analog Devices ' ADI 15.17X and Texas Instruments ' TXN 13.82X, but cheaper than Monolithic Power Systems ' MPWR 17.76X.

Vicor's Shares Trade at a Premium

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Is Vicor worth buying at current prices? Let us dig deep to find out.

VICR Shares Ride on AI Prospects

Year to date (YTD), Vicor shares have outperformed the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, as well as Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments. Vicor returned a whopping 93.4% YTD while the broader sector, Monolithic Power Systems, Analog Devices and Texas Instruments have returned 14.9%, 33.7%, 54.3% and 78%, respectively.

Vicor Stock's Price Performance

Vicor is benefiting from increasing demand for high-density power delivery solutions as AI processors require greater power efficiency and higher current density. The company's second-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technology is emerging as a key growth catalyst. VICR claims that its proprietary all-FPA technology can reduce AI processor power losses by 10-15%, while delivering more than 40 times the current gain of integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and three times the current density of conventional voltage regulators. These advantages are expected to strengthen Vicor's competitive position as next-generation AI processors become increasingly power-intensive.

The company's expanding royalty business has been a key catalyst. In the third quarter of 2026, royalty revenues surged to $66.6 million from $21.7 million in the year-ago quarter. Vicor secured its first VPD license with a leading AI original equipment manufacturer and received licensing inquiries from two hyperscalers. The company expects royalty revenues of at least $43 million in the fourth quarter, even without additional licensing agreements. Further adoption of its patented technologies could create a growing, high-margin revenue stream, although quarterly royalty collections may remain uneven.

Manufacturing expansion represents another important long-term catalyst for the company. Vicor has acquired two additional sites for ChiP Fab-2 and ChiP Fab-3, potentially increasing total manufacturing capacity to nearly five times that of Fab-1. Initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 is expected in the second quarter of 2027. This expansion should help address production bottlenecks, support rising customer demand and unlock additional revenue opportunities.

Story Continues

VICR Benefits From Strong ATE Business & Balance Sheet

Vicor's growth opportunities also extend beyond AI processors. Strong demand for automatic test equipment (ATE) used in ASIC and memory testing is supporting the company's business, with leading ATE customers generating more than $100 million in annual revenues. VICR is also witnessing opportunities in industrial, aerospace and defense markets, particularly from emerging companies developing autonomous technologies. These diversified growth drivers should reduce dependence on any single application and support sustained demand for the company's power solutions.

Vicor's strong balance sheet further supports its long-term expansion plans. The company ended September 2026 with $513.1 million in cash and cash equivalents. VICR expects to finance Fab-2 and eventually Fab-3 without raising additional capital. Improving operating cash generation and increased production scale should strengthen the company' ability to fund innovation, expand manufacturing and capitalize on emerging growth opportunities.

Vicor's 2026 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.94 per share, up 8% over the past 30 days, suggesting 51% growth from the 2025 reported figure.

Vicor Corporation Price and Consensus

Vicor Corporation price-consensus-chart | Vicor Corporation Quote

The consensus mark for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $1.13 per share, down by four cents over the past 30 days and indicating 12% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Despite its premium valuation and impressive YTD rally, Vicor remains an attractive investment proposition, supported by strong AI-driven demand, expanding royalty revenues and growing adoption of second-generation VPD technology. The company's manufacturing expansion, solid backlog and strong balance sheet further strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Although elevated valuation and near-term capacity constraints remain concerns, VICR's technological leadership and expanding growth opportunities justify its premium and make the stock worth considering for long-term investors.

Vicor currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Lumentum Shares Jump 135% YTD: Can AI Momentum Sustain the Rally?
news.Content:
Lumentum LITE shares have surged 135% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 16.5%. The outperformance reflects investor optimism about the company's expanding role in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, accelerating demand for optical connectivity and improving profitability. Strong hyperscaler spending, growing adoption of 1.6T optical transceivers, optical circuit switches (OCS) and next-generation laser technologies are strengthening Lumentum's growth prospects.

These factors have helped LITE shares outperform peers, including Cisco Systems CSCO, Broadcom AVGO, and Coherent COHR YTD. Shares of Coherent and Cisco have returned 27.8% and 45.3%, respectively, while Broadcom shares have dropped 1.1%. Despite robust demand, LITE faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Apart from stiff competition, LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. So, what should investors do with the LITE stock? Let's find out.

LITE Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Lumentum Shares Are Overvalued

Lumentum shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F.

In terms of the trailing 12-month price/sales, LITE is trading at 10.48X, higher than the broader sector's 5.57X. Lumentum is trading at a higher multiple compared with peers, including Coherent's 3.9X, Cisco's 6X and Broadcom's 9.39X.

LITE's Valuation

LITE Faces Multiple Challenges

Lumentum faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Tight availability of laser components and other materials could restrict shipments and delay revenue realization. The company is expanding ultra-high-power laser production across its San Jose, U.K. and Greensboro facilities.

The company suffers from customer concentration. LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. Lumentum's two largest end customers accounted for 26.6% and 15% of fiscal 2026 revenues, respectively, representing a combined 41.6%. Moreover, the company's expanding OCS business currently depends heavily on one major customer.

Lumentum faces competition from established optical technology suppliers, including Coherent, Broadcom, InnoLight and Eoptolink. Additionally, the shift toward silicon photonics presents challenges for Lumentum's EML business.

Story Continues

Can Strong AI Opportunity Aid LITE's Prospects?

Lumentum is benefiting from increasing investments in AI data centers, which require high-bandwidth, low-latency optical connectivity. The transition from copper-based connections to optical technologies is creating opportunities across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up networking architectures. Increasing adoption of AI accelerators and larger computing clusters is driving demand for Lumentum's lasers, optical components and transceivers.

The company is benefiting from accelerating adoption of next-generation 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers as hyperscalers upgrade their AI networking infrastructure. Lumentum achieved record 800G shipments and initiated production shipments of 1.6T transceivers during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Lumentum expects the adoption of 1.6T transceivers to accelerate through calendar 2027, supported by deployments of custom AI clusters among leading hyperscale customers.

Lumentum's OCS business represents a significant growth opportunity as hyperscalers seek energy-efficient networking solutions. OCS technology enables dynamic traffic routing while reducing power consumption and optical signal losses compared with conventional electrical switching. OCS shipments doubled sequentially in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while the company's first-quarter outlook included its first quarter of more than $100 million in OCS revenues.

LITE's 2027 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Rising Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $21.40 per share, up 0.5% over the past 30 days, suggesting 146.8% growth from the fiscal 2026 reported figure.

Lumentum Holdings Inc. Price and Consensus

Lumentum Holdings Inc. price-consensus-chart | Lumentum Holdings Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $4.22 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days and indicating 283.64% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Conclusion

Lumentum's strong exposure to AI infrastructure, accelerating adoption of 1.6T optical transceivers and expanding OCS opportunities bode well for its long-term growth prospects. Upward earnings estimate revisions further reinforce optimism. However, the stock's premium valuation, customer concentration, intense competition and manufacturing capacity constraints warrant caution. Following the sharp YTD rally, much of the growth potential appears priced in, limiting near-term upside. Hence, investors may consider holding LITE shares at current levels rather than chasing the rally, while monitoring execution and profitability improvements.

Lumentum currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Top 5 AI Stocks in Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont’s Portfolios
news.Content:
Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont are two of the brightest minds in investing, and both have strong views on AI. Laffont runs Coatue Management and has built his hedge fund around the technology. Dalio founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975 and warns that AI has become a crowded trade. Let's start with Laffont.

Laffont: AI Is a Supercycle, and the Next $10 Trillion Company Could Come From It

Laffont sees a supercycle in AI, and Coatue's four biggest US long positions as of March 31 were all AI-related, Bloomberg reported. Coatue's flagship hedge fund lost 8.3% in July, its worst month in more than a year, but was still up 14.3% for the year (at the time of the Bloomberg report), after a gain in May that was its best month in 25 years, Bloomberg said in August. Check his top stock picks here.

Laffont expects a $10 trillion company within 10 to 15 years, he told CNBC in June. He thinks the winner could be a new AI name. There is "a good chance that OpenAI and Anthropic could be there," he said, and SpaceX could join them.

Agentic AI excites him most. Laffont described going to bed while a thousand AI agents do the work, and he says the productivity gains already show up in his own office. He does not expect AI models to become free, because people will pay for the best ones.

Dalio: AI Is a Great Tool and a Crowded Trade

Dalio built Bridgewater out of a two-bedroom apartment, and its flagship Pure Alpha fund rose 33% in 2025, Reuters reported. Click to read more about Dalio's portfolio.

A US debt crisis could hit within three years, he told Bloomberg Television in October. The government spends about 40% more than it takes in, he says, and debt payments squeeze out other spending. Stocks look expensive by most of his measures, and the extra return they offer over bonds has shrunk. AI adds to the risk, because a small group of AI stocks drives the market, and the big AI spenders now rely more on debt to fund their buildout. His one warning to investors is to avoid being "too concentrated in one particular asset," such as AI.

Dalio still likes AI as a tool. Using it to systematize investment decisions is the future, he says, and he expects gains to broaden from the AI builders to the companies that use the technology.

Both billionaires own AI stocks. Here are the 5 biggest AI holdings the two funds have in common. You can see the full list of 10 stocks here .

Methodology

We looked at the top 50 holdings in the second quarter 2026 13F filings of Ray Dalio's Bridgewater Associates and Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management. From the AI stocks that appear in both lists, we picked the 10 with the highest combined dollar value across the two stakes and ranked them in ascending order. Stake sizes and share changes come from the funds' 13F filings for the quarter ended June 30.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 599.2% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 372 percentage points ( see more details here ).

You can also watch our video about the top 10 AI picks of these two famous billionaires on YouTube by clicking the image below:

#5 GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE:GEV)

Coatue Stake $3.01 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $144.2 Million

GE Vernova makes the gas turbines and grid equipment that data centers need for power. Coatue trimmed 14,194 shares in the second quarter and held $3.01 billion, or 6.18% of its portfolio. Bridgewater trimmed 312,129 shares and held $144.2 million, or 0.59% of its portfolio. Bulls say the company's order backlog for AI data center power outweighs a recent earnings miss. See the full breakdown here.

GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) is positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by AI data centers. US data center electricity consumption is projected to increase 130% by 2030, creating opportunities across power generation and grid infrastructure. GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog and slot reservations reached 116 gigawatts, while data center orders exceeded $5 billion in the first half of 2026, more than double the total for 2025.

Second-quarter orders surged 88% year over year, lifting the company's total backlog to $176 billion. Its businesses span gas turbines, transformers, substations and electrical equipment, allowing it to benefit from multiple stages of data center development. Growing equipment installations could also generate long-term maintenance and service revenue.

However, not all is good. GE Vernova's valuation already reflects substantial growth expectations. The stock trades at 53.74 times forward non-GAAP earnings, compared with the sector median of 19.32 times. Its forward enterprise value-to-sales ratio of 4.52 is more than double the sector median. These premiums leave limited room for disappointment if AI-related electricity demand grows more slowly than anticipated. Supply chain constraints could also delay the conversion of GE Vernova's substantial backlog into revenue.

#4 Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT)

Coatue Stake $3.05 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $210.7 Million

Applied Materials sells the equipment and services that chipmakers use to manufacture semiconductors. Coatue trimmed 1,034,719 shares and held $3.05 billion, or 6.26% of its portfolio. Bridgewater trimmed 268,492 shares and held $210.7 million, or 0.86% of its portfolio. Jim Cramer thinks there is more to the stock than its earnings multiple shows. Check what he said here.

Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) makes the machines chipmakers use to build semiconductors. Without them, Nvidia, Micron and others could not produce the chips AI needs. Chip shortages are expected to last for years, with memory shortages forecast to run through 2030, so chipmakers must keep adding capacity. Cloud giants keep raising their AI spending, and asset managers are building new funds focused on data centers. In the latest quarter, margins and earnings grew faster than sales. The stock has fallen about 48% from its high, and its forward P/E has dropped from about 55 to 29.5, which gives long-term buyers a cheaper entry.

The bull case rests on AI demand lasting for years, and nobody can guarantee that. Some investors expect the boom to end quickly, and chip equipment orders can swing sharply when chipmakers pause spending. The stock is also very volatile, which makes it a poor fit for conservative investors. A valuation recovery, with the forward P/E climbing back toward 40, is not certain, and a lower multiple would cut any gains. A 48% drop can also mean the market sees a problem that the numbers do not yet show at Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT).

#3 Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)

Coatue Stake $2.82 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $482.8 Million

Coatue raised its Amazon stake by 50% in the second quarter, buying 3,904,033 shares, and held $2.82 billion, or 5.80% of its portfolio. Bridgewater cut 2,363,230 shares, which took the position from 4.08% to 1.98% of its portfolio. The stake is still worth $482.8 million. Amazon also ranks second on our list of President Trump and Nancy Pelosi's top picks. Read why here.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) owns huge data centers full of computers and rents them out over the internet through AWS, its cloud business. AI companies need an enormous amount of computing power, so they rent it from Amazon and pay every month, like tenants paying a landlord. AWS growth has sped up for five straight quarters, reaching 37% last quarter, and Amazon says its capacity is sold out through 2027. Customers have signed contracts for years of future use, and that backlog doubled in the first half of the year. Anthropic and OpenAI are two of the biggest tenants, and Amazon owns stakes in both, so it gets paid as their landlord and as an owner. Advertising adds another strong profit stream, up 26% last quarter.

Amazon is spending so much on new data centers that free cash flow has turned negative and its debt has grown. If AI demand slows, those buildings will be expensive to keep. Much of the backlog comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, two companies that spend far more than they earn. A possible Anthropic IPO, which would put a public price on Amazon's stake, could also price below its last funding round. AI shopping agents could skip the sponsored products that drive most of Amazon's ad revenue, and the FTC's antitrust trial starts in March 2027 for Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN).

#2 Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

Coatue Stake $3.63 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $134.7 Million

Micron makes the memory chips that go into data centers and AI servers. Coatue raised its stake by 1,794%, buying 2,976,338 shares, and the position grew from 0.19% to 7.46% of its portfolio. It was worth $3.63 billion at the end of the quarter. Bridgewater went the other way and trimmed 1,359,038 shares, which cut the weight from 2.23% to 0.55% of its portfolio. It held $134.7 million. A Chinese memory maker could match Micron's DRAM wafer capacity by 2029, and that is the core of the bear case. Read the full bear case here.

Micron (NASDAQ:MU) is trading at about 5 times forward earnings, against a sector median of 21.6. Its forward PEG ratio is 0.07, against 1.13 for the sector, and on trailing earnings it trades at 11.6 times, well below its five-year average of 18.3. Revenue grew 256% from a year ago, and earnings have surged with it.

But before you get too excited about the valuation, listen to the bear argument. Bears say a low P/E on record profits is a warning sign for a cyclical stock. They point to Micron's own history, where strong earnings and a low P/E came before a big drop at least three times in the past decade. Fabs cost billions and take two to three years to build, so new supply from SK hynix and Chinese makers will arrive later, as it did after the PC era, the dot-com bubble, the 2017 cloud surge and the pandemic boom. Even bears say the shortage may last into 2028, but they expect the stock to peak before it ends, and Micron is already well below its June high. AI spending cannot grow forever, and the big spenders already have negative cash flow, which is a risk for Micron (NASDAQ:MU).

#1 Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Coatue Stake $4.09 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $406.6 Million

Lam Research makes the machines that chipmakers use to build chips. It is Coatue's second-largest position, at $4.09 billion or 8.41% of its portfolio, after Coatue trimmed 601,902 shares. Bridgewater trimmed 633,005 shares and held $406.6 million, or 1.67% of its portfolio. The stock was up about 73% for the year when we last covered it. Read our take on whether it is still a smart long-term AI pick here.

Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) makes the etching and deposition machines chipmakers use to build wafers. Advanced AI chips need more of those steps and take longer to make, so manufacturers need more equipment even if unit volumes stay the same. Bulls also see Lam as a shelter if the AI market cools. If AI chip prices fall as costs normalize while volumes rise, chipmakers still have to buy the machines to make them. Sales grew 54% last quarter, operating margins reached a record high, and the stock has fallen 29% since June, which gives new buyers a cheaper entry.

Guidance for the next quarter points to just 4.6% growth from the last one, after 22% in the September quarter, because unusually strong China orders are returning to normal. The stock fell about 12% on the report. China's strength may only be a timing issue as chipmakers absorb equipment they already bought, and ASML and Applied Materials both say demand there remains strong. Even so, equipment orders come in lumps, and a real pullback in AI spending would hit Lam directly.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of LRCX as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than LRCX that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .Click to continue reading and see the expanded list of 10 Stocks Billionaires Laffont and Dalio are Piling Into

news.Title: Garmin Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise Y/Y
news.Content:
Garmin Ltd. GRMN reported pro forma earnings of $2.76 per share for the third quarter of 2026, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.38 by 15.97%. The bottom line increased 39% year over year from $1.99 reported in the year-ago quarter.

Net sales rose 12% to $1.99 billion and came in line with the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Fitness and Outdoor together accounted for 65% of sales, supported by demand for wearables and adventure watches. Gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%.

GRMN's Fitness Revenues Rise on Wearable Demand

Fitness revenues advanced 16% year over year to $694.3 million. The segment benefited from continued demand for wearables, with operating income increasing 19% to $230.6 million. Gross and operating margins were 63% and 33%, respectively.

During the quarter, Garmin launched the CIRQA Smart Band, a screenless wearable offering health and fitness insights. The company also recently introduced new Edge cycling computers, including the Edge 1060 with hands-free voice controls and the Edge Explore 3 series.

Garmin Ltd. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Garmin Ltd. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Garmin Ltd. Quote

Garmin's Outdoor Sales Surge on Adventure Watches

Outdoor revenues jumped 20% to $597.3 million, primarily driven by demand for adventure watches. Operating income climbed 37% to $233 million, while gross and operating margins reached 68% and 39%, respectively.

The company launched the f??nix 9 and f??nix 9 Pro adventure watch series during the quarter. It also introduced Garmin Drive GPS navigators featuring high-resolution ultrawide displays. The launches expanded Garmin's flagship adventure watch and navigation offerings.

GRMN Sees Growth Across Aviation and Marine

Aviation revenues increased 5% to $252.7 million, led by original equipment manufacturer product categories. Operating income rose 8% to $65.8 million. The segment recorded gross and operating margins of 78% and 26%, respectively.

Garmin unveiled the G2000 PRIME flight deck for high-performance piston and electric aircraft and announced certification of an all-glass retrofit cockpit for the original Cessna CitationJet.

Marine revenues grew 16% to $309.9 million, driven by broad-based demand led by sonar products. Marine operating income surged 90% to $94 million, while gross and operating margins were 64% and 30%, respectively. The company launched LiveScope 2 and received six Product of Excellence awards from the National Marine Electronics Association.

Garmin's Auto OEM Revenues Contract

Story Continues

Auto OEM revenues declined 20% year over year to $131.9 million, primarily due to domain controllers. The segment recorded a gross margin of 16% and an operating loss of $11.9 million compared with a loss of $16.7 million a year earlier.

Lower operating expenses helped narrow the operating loss despite the decline in sales. Garmin continues to work toward the launch of its Mercedes-Benz domain controller program.

Garmin's Operating Profitability Improves

Gross profit increased 20% year over year to $1.26 billion, while gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%. Operating income rose 34% to $611.6 million, with operating margin expanding 500 basis points to 30.8%. Favorable segment mix, lower product costs and approximately $33 million in refunds of previously paid tariffs supported profitability. GAAP earnings jumped 35% to $2.80 per share.

Operating expenses increased 10% to $646.1 million. Research and development expenses rose 9% to $312.9 million, mainly due to personnel costs. Selling, general and administrative expenses climbed 10% to $333.2 million, reflecting higher personnel-related and advertising expenses.

Garmin Returns Cash to Shareholders

Garmin generated $393.9 million in operating cash flow and $293.3 million in free cash flow during the quarter compared with $485.6 million and $425.1 million, respectively, a year earlier. Capital expenditures totaled $100.6 million. In the first three quarters of 2026, it generated operating and free cash flows of $1.33 billion and $1.04 billion, respectively. It incurred capital expenditure of $295 million during the first nine months of 2026.

The company paid $202 million in dividends and repurchased $41 million of shares. In the first three quarters of 2026, Garmin paid $578.5 million in dividends and bought shares worth $123.2 million. Approximately $407 million remained under its share repurchase authorization at the end of the third quarter. It ended the quarter with approximately $4.1 billion in cash and marketable securities and $2.25 billion in inventory.

Garmin Raises 2026 Outlook

Garmin now expects 2026 revenues of approximately $8.15 billion, up from its prior projection of $8.05 billion. Pro forma earnings are forecast at $10.80 per share compared with the previous outlook of $10.

The company raised its gross margin forecast to 61% from 59.7% and its operating margin estimate to 29% from 27%. The projected pro forma tax rate remains unchanged at 16.5%.

news.Title: TXN's Gross Margin Crosses 64% in Q3: Can It Improve Further?
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN delivered a strong improvement in profitability in the third quarter of 2026, raising hopes that its gross margin can climb further. The semiconductor maker reported a gross margin of 64.2%, up from 57.4% in the year-ago quarter and 61.4% in the previous quarter.

Texas Instruments' third-quarter gross profit rose 43% year over year to $3.89 billion, outpacing the 28% increase in revenues to $6.06 billion. Higher sales volumes supported the improvement, while better factory utilization, pricing and product mix also helped. These trends suggest that stronger demand can translate into better profitability when production facilities operate more efficiently.

Growth across key markets offers additional support. Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year, while automotive revenues grew at a mid-teens rate. Data center revenues surged about 95%, reflecting rising demand for chips used in expanding computing infrastructure. Continued strength in these markets could help TXN maintain higher production levels and spread manufacturing costs across more units.

Texas Instruments' 300-millimeter wafer manufacturing strategy could also support cost efficiency as output rises. Per the company, an unpackaged chip built on 300-millimeter wafers costs approximately 40% less than one built on 200-millimeter wafers. Texas Instruments has available cleanroom capacity in its Richardson, Sherman and Lehi facilities. Management plans to install additional equipment according to demand, supporting dependable supply and cost efficiency as production volumes increase.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues and earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 37.7% and 94.5%, respectively. These projections imply continued business activity, which could further expand Texas Instruments' margins.

How Do TXN's Competitors Compare on Gross Margin?

Analog Devices, Inc. ADI is a close competitor in analog chips and signal-processing technology. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI's revenues rose 40% year over year to $4.02 billion, while its GAAP gross margin increased to 67.3% from 62.1% in the year-ago quarter.

Its adjusted gross margin reached 72.5% from 69.2% in the year-ago quarter, highlighting strong profitability. These results put Analog Devices ahead of TXN's 64.2% gross margin.

Microchip Technology Incorporated MCHP is another competitor, supplying microcontrollers and embedded-control chips. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues grew 38% year over year to $1.49 billion.

Story Continues

Microchip Technology's GAAP gross margin improved to 63.2% from 53.6% in the year-ago quarter, while its non-GAAP gross margin reached 63.8% from 54.3%. Higher factory utilization and recovering demand supported the improvement.

Both companies show how stronger demand and manufacturing efficiency can lift margins. Analog Devices' higher reported margin sets a competitive benchmark, while Microchip Technology's performance highlights the benefits of better factory utilization.

news.Title: Lam Research Sees Record Foundry Sales: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
Lam Research Corporation LRCX is benefiting from rising demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, its foundry business achieved record revenues, while the foundry's share of Systems revenues increased to 46% from 44% in the previous quarter. Demand came from leading-edge chipmaking and advanced packaging as well as mature-node capacity spending in China. The company's total Systems revenues soared 34.9% sequentially to $5.73 billion.

Advanced logic chips are becoming more complex as artificial intelligence (AI) workloads require greater computing power. This trend increases demand for advanced patterning, deposition and etch equipment, where Lam Research has established capabilities. Advanced packaging also creates opportunities as chipmakers seek better performance and power efficiency. LRCX's investments in these technologies could help it win more equipment orders and expand its market opportunity.

The broader outlook is encouraging. Lam Research expects wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending to exceed $200 billion in calendar year 2027, up from the mid-$150 billion range expected for 2026. Management also identified leading-edge foundry and logic, alongside DRAM, as major sources of future growth. However, cleanroom shortages and supply constraints affecting certain components could limit the industry's ability to meet demand.

Rising AI-related demand and greater chipmaking complexity provide longer-term support for Lam Research's prospects. Rising mature-node capacity spending in China could further boost foundry revenues.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues is currently pegged at $34.66 billion and $41.38 billion, respectively. The consensus mark for fiscal 2027 and 2028 top lines indicates year-over-year growth of 49.2% and 19.4%, respectively.

How Applied Materials and KLA Compete With Lam Research

Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT competes with Lam Research in semiconductor manufacturing equipment used to make advanced chips. Its tools support materials engineering, leading-edge foundry production and advanced packaging.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Applied Materials reported record revenues of $9.12 billion, up 25% year over year. Non-GAAP earnings per share climbed 41% year over year to $3.50. Its growth outlook highlights strong demand for advanced foundry and logic equipment, making it a serious competitor as chipmakers expand capacity.

KLA Corporation KLAC offers a different but relevant competitive challenge through inspection and process-control equipment that helps chipmakers detect defects and improve production yields.

Story Continues

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, KLA's revenues increased 15.2% year over year to $3.66 billion. Results benefited from AI infrastructure investment, leading-edge foundry/logic demand and rising process control intensity. Advanced packaging process control revenues are now expected to reach about $1.1 billion in calendar year 2026. The company's non-GAAP earnings increased 11.7% year over year to $1.05 per share.

Applied Materials competes more directly in equipment manufacturing, while KLA benefits from the growing need for chip quality control. Their growth underscores the opportunity and competitive pressure for Lam Research as foundry spending rises.

news.Title: HPE Benefits From AI Infrastructure Demand: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE is benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads across Agentic AI, Enterprise AI, Private Cloud AI, AI fabs and hyperscalers, leading to multiyear revenue growth and record backlogs.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, HPE's Cloud & AI revenues reached $9 billion, up 25% year over year, with a 17% operating margin. Server revenues rose 35%, while traditional server orders increased 75% as customers favored AI-ready configurations and higher-value systems. HPE's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Cloud & AI revenues are expected to grow 60% to 72%.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, AI systems orders were $2.4 billion, up more than 30% sequentially, while AI systems backlog rose 14% sequentially to $6.8 billion. Private Cloud AI orders increased triple digits year over year, showing wider adoption of HPE's on-premises AI factory approach.

HPE was also awarded a $3.5 billion inferencing deal with a hyperscaler customer, adding evidence that enterprise AI deployments are moving beyond pilots. Supporting its AI infrastructure, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is expanding its hybrid cloud operating model through GreenLake, which lets customers manage infrastructure and software across on-premises and cloud environments with consumption-based economics.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise has used acquisitions to add networking, cloud management, security and data-management capabilities around its hybrid IT model. These factors will support HPE's capabilities and long-term growth outlook.

How Competitors Fare Against HPE

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's closest competitors in this domain are Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO. Dell AI Factory combined with NVIDIA is arguably the most direct alternative for HPE private cloud AI.

Dell provides pre-integrated GPU servers, storage, networking and software for enterprise AI and competes head-to-head with HPE for Fortune 1000 AI deployments. Cisco focuses on AI networking and integrated AI Pods. Cisco has started competing strongly with HPE after acquiring Splunk and through its partnership with NVIDIA.

news.Title: NXPI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Auto and Industrial Growth
news.Content:
NXP Semiconductors N.V. NXPI reported better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, driven by higher automotive semiconductor content, industrial demand and data center infrastructure growth.

NXPI reported non-GAAP earnings of $4.20 per share, which increased 35% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.45%.

Revenues increased 19.3% year over year to $3.79 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate by 0.41%. Automotive sales crossed $2 billion for the first time, while Industrial & IoT revenues surged 39% as customers expanded automation and intelligent-edge deployments.

NXPI's Automotive Business Benefits From Content Gains

Automotive revenues were $2.07 billion, up 13% year over year and 7% sequentially. Excluding the divested MEMS sensor business, automotive sales grew 17% year over year. Management attributed the strength to software-defined vehicles, electrification, connectivity and radar rather than an increase in vehicle production.

Software-defined vehicle revenues are running above $1.5 billion on an annualized basis, keeping NXPI on track for its $2 billion target in 2027. The company plans to begin shipping its S32K5 zonal processor and S32N central compute platforms next year. Volkswagen and Rivian's joint venture selected S32K5 for its zonal platform, supporting NXPI's position in the emerging vehicle architecture market.

NXP Semiconductors N.V. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NXP Semiconductors N.V. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NXP Semiconductors N.V. Quote

NXPI's Industrial and Infrastructure Sales Accelerate

Industrial & IoT revenues climbed 39% year over year and 6% sequentially to $802 million. The industrial portion grew nearly 50%, supported by data centers, factory automation and health care, and now accounts for about 70% of the end market's revenues.

Communication Infrastructure & Other generated $503 million, up 54% year over year and 11% sequentially, benefiting from data center and secure-card demand. Mobile revenues, however, declined 4% year over year to $411 million, despite a 17% sequential increase, reflecting a more uneven demand profile across NXPI's portfolio.

NXPI's Margins Improve With Higher Factory Utilization

Non-GAAP gross profit rose 22% year over year to $2.22 billion, while gross margin increased 160 basis points to 58.6%. Management cited higher factory utilization and improved revenue flow-through, alongside favorable product mix and operating efficiencies.

Non-GAAP operating income climbed 31% to $1.41 billion. Operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 37.1%, while non-GAAP operating expenses were $810 million, or 21.4% of revenues. Management expects manufacturing utilization to rise further in 2027 and gross margin to reach 60% during that year.

Story Continues

NXPI's Cash Generation Supports Larger Buybacks

Operating cash flow reached $1.26 billion in the quarter. After $50 million of net capital spending, non-GAAP free cash flow totaled $1.21 billion, representing 31.9% of revenues. NXPI returned $359 million through dividends and share repurchases.

The company finished the quarter with $3.94 billion in cash and $10.98 billion in debt, leaving net financial leverage at 1.3 times. Inventory days fell to 148 from 156 in the preceding quarter. Following quarter-end, the board authorized an additional $5 billion in share repurchases, bringing total authorization to about $6.3 billion.

NXPI Guides Fourth-Quarter Growth and Higher Earnings

For the fourth quarter of 2026, NXPI forecasts revenues between $3.75 billion and $3.95 billion. The $3.85 billion midpoint implies 15% year-over-year and 2% sequential growth. The company expects automotive and industrial sales to increase sequentially, while mobile demand remains weaker year over year.

Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 59% at the midpoint, with an operating margin of 37.5%. Non-GAAP earnings per share are expected between $4.14 and $4.58, with a midpoint of $4.36. Looking to 2027, management anticipates double-digit revenue growth, supported by software-defined vehicles, industrial AI and data center infrastructure.

news.Title: FFIV Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Systems Growth
news.Content:
F5, Inc. FFIV reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.42 per share increased 0.7% year over year and surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.3%.

Revenues rose 13% year over year to $917 million, beating the consensus mark by 3.7%. Results benefited from robust systems demand, software expansion and hybrid multicloud adoption. Product revenues advanced 23%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

FFIV's Q4 Revenue Details

Product revenues, representing 56% of total revenues, increased 23% year over year to $510 million. Systems revenues jumped 29% to $239 million, driven by infrastructure refreshes, capacity expansion, competitive displacements and investments in digital sovereignty and AI readiness.

Software revenues rose 19% to $271 million. Subscription-based software revenues increased 16% to $229 million, representing 85% of software revenues. Perpetual license revenues climbed 37% to $42 million. Services revenues, accounting for 44% of total revenues, grew 3% to $408 million.

F5, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Recurring revenue sources contributed 68% of quarterly revenues. Geographically, EMEA led growth with a 31% increase, representing 30% of total revenue. APAC revenues rose 14%, contributing 17%, while Americas revenues increased 5%, accounting for 53%.

F5 Benefits From Hybrid Multicloud and AI Demand

Management highlighted sustained demand from hybrid multicloud adoption, application security modernization and AI inference workloads. Platform consolidation remained a key opportunity, with 29% of F5's top 1,000 customers adopting three or more product families, up from 22% in fiscal 2025.

During the quarter, a large North American financial institution selected F5 for an eight-figure application delivery and security deployment, displacing four incumbent vendors. An Asian central bank technology authority also selected F5 for a national financial services cloud, replacing two competitors.

AI-related opportunities accelerated. Direct AI use-case bookings exceeded $100 million in fiscal 2026, growing nearly 300% year over year. The customer base for these solutions expanded fourfold to more than 200, supported by demand for AI data delivery, runtime security and AI factory load balancing.

FFIV Expands Security and Software Opportunities

F5 continued expanding its AI-powered security portfolio as enterprises sought protection against increasingly sophisticated application and API threats. Its AI-powered Distributed Cloud WAF capabilities attracted more than 300 customers since their March launch, with over 75% operating in blocking mode.

Story Continues

The company also gained more than 200 F5 Insight customers since its March launch. The platform provides automated fleet management and upgrade orchestration, helping enterprises reduce operational complexity and accelerate security updates.

For fiscal 2026, software revenues increased 8% to $870 million. SaaS and managed services annualized recurring revenues reached $211 million, up 14% year over year. Core SaaS and managed services ARR grew 24%, while total security-related revenues increased 10% to approximately $1.3 billion.

F5's Operating Margins Face Cost Pressures

Non-GAAP gross margin contracted 30 basis points year over year to 84%. Non-GAAP operating margin declined 330 basis points to 33.7%, reflecting higher operating expenses despite strong revenue growth.

Management attributed higher operating expenses partly to investments in sales capacity, AI security specialists and marketing. Strong year-end performance also increased commission and bonus expenses.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $309 million from $299 million.

FFIV Maintains Solid Liquidity and Shareholder Returns

F5 generated $118 million in operating cash flow and $91 million in free cash flow during the quarter. Working capital investments, including inventory accumulation and supplier prepayments, affected cash generation as management secured components for future systems demand.

Cash and investments totaled $1.62 billion at quarter-end. The company repurchased $100 million of shares during the quarter, bringing fiscal 2026 repurchases to $600 million. Its board authorized an additional $1.5 billion for share repurchases, supplementing the $322 million remaining under the existing program.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, F5 expects revenues between $875 million and $895 million. Non-GAAP earnings are projected in the range of $4.25-$4.37 per share. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 81.5% and 82.5%.

For fiscal 2027, management projects revenue growth of 8-9% and non-GAAP earnings of $18.00-$18.30 per share. The company anticipates upper-single-digit systems growth, double-digit software growth and low-to-mid-single-digit services growth.

Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 80.5% and 82.5%, suggesting higher component costs. Non-GAAP operating margin is projected at 33-35%. news.Title: NXPI Q3 Earnings Call Highlights SDV and Data Center Growth
news.Content:
NXP Semiconductors N.V. NXPI emphasized software-defined vehicles (SDVs), industrial artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure as key growth drivers during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call.

The company exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate for both earnings and revenues. Management also outlined expectations for double-digit revenue growth in 2027, margin expansion and accelerated shareholder returns while addressing supply constraints and pricing trends.

NXP Beat Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

NXPI reported third-quarter non-GAAP earnings of $4.20 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.14 by $0.06. Earnings increased 35% year over year from $3.11.

Revenues totaled $3.79 billion, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.77 billion. The top line increased 19% year over year and 8% sequentially.

NXP Semiconductors N.V. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NXP Semiconductors N.V. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NXP Semiconductors N.V. Quote

CFO Bill Betz attributed the improvement to higher factory utilization and operating leverage. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 58.6%, while operating margin expanded to 37.1%.

NXPI Targets Higher Automotive Content Through SDVs

President and CEO Rafael Sotomayor highlighted the accelerating adoption of zonal and centralized computing architectures, which provide two to three times greater semiconductor content per vehicle.

Automotive revenues reached $2.07 billion, increasing 13% year over year. The SDV business exceeded a $1.5 billion annualized revenue run rate, supporting its $2 billion target for 2027.

Sotomayor highlighted RV Tech's decision to standardize its zonal platform on NXP's S32K5 processor. Initial shipments into China are expected in early 2027, with broader production ramps anticipated in 2028.

NXP Expands Its Data Center Revenue Ambitions

Sotomayor raised expectations for NXP's data center business, projecting revenues above $500 million in 2026 and exceeding $1 billion by 2028.

Responding to questions from Bank of America Securities, he explained that NXP focuses on control-plane processors, networking and security rather than discrete power components.

Management emphasized that growth depends on product introductions, customer design wins and software deployments, positioning data centers as another source of revenue diversification.

NXPI Sees Industrial AI Adoption Accelerating

Industrial & IoT revenues increased 39% year over year to $802 million, supported by factory automation, health care and data center demand.

Story Continues

Sotomayor expects AI-enabled processors to account for approximately 15% of Industrial & IoT processor revenues in 2026, more than doubling their contribution from 2025.

NXP also secured its first S32K5 design win in humanoid robotics. Its Ara discrete neural processing unit continues to attract customer interest, with volume production expected in 2028.

NXP Addresses Supply Tightness and Inventory Trends

During the Goldman Sachs discussion, Sotomayor said widespread automotive customer restocking had not materialized despite improving demand visibility.

Betz subsequently told JPMorgan that book-to-bill remained well above one across all end markets and regions. Approximately 80% of lead times exceeded 16 weeks compared with 25% a year earlier.

Addressing questions from UBS, Betz identified tight back-end manufacturing capacity and potential front-end constraints in 2027. Planned capacity investments are intended to support additional demand.

NXPI Outlines Margin Expansion and 2027 Growth

For the fourth quarter, management guided revenues to $3.75-$3.95 billion and non-GAAP earnings between $4.14 per share and $4.58 per share.

Betz expects non-GAAP gross margin of 59% at the midpoint, supported by improved utilization. Management targets a 60% gross margin during 2027 and further expansion in 2028.

During the Barclays discussion, Betz attributed margin improvements primarily to operational efficiencies rather than price increases. For 2027, management anticipates double-digit revenue growth and capital expenditures around 5% of revenues.

NXP Prioritizes Cash Generation and Shareholder Returns

Third-quarter free cash flow reached $1.21 billion, representing approximately 32% of revenues and supporting manufacturing investments and shareholder distributions.

The board authorized an additional $5 billion in repurchases, bringing the total authorization to approximately $6.3 billion. Betz expects buybacks to accelerate during the fourth quarter and throughout 2027.

Management's priorities remain executing product ramps, expanding manufacturing capacity and improving profitability while returning excess free cash flow to shareholders.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: Cirrus Logic (CRUS) Q2 Earnings Expected to Decline
news.Content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues when Cirrus Logic (CRUS) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 4, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.44 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -13.8%.

Revenues are expected to be $540.56 million, down 3.6% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 5.6% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Cirrus Logic?

For Cirrus Logic, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.82%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #5.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Cirrus Logic will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Cirrus Logic would post earnings of $1.8 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.84, delivering a surprise of +2.22%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. news.Title: Volkswagen Bets $4B on Audi's U.S. Expansion: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Volkswagen VWAGY is strengthening its manufacturing and technological capabilities through two strategic initiatives. Its luxury brand Audi plans to invest approximately $4 billion in its first U.S. manufacturing facility in Georgia, while Volkswagen has expanded its partnership with NXP Semiconductors NXPI to advance its software-defined vehicle technology.

These initiatives could help Volkswagen reduce tariff exposure, improve cost efficiency and strengthen its global competitiveness, although significant investments and execution risks remain.

Audi's $4B U.S. Plant to Reduce Tariff Exposure

Audi plans to invest approximately $4 billion in a Georgia manufacturing facility, creating around 4,500 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027, with production expected in the early 2030s. The plant will have an annual capacity of up to 200,000 vehicles, manufacturing premium SUVs, including the Q7, Q8 and Q9. Roughly half of the output is expected to be exported.

The investment could strengthen Audi's position in the U.S. premium automotive market, where deliveries remained roughly flat through the first nine months of 2026 after declining 16% in 2025. Local production could improve its competitiveness against BMW and Mercedes-Benz, which already have U.S. manufacturing operations.

Importantly, the facility could reduce tariff-related costs. Audi incurred approximately €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) in tariff expenses in 2025, with all U.S.-bound vehicles imported from Europe or Mexico. With tariffs on German vehicle imports currently at 15%, localized manufacturing could lower import expenses, logistics costs and currency risks.

The plant would also establish North America as Audi's third major production hub alongside Europe and China, improving geographic diversification. However, significant upfront capital expenditures, construction risks and Volkswagen's ongoing European restructuring could pressure near-term cash flows.

NXP Partnership to Improve Volkswagen's Operating Efficiency

Volkswagen has expanded its collaboration with NXP Semiconductors to develop its next-generation software-defined vehicle architecture. NXP's S32K5 microcontrollers will be a common component of the zonal architecture Volkswagen is developing through its joint venture with Rivian Automotive RIVN. The first vehicle featuring the technology is planned for 2027.

The architecture will consolidate multiple vehicle functions into fewer electronic control units, reducing hardware complexity and component requirements. Standardizing this technology across Volkswagen's brands could generate economies of scale, lower development costs and accelerate the introduction of advanced digital features.

Story Continues

What Lies Ahead for Volkswagen?

Volkswagen's initiatives could improve its long-term profitability by addressing high import-related expenses and growing vehicle technology costs. Audi's U.S. expansion may support premium vehicle sales and margins, while semiconductor standardization could deliver group-wide manufacturing and development efficiencies.

Nevertheless, the benefits will materialize gradually, with the new semiconductor architecture expected in 2027 and Audi's U.S. production beginning in the early 2030s. Substantial capital requirements, ongoing restructuring and execution risks could constrain near-term earnings.

news.Content:
Investing.com - Nasdaq futures advanced on Wednesday after stronger-than-expected results from South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix sparked a global rally in artificial intelligence-linked semiconductor stocks. Investors were also looking ahead to earnings from major technology companies and a Federal Reserve interest rate decision.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 06:06 ET (10:06 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures had gained 132 points, or 0.4%, while S&P 500 futures had risen 10 points, or 0.1%. Dow futures, meanwhile, had dropped 105 points, or 0.2%.

Here are some of the biggest premarket U.S. stock movers today:

SK Hynix shares surged 7.4% in premarket trading to $156.15 after the memory chipmaker reported record third-quarter 2026 results, with revenue exceeding KRW 100 trillion for the first time in a single quarter. Revenue reached KRW 104.62 trillion, while operating profit jumped 632% year-over-year to KRW 83.33 trillion, representing an operating margin of 80% and beating analyst expectations. The company also announced plans to return approximately KRW 100 trillion to shareholders through fiscal 2026, including at least KRW 30 trillion in cash dividends and at least KRW 60 trillion in share repurchases and cancellations, marking its largest shareholder-return commitment to date.

Vertiv Holdings surged 15.1% before the bell after the data-center power and cooling equipment provider reported third-quarter results that comfortably beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year outlook. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.21 per share, above the $1.82 consensus, while revenue jumped 61% year-over-year to $4.31 billion, topping forecasts of $3.75 billion. Organic orders more than doubled from a year earlier, easing concerns that delays in AI-related projects were holding back revenue growth. Vertiv raised its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast to $7.15 per share, compared with the previous consensus of $6.73, and projected revenue of $14.65 billion, above expectations of $13.99 billion. Its fourth-quarter outlook also exceeded analyst estimates.

Ultra Clean Holdings climbed 12% in premarket trading after the semiconductor equipment supplier reported record third-quarter results and issued an upbeat forecast for the current quarter. Adjusted earnings reached $1.15 per share, beating the $0.94 analyst consensus, while revenue rose nearly 49% year-over-year to a record $759 million, above estimates of $728.07 million. Profitability also improved, with non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 17.3% from 15.7% in the previous quarter and operating margin increasing to 9% from 7%. For the fourth quarter, the company forecast revenue of $800 million to $860 million, with the midpoint above the $813.9 million consensus, and adjusted earnings of $1.11 to $1.35 per share.

Story Continues

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

GE HealthCare Technologies jumped 5.4% before the open after the medical technology company reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and raised its full-year outlook. Adjusted earnings came in at $1.34 per share, ahead of the $1.20 analyst estimate, while revenue reached $5.5 billion, exceeding expectations of $5.35 billion. Revenue grew 7.2% overall and 6.2% organically. Net income margin expanded to 11.1% from 8.7% a year earlier, while adjusted EBIT margin rose to 16.6% from 14.8%, supported by volume growth, pricing and cost productivity. Free cash flow increased by $310 million year-over-year to $793 million.

F5 fell 6.6% in premarket trading after the application security and delivery company paired a fiscal fourth-quarter earnings beat with a 2027 outlook that disappointed investors. The company forecast revenue growth of 8% to 9% for the coming fiscal year, while projecting a non-GAAP gross margin of 80.5% to 82.5%, below the 84% reported in the latest quarter. The outlook raised concerns that higher component costs and increased investment in sales capacity could weigh on profitability, despite the latest earnings beat.

Enphase Energy plunged 15.8% after the solar technology company reported third-quarter earnings and revenue below expectations and issued a weaker-than-anticipated fourth-quarter forecast. Adjusted earnings came in at $0.41 per share, missing the $0.51 consensus, while revenue of $293.3 million fell short of estimates of $303.85 million and declined sharply from the year-earlier period. Enphase forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $225 million to $255 million, with the midpoint of $240 million well below analysts' expectations of around $300.5 million, pointing to further sequential weakness in sales.

SolarEdge Technologies fell 7.1% in premarket trading to $29.87, following the selloff in solar stocks triggered by Enphase Energy's disappointing results and weak revenue guidance. Enphase's earnings miss and forecast for fourth-quarter revenue well below Wall Street expectations heightened concerns about demand across the solar sector, dragging down peer stocks.

NXP Semiconductors dropped 8.5% before the bell as investors focused on the chipmaker's fourth-quarter outlook despite a stronger-than-expected third-quarter performance. Revenue rose 19% year-over-year to $3.79 billion, while adjusted earnings of $4.20 per share topped the $4.11 consensus. However, the company's fourth-quarter revenue forecast of $3.85 billion at the midpoint came in slightly below analyst expectations. Its projected adjusted operating income of $1.374 billion to $1.442 billion also fell short of the $1.44 billion FactSet consensus at the midpoint, raising concerns about a slowdown from the previous quarter's momentum.

Boston Scientific slid 3.6% in premarket trading to $43.42 after the medical device maker reported a third-quarter earnings miss and lowered its full-year forecast. Adjusted earnings came in at $0.73 per share, below the $0.75 consensus, while revenue of $5.14 billion edged past estimates of $5.12 billion and grew 1.5% year-over-year. The company forecast fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.77 to $0.79 per share, below the $0.83 analyst consensus, and cut its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings outlook to $3.16 to $3.18 per share from $3.28 to $3.32. Boston Scientific also expects fourth-quarter sales to decline 1% to 3% year-over-year, citing lingering disruption from an August cyberattack that affected manufacturing, order processing and global shipments.

VF Corporation fell 5.5% before the bell despite the apparel maker reporting better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter 2027 results. Adjusted earnings reached $0.70 per share, beating the $0.53 analyst consensus, while revenue of $2.7 billion topped estimates of $2.66 billion. Adjusted operating income of $364 million also exceeded the company's guidance of approximately $315 million. The decline came despite the earnings beat, as investors appeared to take profits after the stock had rallied sharply ahead of the results.

news.Title: SK Hynix Stock Gains 1.9% on AI Chip Demand, Dividend Hopes
news.Content:
SK hynix Inc. 's SKHY shares jumped on Oct. 27, supported by optimism over potential shareholder payouts, resilient demand for artificial intelligence (AI) chips and expectations surrounding the memory-chip maker's quarterly results. The stock's movement reflected investors' continued interest in companies supplying critical components for AI infrastructure, as data-center operators and technology companies maintain substantial spending on advanced computing capacity.

A major near-term catalyst was the anticipation of SK Hynix's third-quarter earnings announcement, scheduled for Oct. 28. Reports that the company was considering a special dividend of about 16 trillion won ($12 billion), potentially funded by gains from its investment in Japanese memory-chip maker Kioxia, also boosted sentiment. However, SK Hynix clarified on Oct. 26 that no decision had been finalized, saying it was reviewing various shareholder-return measures.

The dividend speculation came against a favorable industry backdrop. SK Hynix is a major supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which is essential for advanced AI accelerators and data-center applications. Increasing demand for these products has supported memory pricing and strengthened expectations for revenue growth. Investors have also been monitoring developments in next-generation HBM technology and manufacturers' ability to expand production to meet customers' requirements.

Broader market sentiment provided additional support. Asian equities advanced as technology shares benefited from renewed optimism about AI-related investments following a rally on Wall Street. SK Hynix's prospects remained closely tied to capital expenditure by major cloud-service providers and the pace at which AI adoption translates into sustained demand for memory chips.

Comparison With Peers

SKHY, which currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), is part of the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry. Its shares have gained 14.4% over the past three months against a 1% decline for the industry. Lam Research Corporation LRCX and Broadcom Inc. AVGO, two of SKHY's peers from the same industry, have lost 4.5% and 7.5% in the period, respectively. While AVGO carries a Rank #3, LRCX has a Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Bottom Line

Overall, SK Hynix's Tuesday advance reflected earnings anticipation, potential shareholder returns and confidence in AI-driven memory demand. Nevertheless, the proposed special dividend remained unconfirmed, while investors still weighed the sustainability of elevated chip prices and continued AI infrastructure spending when assessing the stock's outlook.
