news.Title: Broadcom Drops 6% in a Month: Buy, Sell or Hold the AVGO Stock?
news.Content:
Broadcom AVGO shares have dropped 5.8% over the past month, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's drop of 5.1%. The company's shares have suffered from margin pressure from the rising AI mix, supply constraints, a concentrated AI clientele and weak non-AI business.

AVGO shares have also underperformed NVIDIA NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Skyworks SWKS over the same period. Shares of NVIDIA have dropped 5.6%, while AMD and Skyworks have declined 12.6% and 4.8%, respectively. So, what should investors do with the AVGO stock post the dip? Let us find out.

AVGO Stock's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AVGO's Prospects Suffer From Multiple Challenges

Broadcom's rapidly expanding custom accelerator business is weighing on consolidated gross margins because XPUs carry an increasing proportion of expensive memory content. In the third quarter of 2026, non-GAAP gross margin declined 210 basis points sequentially to 75%. AVGO expects gross margin to decline further to approximately 73% in the fourth quarter compared with 78% in the year-ago period. Continued growth in lower-margin AI hardware relative to software could limit profitability expansion, although operating leverage should provide some offset.

AVGO faces limitations involving advanced semiconductor wafers, high-bandwidth memory, substrates and optical components. The company's custom AI accelerator business currently depends on six major customers, exposing AVGO to changes in hyperscaler capital spending and product strategies. Competition from NVIDIA, AMD, MediaTek and customers' internal semiconductor development teams could intensify over time. Any loss of design wins, customer insourcing or moderation in AI infrastructure investments could affect revenue growth and long-term earnings visibility.

Moreover, Broadcom's non-AI semiconductor business continues to experience relatively modest growth compared with its AI portfolio. In the third quarter of 2026, non-AI revenues increased only 5% year over year to $4.2 billion and remained flat sequentially. While broadband and server storage demand improved, weakness in wireless partially offset these gains. Continued softness across traditional semiconductor end markets could constrain revenue diversification. Broader concerns surrounding the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending have also weighed on semiconductor stocks, including Broadcom.

Can AVGO's Strong AI Growth Boost Competitive Prowess?

Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenues to reach approximately $58 billion in fiscal 2026, followed by $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. These projections reflect increasing deployments of custom accelerators and AI networking equipment by leading frontier-model developers.

Broadcom's long-term agreement with Google to develop and supply future generations of TPUs and networking products through 2031 strengthens revenue visibility. Anthropic is expected to deploy an additional 5 gigawatts of TPU capacity in 2027 and 10 incremental gigawatts in 2028. OpenAI is targeting more than 5 gigawatts of custom accelerator deployments in 2028, while Meta is expected to deploy approximately 3 gigawatts through 2028. These customer roadmaps offer substantial multiyear growth opportunities.

Broadcom's expertise in advanced packaging, high-speed SerDes, chip-to-chip interconnects and high-bandwidth memory integration provides a competitive advantage. The company's ability to co-develop accelerators optimized for customers' specific AI workloads could support additional design wins. Increasing semiconductor complexity and the transition toward multi-die architectures may further strengthen demand for Broadcom's engineering capabilities.

Growing enterprise requirements for data sovereignty, cybersecurity and cost-effective AI infrastructure could strengthen adoption of VMware Cloud Foundation and VMware Private AI Cloud. These platforms enable organizations to operate AI workloads alongside existing enterprise applications. Rising subscription adoption and recurring revenues could improve software revenue visibility and support Broadcom's long-term profitability.

However, Broadcom's projected growth relies heavily on sustained capital expenditures by a limited number of hyperscalers and AI model developers. Higher HBM content, increasingly complex packaging and growing dependence on custom accelerators could continue pressuring gross margins. Although Broadcom expects operating leverage to offset some dilution, rising manufacturing costs or unfavorable semiconductor pricing could constrain long-term margin expansion. The company is facing stiff competition, which is a concern for investors.

Story Continues

AVGO's FY26 Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Steady Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $11.79 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating 72.87% growth from the fiscal 2025 reported figure.

AVGO Stock: Buy, Sell or Hold?

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales (P/S), AVGO is trading at 9.04X, higher than the broader sector's 5.49X. Broadcom is also trading at a premium compared with peers, NVIDIA and Skyworks, shares of which are currently trading at 9.96X and 2.76X, respectively.

news.Title: SCI Stock Surges More Than 111% in 6 Months: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
SCI Engineered Materials, Inc. 's SCIA investors have been gaining from the stock over the past few months. Shares of the Columbus, OH-based global supplier and manufacturer of advanced materials for Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) thin-film applications surged 111.3% in the past six months against the industry's 11.2% decline. It has also outperformed the sector and the S&P 500's gains of 6.6% and 6.4%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Two major developments of SCIA in recent months include the installation of a Plasma Spheroidization System or PSS (in August) and the announcement of its promising second-quarter 2026 results (in July).

In the second quarter, SCI reported record revenues and strong earnings growth, supported by higher raw material input costs, favorable product mix and increased volume. Higher revenues boosted gross profit, operating income and net income. However, gross margin contracted due to elevated raw material costs and product mix.

Management highlighted improving demand, new customer additions and growing traction in key markets. SCIA also expanded its workforce and ordered manufacturing equipment to support future growth, while interest in its specialized services continued to increase.

SCIA's Six-Month Price Comparison

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Over the past six months, the stock's performance has remained strong, outperforming its peers like Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Cirrus Logic, Inc. CRUS. Marvell Technology and Cirrus Logic's shares have gained 52.6% and lost 30.5%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Despite risks related to significant customer concentration, fluctuating raw material costs and tariff uncertainties, SCI's favorable share price movement reflects positive investor sentiment.

SCIA primarily serves the photonics industry, supplying advanced materials for PVD thin-film applications. Its target markets include aerospace, automotive, defense, glass, optical coatings and solar. SCI collaborates with end users and original equipment manufacturers to develop customized material solutions.

SCIA's Growth Opportunities

SCI's expanding order backlog reflects improving business activity and provides greater visibility into potential future revenues. The backlog increased both sequentially and year over year at the end of the second quarter, indicating a stronger pipeline of customer orders. This development could support production planning and help sustain business activity as pending orders are fulfilled. Continued execution of these orders remains important for maintaining growth momentum.

Story Continues

SCI's installation of a PSS in August expanded its advanced materials manufacturing capabilities. The equipment enables the production of high-purity spherical powders suitable for additive manufacturing, including those derived from high-value precious metals. These capabilities could create opportunities in aeronautical, defense and biomedical applications, where material quality and performance are critical. Planned targeted marketing initiatives may help SCIA establish a stronger presence in these specialized markets.

SCI's toll manufacturing business offers additional opportunities beyond conventional material sales. Its capabilities include diffusion bonding, indium bonding, powder processing and vacuum hot pressing, addressing customers' specialized production requirements. Revenue from toll manufacturing and related services improved in the previous fiscal year, alongside growing demand for engineering-related projects. These customized offerings could deepen customer relationships and support additional business opportunities.

SCI's Financial Strength

SCI's operating cash flow strengthened during the first half of the year, supported by improved profitability and higher customer deposits. Cash reserves and working capital also increased from the previous year-end, reinforcing its liquidity position. These resources provide flexibility to meet operational requirements, fund equipment investments and pursue growth initiatives. The availability of an undrawn credit facility further supports its financial flexibility without immediately increasing borrowing obligations.

SCIA's ongoing share repurchase program reflects its commitment to shareholder-focused capital allocation. The company continued purchasing common shares during the first half of the year, reducing its share count and supporting earnings per share. Continued repurchases, subject to management discretion and business requirements, could further benefit per-share financial metrics.

Challenges Ahead of SCIA

SCI relies heavily on a limited number of major customers, exposing revenues to potential order reductions, delays or cancellations. The absence of minimum purchase commitments further heightens uncertainty regarding future sales visibility and business stability. SCIA's gross margins remain vulnerable to elevated raw material costs and unfavorable product mix. Its ability to protect profitability depends partly on passing higher input costs to customers without adversely affecting demand or competitive positioning.

SCI Stock's Valuation

SCI's trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 1.2X is lower than the industry's average of 13.3X but is higher than its five-year median of 0.6X.

Marvell Technology and Cirrus Logic's trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 21.8X and 2.3X, respectively.

Our Final Take on SCIA

SCI's impressive stock rally reflects strengthening business fundamentals and expanding growth opportunities. Its improving order pipeline, broader manufacturing capabilities and healthy financial position provide a supportive backdrop for continued business growth. However, customer concentration and cost-related pressures remain important considerations that could influence future performance.

From a valuation perspective, SCIA appears relatively inexpensive compared with the broader industry, suggesting potential room for further appreciation. However, its premium to historical valuation levels indicates that investors are already assigning greater value to its improving business prospects. This raises expectations for future performance and leaves less room for operational disappointments.

Overall, SCIA's positive momentum could continue if the company sustains operational improvements and capitalizes on emerging opportunities. Existing shareholders may consider maintaining their positions, while prospective investors may consider waiting for a more attractive entry point, given the sharp rally and valuation premium relative to historical levels.

news.Title: Equities Bounce: 3 Top Ranked Stocks to Buy Now (TER, LRCX, ATI)
news.Content:
After a sharp bout of volatility, the stock market appears to be finding its footing ahead of a busy week of corporate earnings, central bank meetings and critical economic data.

While these selloffs can be painful, it is worth remembering just how consistently the market manages to climb the proverbial wall of worry. Whether it's concerns over AI, tariffs, elections or geopolitical tensions, the resilience of the US stock market has been remarkable.

And while it can be tempting to follow every headline and attempt to anticipate every possible scenario, investors are often better served by tuning out the noise and focusing on what matters most: buying high-quality companies at attractive valuations, particularly when earnings expectations are moving higher.

That combination of strong fundamentals, reasonable valuations and positive earnings revisions has historically been a powerful formula for long-term investment success.

With that in mind, three stocks currently stand out to me as particularly compelling opportunities. Teradyne (TER), Lam Research (LRCX) and ATI INC (ATI) are established industry leaders with impressive long-term track records, favorable earnings revision trends and exposure to powerful secular growth opportunities.

All three have delivered tremendous returns over the years, but recent market volatility has created potentially attractive entry points for investors looking to capitalize on the next leg higher.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Teradyne Stock: Exceptional Growth at a Fair Price

Teradyne is a leading provider of automated test equipment used to verify the performance and reliability of semiconductors, along with advanced robotics systems for industrial automation. The company is a major beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom, as increasingly sophisticated chips and memory components require more extensive testing.

The growth outlook is exceptional. Analysts expect sales to surge 58.9% this year, followed by another 20.9% increase next year. Meanwhile, earnings are projected to grow at an annualized rate of 54.4% over the next three to five years.

Despite that tremendous growth outlook, Teradyne trades at 33.9x forward earnings, giving it a remarkably attractive PEG ratio of just 0.62 . That suggests investors are paying a relatively modest premium for the company's anticipated earnings growth.

With a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , Teradyne offers a compelling combination of powerful secular tailwinds, explosive earnings growth and a valuation that looks increasingly reasonable following the recent pullback.

Story Continues

Lam Research Stock: A Semiconductor Powerhouse

Lam Research is one of the world's leading suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, specializing in the technologies used to deposit, etch and clean materials on silicon wafers. Its equipment is essential to producing advanced logic chips and memory, making Lam a critical supplier to the ongoing AI infrastructure expansion.

The company is particularly well positioned to benefit from the memory supercycle, as demand for high-bandwidth memory and increasingly complex chip architectures drives greater investment in semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

Analysts expect sales to grow 49.7% this year and another 19% next year, while earnings are projected to compound at an annualized rate of 28.2% over the next three to five years.

Even with that impressive growth profile, Lam trades at just 24.8x forward earnings , giving it a PEG ratio of 0.88. For a company with such an entrenched competitive position and exposure to one of the market's strongest investment themes, that valuation looks attractive.

Lam currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , reinforcing its favorable earnings outlook and making it another compelling opportunity for long-term investors.

ATI Stock: Aerospace Growth at a Compelling Valuation

ATI INC is a leading producer of high-performance specialty materials, including titanium alloys, nickel-based superalloys and advanced components used in aerospace, defense and other demanding industrial applications.

The company occupies an attractive position in the aerospace supply chain, providing critical materials used in jet engines, aircraft structures and defense systems. Rising commercial aircraft production, growing defense spending and demand for next-generation engines create a long runway for growth.

ATI's earnings outlook is particularly impressive, with analysts forecasting annualized EPS growth of 32.8% over the next three to five years.

Shares currently trade at 32.1x forward earnings, giving the stock a PEG ratio just below 1.0 . While that earnings multiple might initially appear elevated for an industrial company, the anticipated growth rate makes the valuation considerably more attractive.

ATI also carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , reflecting positive earnings estimate revisions and strengthening expectations for the business.

Should Investors Buy Shares in LRCX, ATI and TER?

Market volatility can be unsettling, but it also creates opportunities to buy exceptional businesses at more attractive prices.

Teradyne, Lam Research and ATI operate in different corners of the economy, yet all three share several important characteristics: strong competitive positions, exposure to durable secular growth trends and impressive long-term earnings prospects.

More importantly, their valuations appear reasonable relative to their projected earnings growth, with all three sporting PEG ratios below 1.0.

Of course, none is immune to a broader market correction, and those ambitious growth forecasts will need to be met. But with favorable Zacks Ranks, powerful industry tailwinds and compelling growth-adjusted valuations, TER, LRCX and ATI deserve serious consideration from investors looking to take advantage of the recent market volatility.

news.Title: Coherent vs. Arm Holdings: Which Tech Stock Offers More Upside Now?
news.Content:
Both Coherent Corp. COHR and Arm Holdings ARM are technology companies whose business models focus heavily on advanced hardware and innovation at the core of modern computing.

ARM is best known for its semiconductor IP, providing chip architectures that power a vast share of smartphones, servers and increasingly AI-focused processors. COHR, on the other hand, operates in the realm of photonics, lasers and optical components, enabling the ultra-fast connectivity and precision manufacturing that form the backbone of today's data and electronics industries.

The two companies compete for investor interest in high-growth, innovation-driven segments of the tech infrastructure ecosystem.

COHR's Case

The AI opportunity extends well beyond the construction of new data centers. Existing facilities must continually upgrade as newer GPUs, switches and networking platforms require greater bandwidth. As AI clusters expand, more connections are needed among processors, racks, switches and facilities, increasing the importance of high-speed optical networking.

This trend plays directly into Coherent's strengths. Its portfolio includes indium phosphide lasers, VCSELs, silicon photonics, specialty fiber, detectors and micro-optics. That broad technological base gives the company multiple ways to benefit as data-center operators shift toward faster, denser and more power-efficient network architectures.

Continued improvements in AI models, falling inference costs and broader commercial adoption could further stimulate computing requirements. As AI becomes embedded in more applications, network capacity should become increasingly critical alongside computing power.

PhotonLink could strengthen Coherent's position by moving the company further beyond individual components and into integrated optical subsystems. Combining internally developed technologies with integration, assembly and testing capabilities enables Coherent to capture a greater portion of the value created within an AI system.

This approach could also deepen customer relationships. Replacing a single component supplier is generally simpler than switching a provider whose subsystem has been designed and qualified within a broader architecture.

Coherent is also positioned across multiple technology pathways, including conventional pluggable optics, co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics and chip-to-chip connectivity. This diversified exposure reduces dependence on any single optical architecture becoming the dominant industry standard.

Story Continues

ARM's Case

The accelerating pace of AI infrastructure development presents a significant opportunity for Arm. Technology companies are committing substantial resources to build data centers, develop advanced processors and expand computing capacity to support increasingly sophisticated AI applications.

AI developer Anthropic's ambitious infrastructure spending plans underscore the massive investments required to support next-generation AI models. Meanwhile, major cloud providers, including Alphabet GOOG and Microsoft MSFT, continue investing heavily in AI infrastructure and computing technologies. These investments should support sustained demand for advanced semiconductor architectures.

Arm Holdings stands to benefit from this transition through its energy-efficient processor designs, which are increasingly relevant to cloud computing, AI inference and edge applications. As computing workloads become more demanding, the need for processors capable of delivering higher performance without excessive power consumption should strengthen the company's market opportunities.

Additionally, the growing adoption of Arm-based architectures across data centers could diversify its revenue sources beyond smartphones, supporting a more balanced long-term growth profile.

The emergence of autonomous AI agents is creating additional opportunities for central processing units (CPUs). Unlike conventional AI applications primarily focused on model training, agentic systems require considerable general-purpose processing capabilities to coordinate tasks, manage workflows and execute instructions.

This development could accelerate demand for energy-efficient CPUs alongside specialized AI accelerators. Arm Holdings' expanding processor portfolio positions it to capture opportunities as enterprises deploy more sophisticated AI systems across cloud environments.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for COHR & ARM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for COHR's fiscal 2027 sales and EPS indicates year-over-year growth of 50% and 68%, respectively. EPS estimates have been trending flat over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ARM's current-year sales suggests 22% year-over-year growth, while EPS is expected to grow 24%. EPS estimates have been trending flat over the past 60 days.

COHR's Valuation Reflects Strong Growth Potential

While COHR appears attractively valued with a forward 12-month P/E of 20.34X versus its median of 39.95X, ARM's higher forward P/E of 82.79X, below its median of 145.78X, reflects investor confidence in its strong earnings growth potential.

Coherent Stands Out as the Better Placed

Coherent appears better positioned than Arm Holdings, supported by its accelerating exposure to AI-driven optical networking demand, diversified photonics portfolio and expanding opportunities in integrated optical subsystems. Growing investments in AI infrastructure and increasing demand for high-speed connectivity should strengthen Coherent's long-term growth prospects. Although Arm benefits from rising adoption of energy-efficient processors across data centers and AI applications, its elevated valuation leaves less room for potential disappointments. Coherent's stronger projected earnings and revenue growth, coupled with its relatively attractive valuation, gives it an edge.

COHR and ARM currently carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) each. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Arm vs. Western Digital: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy in November?
news.Content:
The surge in artificial intelligence (AI) has forced investors to choose between infrastructure providers. Choosing between Arm (NASDAQ:ARM) and Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) involves weighing architectural licensing against physical data storage solutions.

Arm provides the blueprints for power-efficient processors found in nearly every smartphone and increasingly in data centers. Western Digital manufactures the physical hardware used to store vast amounts of digital information. While both benefit from rising compute demands, they operate at opposite ends of the hardware stack with very different financial profiles.

The case for Arm

Arm designs and licenses processor architecture and software to a wide range of partners among semiconductor stocks . The company targets several high-growth markets including mobile devices, automotive systems, and cloud-based artificial intelligence. While its technology powers billions of devices, Arm does not disclose specific major customers in its regulatory filings.

Through the July 2026 quarter, trailing 12-month (TTM) revenue reached nearly $5.2 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 25% over the previous year. The company reported net income of roughly $1 billion for the period. This resulted in a net margin of close to 20%.

As of its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1x. This metric measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, suggesting the company uses very little borrowed money. The current ratio, a liquidity measure indicating whether a company can cover short-term obligations, was nearly 5.3x.

TTM free cash flow, calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, reached approximately $1.5 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 69% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow.

The case for Western Digital

Western Digital specializes in hard disk drive technology and data storage solutions for cloud providers and retail consumers. The cloud end market is the most critical segment for the business, accounting for nearly 89% of net revenue as of its latest annual report filed in 2026. Customer concentration is a significant factor, as the top ten customers account for roughly 73% of net revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

TTM revenue through the October quarter reached nearly $14.5 billion, a substantial increase of approximately 43% from the prior year. The company reported net income of $10 billion during this period. This led to a net margin of approximately 69%, representing a sharp increase from previous fiscal years.

Story Continues

Based on its October 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.1x. The current ratio stood at approximately 1.4x, suggesting the company maintains enough short-term assets to cover its immediate debts.

TTMF free cash flow reached approximately $4.3 billion for the fiscal year.

Risk profile comparison

Arm faces competition from alternative architectures, such as the open-source RISC-V standard. Because the company relies on licensing its intellectual property, any shift in designer preferences could impact its long-term royalty revenue. Additionally, the business remains sensitive to the cyclical nature of the global smartphone and consumer electronics markets.

Western Digital deals with high revenue concentration, making it vulnerable to demand shifts from a small number of cloud customers. The company relies on a limited number of single-source suppliers for critical components, which creates potential supply chain disruptions. Furthermore, failing to transition successfully to new storage technologies like Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR) could hurt its competitive position.

Valuation comparison

Western Digital appears to be the more value-oriented choice because its Forward P/E , which compares price to future earnings estimates, is significantly lower than Arm's.

The P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy right now?

Western Digital is growing at a higher rate, benefiting from a strong AI-driven demand cycle. But it basically sells a commodity product that can cause sharp swings in selling prices, which can weigh on financials. I would buy and hold Arm for its more consistent operating history and opportunities to gain share in the data center market.

Agentic AI runs on CPUs, which could drive significant growth for Arm. Importantly, Arm doesn't manufacture chips. It designs them and then profits from royalties and licensing fees on every chip shipped using its chip architecture. That's an attractive business model and is why the stock generally gets rated at a high P/E.

Arm's revenue has grown at a compound annual rate of 25% over the past three years. CEO Rene Haas mentioned on the July 2026 earnings call that the addressable market for CPUs was estimated at $100 billion earlier in 2026 but could now be approaching $200 billion.

Overall, I would rather pay up for a more consistent business that generates profits from licensing fees, which is why I would rather buy Arm today to hold for the long term.

news.Title: Texas Instruments (TXN) Recently Broke Out Above the 20-Day Moving Average
news.Content:
Texas Instruments (TXN) reached a significant support level, and could be a good pick for investors from a technical perspective. Recently, TXN broke through the 20-day moving average, which suggests a short-term bullish trend.

The 20-day simple moving average is a well-liked trading tool because it provides a look back at a stock's price over a 20-day period. Additionally, short-term traders find this SMA very beneficial, as it smooths out short-term price trends and shows more trend reversal signals than longer-term moving averages.

Like other SMAs, if a stock's price is moving above the 20-day, the trend is considered positive. When the price falls below the moving average, it can signal a downward trend.

Shares of TXN have been moving higher over the past four weeks, up 7.1%. Plus, the company is currently a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stock, suggesting that TXN could be poised for a continued surge.

The bullish case only gets stronger once investors take into account TXN's positive earnings estimate revisions. There have been 9 revisions higher for the current fiscal year compared to none lower, and the consensus estimate has moved up as well.

With a winning combination of earnings estimate revisions and hitting a key technical level, investors should keep their eye on TXN for more gains in the near future.

news.Title: Investors Heavily Search Texas Instruments Incorporated (TXN): Here is What You Need to Know
news.Content:
Texas Instruments (TXN) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Shares of this chipmaker have returned +7.1% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -0.8% change. The Zacks Semiconductor - General industry, to which Texas Instruments belongs, has lost 5.9% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Texas Instruments is expected to post earnings of $2.53 per share, indicating a change of +99.2% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +19.6% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $8.85 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +62.4%. This estimate has changed +5.1% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $11.03 indicates a change of +24.7% from what Texas Instruments is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +12.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for Texas Instruments.

Story Continues

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Texas Instruments, the consensus sales estimate of $6.09 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +37.7%. The $22.26 billion and $25.62 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +25.9% and +15.1%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Texas Instruments reported revenues of $6.06 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +27.7%. EPS of $2.62 for the same period compares with $1.48 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.93 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +2.17%. The EPS surprise was +9.17%.

Over the last four quarters, Texas Instruments surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Texas Instruments is graded F on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Texas Instruments. However, its Zacks Rank #1 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Here's How Much a $1000 Investment in Texas Instruments Made 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
news.Content:
How much a stock's price changes over time is important for most investors, since price performance can both impact your investment portfolio and help you compare investment results across sectors and industries.

The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Texas Instruments (TXN) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to TXN for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Texas Instruments' Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Texas Instruments' main business drivers.

Headquartered in Dallas, TX, Texas Instruments Incorporated is an original equipment manufacturer of analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits.

Texas Instruments has manufacturing and design facilities, including wafer fabrication and assembly/test operations in North America, Asia and Europe.

Management's strategy has been to build assets that would be fully utilized through their lifetimes and outsource any excess demand in peak situations to outside foundries.

In 2025, Texas Instruments generated total revenues of $17.68 billion, up 13% from 2024. The company has two reporting financial segments, Analog and Embedded Processing. It reports the results of its remaining business activities in Other.

Analog segment revenues grew 15% to $14.01 billion and accounted for approximately 79% of total revenues in 2025. Analog products have been categorized into two categories, Power and Signal Chain. Power products manage and distribute electricity, while Signal Chain products sense, condition and convert real-world signals.

Revenues from the Embedded Processing segment rose 6% to $2.70 billion and contributed approximately 15% to 2025 total revenues. This segment includes microcontrollers, processors, wireless connectivity and radar products.

The Other business generated $979 million in revenues and accounted for approximately 6% of 2025 total sales. The segment includes smaller product lines, such as DLP products, calculators and certain application-specific integrated circuits. Revenues from this segment increased 3% in 2025.

The company's products are sold in industrial, personal electronics, automotive, data center and communications equipment markets. In 2025, industrial and automotive each represented 33% of revenue. Personal electronics accounted for 21%, data center 9% and communications equipment 3%. Calculators represented about 1% of revenue.

Texas Instruments has more than 80,000 products and over 100,000 customers. In 2025, more than 80% of revenue was generated through direct sales channels.

Story Continues

Bottom Line

Anyone can invest, but building a successful investment portfolio requires research, patience, and a little bit of risk. So, if you had invested in Texas Instruments, ten years ago, you're likely feeling pretty good about your investment today.

According to our calculations, a $1000 investment made in October 2016 would be worth $4,157.30, or a gain of 315.73%, as of October 27, 2026, and this return excludes dividends but includes price increases.

Compare this to the S&P 500's rally of 258.82% and gold's return of 203.96% over the same time frame.

Analysts are anticipating more upside for TXN.

Texas Instruments is benefiting from a broad recovery in industrial and automotive demand and sustained data center expansion. Its analog and embedded portfolios serve diverse, long-lived applications. Internal manufacturing and growing capacity strengthen supply reliability while supporting margin recovery as utilization rises. Rising cash generation provides greater room for dividends and long-term investment. The planned Silicon Labs acquisition could extend its wireless connectivity reach. Management's outlook points to continued demand across its core markets. Semiconductor cyclicality, pricing competition, trade exposure and debt remain risks. Equipment delivery constraints could also slow capacity additions. Nonetheless, improving factory economics and a wider range of growth opportunities support an Outperform view.

The stock is up 7.12% over the past four weeks, and no earnings estimate has gone lower in the past two months, compared to 9 higher, for fiscal 2026. The consensus estimate has moved up as well.

news.Title: 智原Q4營收估季持平；明年三大產品線齊向上
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-27 16:42:18 黃立安 發佈

ASIC設計服務暨矽智財(IP)廠智原(3035)今(27)日舉行法說會，總經理王國雍表示，今(2026)年第四季IP業績可望續創高，NRE業務也將顯著成長，不過量產業務可能下滑，整體單季營收將較第三季的36.6億元約略持平，毛利率則回升至45%。2027年營收將成長兩位數，包括IP、NRE和量產三大產品線均可望同步向上。此外，近期先進製程成功接下美國客戶2奈米雲端AI應用專案，總金額高達數千萬美元，成為智原史上最大規模專案。

針對該2奈米專案，王國雍表示，此為首個2奈米環繞閘極(GAA)製程專案，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，但考量到產品生命週期，決定改採2奈米製程，且專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第一筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，此案是智原史上最大金額的專案，將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電(2303)及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

王國雍指出，此項AI專案對公司深具指標性意義，並於四個面向均創下公司紀錄-設計製程、設計複雜度、NRE金額規模及高階封裝技術，同時此除證明客戶對公司設計能力的肯定及信賴，亦為後續先進製程及高階封裝接單及推廣建立了重要的指標性案例。

回顧第三季表現，智原在量產業務帶動下，單季營收達36.6億元，不僅優於原先預期，更逆勢季增11%、年增13%；毛利率42.5%，季減2.7個百分點、年增9.3個百分點；營業利益為2.1億元，季減21%，雖較第二季小幅回落，但受到營收規模擴大及毛利結構改善，年增達443%；營業利益率5.8%；稅後淨利2.8億元，季增41%，年增84%，EPS為1.07元。

智原2026年第三季營運創下多項紀錄，包括IP營收創歷史新高，量產及單季合併營收雙雙寫下歷年同期新高。

以產品別來看，IP營收4.5億元，季增4%，年增8%，創下歷史新高；NRE收入為3.1億元，季減31%，年減37%；量產營收則為第三季季主要成長動能，不僅MCU相關營收再創單季新高，ASIC量產在AI相關高階封裝專案出貨動能加速下，亦同步走揚，推升量產營收季增20%，年增25%，達29.1億元，創下歷年同期高點。

news.Title: 智原第三季每股賺1.07元，成功搶下2奈米AI專案明年上半年開始入帳
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】智原(3035)今日召開法說會，公布第三季成績單，單季本業部分，量產業務大增，業外收益也同時進補，帶動單季每股淨利1.07元，展望第四季，估營收與前季持平，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑，至於第四季毛利率估為45%。產線斬獲部分，獲得國際客戶開案，採用2奈米GAA製程，承接瞄準雲端AI應用之大型專案，預計2027年上半年會開始有收益。智原第三季受惠量產業務大幅成長，單季合併營收達36.64億元，季增10.6%、年增13.2%；營收中，IP營收4.48億元，季增3.5%、年增8.4%；NRE營收3.09億元，季減31.3%、年減37.1%；量產業務營收則達29.07億元，季增19.6%、年增24.7%，成為推升整體營收成長的主要動能。

獲利方面，智原第三季營業毛利15.57億元，季增3.9%、年增44.9%；毛利率42.5%，雖低於第二季的45.2%，但仍明顯高於去年同期的33.2%。第三季營業利益率為5.8%，低於第二季的8.2%，但優於去年同期的1.3%。但智原第三季業外收入達到2.66億元，季增138.8%、年增53.2%，主因業外轉投資評價利益挹注，挹注第三季本期淨利增至3.69億元，季增29.2%、年增124.1%。第三季歸屬母公司業主稅後淨利為2.79億元，季增40.8%、年增83.8%，單季每股淨利1.07元，。

展望第四季，公司自估，營收與第三季相比，大致約持平，毛利率估為45%。產線方面，IP持續成長創新高，NRE顯著成長，量產業務下滑。至於在產品線的斬獲部分，智原總經理王國雍透露，藉由和聯電(2303)、三星，以及記憶體廠等廠商的合作，公司已經獲得總金額數千萬美元、美系業者的2奈米AI雲端專案訂單。而整體2027年，智原看法樂觀，營收會年增雙位數百分比，三大產線都會年增。

news.Title: 智原攜手三星、聯電　搶下美國2奈米雲端AI專案訂單
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年10月27日電）特殊應用晶片廠智原 (3035) 總經理王國雍今天表示，透過與三星（Samsung）、聯電 (2303) 和記憶體廠等夥伴合作，成功搶下美國廠商2奈米雲端人工智慧（AI）專案訂單，總金額高達數千萬美元，是智原史上最大規模專案。

智原今天召開線上法人說明會，王國雍說，智原客戶委託設計（NRE）業務在先進製程有新斬獲，成功搶下2奈米環繞閘極（GAA）製程雲端AI專案訂單，這對智原意義重大，是最先進的製程，也是第1個2奈米GAA製程專案，複雜度也最高。

王國雍表示，原本客戶計劃採用4奈米製程，基於延長產品生命週期考量，決定改採2奈米製程；這專案總金額達數千萬美元，預計2027年上半年將有第1筆收入入帳，後續依進度認列，是智原史上最大金額的專案。

王國雍說，智原具備設計以及統籌協調能力，是能夠搶下2奈米專案的關鍵，此案將採用三星的晶圓代工，另外還與聯電及記憶體廠等夥伴合作。

智原第3季受惠量產業務優於預期，加上矽智財（IP）業績創下歷史新高，整體第3季營收攀高至新台幣36.64億元，季增10.6%，為歷年同期新高。

受產品組合變化影響，低毛利的量產業務比重攀升，智原第3季毛利率42.5%，較第2季下滑2.7個百分點，營業利益2.14億元，季減20.8%，受惠業外轉投資評價利益挹注，智原第3季歸屬母公司淨利2.79億元，季增40.8%，每股純益1.07元。

展望未來，智原預期，第4季IP業績可望持續成長創高，NRE業務將顯著成長，量產業務可能下滑，整體第4季營收將較第3季持平，毛利率約45%。

王國雍表示，2027年營收將成長2位數，包括IP、NRE和量產3大產品線2027年營收可望同步成長。

news.Title: KLA Corporation (KLAC) vs. AMAT and LRCX: Can Rising Semiconductor Complexity Create Another Growth Cycle?
news.Content:
Is KLAC a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on KLA Corporation on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on KLAC. KLA Corporation's share was trading at $145.61 as of October 23rd 2026. KLAC's trailing and forward P/E were 39.78 and 26.95 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a semiconductor equipment company pitched as a great investment. KLAC shares gained 19.83% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Applied Materials and Lam Research gained 63.07% and 46.65%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor equipment stocks rising, and does KLAC's recent weakness make this a good time to buy?

Posonskyi Andrey/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire Dan Loeb and KLAC ranked #8 in that article. KLAC has declined since then, leaving investors who backed the stock waiting for that confidence to translate into returns. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on KLAC. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) provides tools that help chip makers find defects, measure wafer quality, and run their factories more efficiently. Its fastest-growing opportunity right now is tied to artificial intelligence-driven semiconductor demand, and that is central to understanding the stock. As chips become smaller and more complex, manufacturers need more advanced inspection and measurement tools to keep production yields high, which is exactly where KLA Corporation operates.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

In fiscal 2026, the company's revenue reached $13.6 billion, up 11.7% from a year earlier, and it kept very healthy profit margins. These are strong results, but the stock is not cheap, as it trades at about 49 times trailing earnings and 33 times forward earnings. This suggests investors are paying not just for today's performance, but also for several more years of AI-related growth.

The positive case rests on KLA Corporation being a leader in process control, meaning the tools that catch problems during chip making. Every new generation of advanced chips needs more inspection and measurement, and even tiny defects can hurt production yields. As AI pushes chip makers to expand capacity and invest in newer manufacturing technology, demand for KLA Corporation systems should benefit. The company also enjoys long relationships with leading chip makers, who find it costly and difficult to switch suppliers. Growth in advanced packaging and AI-related chip investment could support the business for years.

Story Continues

The company's recent results support this view. KLA Corporation turned a large share of its sales into real cash, generating $4.14 billion in operating cash flow and $3.8 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026. Its 35.6% net margin and 76.1% return on equity show how efficiently it makes money for shareholders. Fourth-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion also came in above the midpoint of management's guidance, showing steady execution even in a choppy industry. If AI-driven chip spending continues and manufacturers keep adding advanced capacity, bulls believe the company can keep growing earnings and justify its premium price.

Analysts are also fairly upbeat. Their average price target of about $233.77 implies nearly 29% upside from the current price of roughly $180.64, with individual targets ranging from $175 to $325. This bullish outlook depends on continued AI-related chip investment, strength in advanced packaging, and stable margins. However, because the stock already carries a high valuation, slower earnings growth or weaker chip spending could make that price harder to defend. You can check out why Jim Cramer recommends buying KLA stock in small doses here .

A slowdown in chip industry spending is the main risk. Even if AI demand stays strong, semiconductor equipment is a cyclical business that depends on customers' investment decisions. Wider U.S. export limits on selling chip equipment to China add another challenge, since China has historically been a meaningful source of revenue for KLA Corporation. With a premium valuation and little room for error, the stock could come under pressure if growth slows, margins shrink, or geopolitical restrictions tighten.

Another risk for the stock is that rising chip complexity makes KLA's own product development harder and more expensive. Each new manufacturing process requires inspection tools that can detect smaller defects accurately without slowing production. KLA warns that its success depends on anticipating customer needs and launching new technologies on time and at competitive costs. Existing customer relationships cannot guarantee it wins every new equipment purchase. A delayed launch or a better competing tool could cost it business even while AI investment remains strong. Higher development spending could also pressure margins before new products generate revenue. In our opinion, this execution risk could pressure KLA's valuation if growing inspection demand fails to translate into sustained earnings growth.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 81 hedge fund portfolios held KLA Corporation at the end of the second quarter, up from 71 in the previous quarter. That is a steady climb, suggesting institutional interest in the company is improving. Among its peers, Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) was held by 137 hedge funds, down from 138, while Onto Innovation (NASDAQ:ONTO) was held by 75 hedge funds, up from 67, and Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) was held by 139 hedge funds, up from 123. This shows institutional investors grew most confident in Lam Research Corporation during the quarter, with KLA Corporation and Onto Innovation also seeing solid gains, while Applied Materials held roughly steady with only a marginal dip in ownership.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture, with just 1.86% of KLA Corporation shares sold short. That compares with 1.71% for Applied Materials, Inc., 2.07% for Lam Research Corporation, and a much higher 7.68% for Onto Innovation Inc. Because fewer investors are betting against KLA Corporation than Onto Innovation Inc., there is little direct bearish pressure on the stock. Still, its premium valuation and reliance on continued chip spending remain the key things to watch.

Valuation Analysis

KLAC's forward P/E is 26.95x. Applied Materials, Inc., Lam Research Corporation, and Onto Innovation Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 21.14x, 24.88x, and 16.84x, respectively. KLAC's own forward P/E was 33.44x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 19% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about semiconductor spending cycles, export restrictions, and the durability of AI-driven equipment demand. However, its premium to all three peers suggests that the historical decline has reduced expectations without making the shares an obvious bargain. KLA's fiscal 2026 revenue increased 11.7% to $13.6 billion, while fourth-quarter adjusted earnings per share rose approximately 12% from $0.94 to $1.05, supported by annual free cash flow of $3.77 billion. We believe continued earnings growth could support the current valuation, but a narrowing premium would reduce shareholder returns even if profits keep rising. If KLA can convert increasing chip complexity and advanced packaging demand into sustained earnings and cash flow growth, the shares could offer attractive long-term returns, although we would prefer a lower entry price to provide more protection against a slower semiconductor spending cycle.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on KLA Corporation (KLAC) by Quality Equities in January 2025, which highlighted semiconductor tailwinds, TSMC's capex expansion, and AI-driven demand for KLA's process control tools. KLAC's stock price has appreciated by approximately 94.19% since our coverage. We believe KLAC could be a good long-term investment at a lower price, as its premium valuation could limit returns even if earnings continue growing, particularly if semiconductor spending slows.

KLA Corporation is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While KLAC could benefit from growing demand for advanced chip inspection and packaging tools, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than KLAC that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .

news.Title: Nvidia Just Gave a Huge Catalyst to This AI Stock. How to Play AMBA Stock Here.
news.Content:
An American fabless semiconductor company, Ambarella (AMBA), suddenly becomes the most interesting stock in edge AI. On Oct. 21, a post from Betaville suggested Nvidia (NVDA) could be the third party to buy the edge-AI chipmaker, after NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) and Qualcomm (QCOM).

The company was said to be getting the same advice from Goldman Sachs, which was also reportedly looking at a potential sale, but there has been no official bid, price, or deal announced.

More News from Barchart

How to Play RKLB Stock as Rocket Lab Pushes Its Neutron Launch to Next Year

Morgan Stanley Sees Amazon Stock Surging 100% with AWS Hitting $1 Trillion in Revenue Sooner Than People Think

Dell, Lenovo, Cisco, HPE, Supermicro: Why AMD's New AI Blueprint Has Everyone Signing On

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

The impression of strategic logic appears to be correct: Ambarella offers low-power processors that, for example, analyze video and operate AI in cars, cameras, or robotics applications, while Nvidia would appear to be the leader in AI computing in data centers.

The acquisition of Ambarella could expand Nvidia's reach in physical AI and edge computing. Now unless a serious offer materializes, or if the talks go stale, those rumored gains could disappear just as fast as they came.

While investors might be tempted to be drawn into a possible bid, a more important question is whether Ambarella can generate yet more revenue and cash flow to support this valuation without being simply taken over.

A Rough Year for AMBA Stock

AMBA stock is down 6% year-to-date (YTD) in 2026, and it is down roughly 31% from its 2026 high. The stock rallied about 8% in late October on the Nvidia rumor, but that pop did not erase the earlier losses.

The negative catalysts were slow X7 adoption and margin pressure from rising memory costs. The positive catalyst is the buyout interest from three credible suitors. Without the M&A bid, the stock would likely be much lower.

Turning to valuation, Ambarella trades at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 6x. That is below its own historical median of 8x and below the semiconductor industry median. The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 81.97. That looks expensive. But it reflects a depressed earnings base. On sales, the stock looks fairly valued on the slightly cheap side. On earnings, it is expensive. The market is pricing in a lot of future growth.

Story Continues

Why Nvidia Makes Sense as a Suitor

So the chip giant Nvidia is reportedly interested in the acquisition of Ambarella, with Goldman Sachs on board for the deal. Ambarella is the tech company that specializes in low-power AI chips for cameras, cars, and robots. That's the tangible aspect of AI. Currently, AI training in the data center is dominated by Nvidia. By acquiring Ambarella, Nvidia will gain a better position in the field of AI inference in actual devices.

Being the third bidder in the process, and the one with the largest purse, also increases the chances of getting a better deal. Theoretically, it is a good strategy. However, it is all still just a rumor. Traders are betting on a maybe and not something even remotely set in stone. This is why AMBA stock is still trading well below its YTD level despite the rally.

After that is the newest big move: the launch of the X7 AI accelerator. Ambarella announced the X7 on Sept. 15, 2026. It is designed for edge infrastructure and is extremely power-efficient and memory-consuming. It's also entered into seven-year distribution deals with Macnica and Capgemini (CGEMY). The opportunity from those deals would drive up to $500 million in incremental revenue over seven years. The moves illustrate that Ambarella has a larger enterprise going on the buyout side. The distribution deals expand the moat.

Q2 Was a Record Quarter

Ambarella's fiscal second quarter of 2027 reported solid growth due to higher demand for its edge AI chips in the automotive and Internet of Things (IoT) segment.

Revenue increased by 13% over the prior-year figure to $108.1 million and above management's guidance as well. Solid sales of commercial vehicles and edge artificial intelligence revenue helped handily. The enterprise IoT segment also performed better than the consumer-focused segments.

Profitability went up as well. Ambarella registered a net loss of $6.7 million, compared to a $20 million loss a year ago. Adjusted net income was $8.2 million, or $0.18 per share, in the current quarter compared to $8,200,000, or $0.15 per share, for the same quarter last year.

But the free cash flow was negative at $7.1 million. At the end of the quarter, the company had $272.3 million in cash and marketable securities for financial flexibility as the company started to invest in new products.

CEO Fermi Wang was upbeat. "Our edge AI revenue reached record levels in Q2, with balanced sequential growth in Auto and IoT markets," he said. He also highlighted the X7 launch and the new distribution deals.

For the coming fiscal 3Q results, Ambarella is forecasting $115 million to $124 million in revenue and gross margins from 59% to 60%. Analysts are estimating fiscal 2027 revenue at about $440.6 million and adjusted earnings per share at a loss of $1.12, so higher revenue can be expected if sales demand continues.

Wall Street Is Split on AMBA Stock

Wall Street opinion towards AMBA stock is generally mixed but leaning positive. Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore has a "Buy" rating and a $96 price target. Roth Capital cut its target to $65 with a "Neutral" rating. Bank of America lowered its target to $70 with a "Neutral" rating.

The consensus rating among 13 analysts is "Moderate Buy." The mean price target is nearly $90, implying about 35% upside from the current price.

Summing it all up. I think the stock is considered binary risk. A buyout may result in a premium. In the absence of an agreement, the stock may revert to a loss-making estimate. As one analyst said, "…there is a two-way risk for investors here, either a premium on the deal, or the valuation hitting loss warrant levels." This is the debate in a nutshell.

Currently, the only thing that's seriously driving AMBA stock is the buyout chatter. However, the core business is improving. The investors who purchase AMBA are now hoping there will be a deal. They are also taking a keen bet on the edge AI story continuing to go up. Either wager is a winner. Neither is guaranteed.

news.Title: Advanced Energy vs. KLA: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy?
news.Content:
Advanced Energy Industries AEIS and KLA KLAC both serve the semiconductor manufacturing equipment market. AEIS specializes in precision power solutions for semiconductor equipment, while KLA provides advanced process control and inspection solutions that help manufacturers produce increasingly complex semiconductors for AI data centers and applications. Both companies benefit from growing demand for increasingly complex semiconductors used in AI data centers and other advanced computing applications.

So, AEIS or KLAC — Which of these semiconductor stocks has the greater upside potential? Let's find out.

The Case For AEIS Stock

Advanced Energy is benefiting from robust demand for semiconductor equipment, driven by increasing investments in leading-edge memory and logic technologies. Rising etch and deposition intensity, coupled with growing complexity in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, is boosting demand for the company's precision power solutions. In the second quarter of 2026, semiconductor revenues jumped 33% year over year to a record $278 million.

The company's next-generation eVerest and eVoS plasma power platforms are gaining traction, delivering improved yield and throughput for advanced manufacturing processes. Design wins in semiconductor testing, atomic layer deposition, and thermal sensing further strengthen its competitive position. The company expects semiconductor revenues to grow nearly 50% year over year in the second half of 2026, and believes new product adoption can support market share gains into 2027 and beyond.

AEIS's strong semiconductor revenue growth, expanding product portfolio, and improving manufacturing capabilities are expected to boost top-line growth. For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million.

The Case for KLAC Stock

KLA is benefiting from strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory, and advanced packaging. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues reached a record $3.66 billion, increasing 15% year over year and 7% sequentially. Management attributed the performance to rising AI infrastructure investments and greater process-control intensity across memory and advanced packaging.

Advanced packaging provides another significant growth opportunity. KLA now expects advanced packaging process-control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year and exceeding its previous expectation of high-50% growth. Meanwhile, Specialty Process, PCB and Component Inspection businesses are expected to grow more than 25% in calendar year 2026, supported by high-performance computing and greater package complexity.

The broader semiconductor equipment environment also remains favorable. KLA raised its calendar year 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market estimate, including advanced packaging, to the low-$150-billion range from its previous expectation of more than $140 billion. Broad-based investment across leading-edge logic, foundry, DRAM, HBM, NAND and advanced packaging is expected to sustain capacity expansion. KLA expects second-half 2026 revenues to increase roughly 20% from the first half.

Story Continues

Price Performance and Valuation of AEIS and KLAC

In the year-to-date period, shares of AEIS and KLAC have rallied 3.5% and 19.8%, respectively. The outperformance in KLAC can be attributed to strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory, and advanced packaging.

Despite AEIS expanding its portfolio, the company faces customer concentration, inventory and capex execution risks, tariffs, currency swings and convertible debt complexity.

Valuation-wise, AEIS and KLA shares are currently overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of D.

On a forward 12-month price-to-sales basis, AEIS shares trade at 2.99X, lower than KLA's 10.02X.

AEIS and KLAC Valuation

How Do Earnings Estimates Compare for AEIS & KLAC?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AEIS's 2026 earnings is pegged at $3.06 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This indicates a 75.86% increase year over year.

KLA Corporation Price and Consensus

KLA Corporation price-consensus-chart | KLA Corporation Quote

Conclusion

While both AEIS and KLAC are well-positioned to benefit from rising semiconductor and AI infrastructure investments, KLAC appears better positioned for long-term growth, supported by its leadership in process control, expanding advanced packaging opportunities, and stronger stock performance.

However, AEIS faces headwinds from customer concentration, tariff uncertainty, currency fluctuations, and execution risks tied to manufacturing expansion, which could weigh on its growth prospects.

news.Title: FormFactor Stock Before Q3 Earnings: Smart Buy or Risky Move?
news.Content:
FormFactor FORM is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28.

The company expects third-quarter 2026 earnings to be 86 cents (+/- 9 cents) per share. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 earnings has remained steady at 86 cents per share over the past 30 days, suggesting 160.6% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

FormFactor expects third-quarter 2026 revenues to be $270 million (+/- $10 million). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter revenues is pegged at $270.6 million, indicating an increase of 33.5% from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Consensus Estimate Trend

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

FormFactor's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 30.58%.

FormFactor, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

FormFactor, Inc. price-eps-surprise | FormFactor, Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up for the upcoming announcement.

Factors to Drive FORM's Q3 Results

FormFactor's third-quarter 2026 top-line growth is expected to have benefited from strong foundry and logic demand, sustained DRAM activity and growing co-packaged optics (CPO) adoption. Accelerating demand for advanced probe cards used in data center CPUs, networking processors and custom AI accelerators is expected to have driven top-line growth. Increasing compute intensity associated with agentic AI workloads has been driving demand for high-performance CPUs and sophisticated semiconductor testing solutions.

FormFactor's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from sustained DRAM probe card demand, particularly for DDR5 applications. Strong memory pricing and constrained supply have encouraged DRAM manufacturers to shift wafer production toward DDR products to capitalize on higher profitability. Although FORM anticipated a product-mix shift away from high-bandwidth memory (HBM), overall DRAM probe card revenues were expected to remain near the record second-quarter level of $85 million.

FORM's expanding relationships with leading compute providers, combined with multiple design wins at a major fabless XPU customer, are likely to have supported top-line growth in the to-be-reported quarter. Growing testing complexity for DRAM and the company's established relationships with major memory manufacturers are likely to have supported revenues in the third quarter of 2026. Increasing semiconductor manufacturing activity in Taiwan, particularly in advanced logic, GPU and custom ASIC applications, is also expected to have benefited FORM's top-line growth.

Moreover, strong demand for CPO testing solutions is expected to have driven FormFactor's third-quarter Systems segment revenues. Increasing deployment of optical interconnect technologies in AI data centers is driving demand for advanced silicon photonics testing equipment. FormFactor's leadership in early-stage photonic integrated circuit wafer testing and increasing adoption of its Triton high-volume manufacturing platform have been significant growth drivers. The company previously expected CPO revenues of $10 million to $20 million in 2026 but subsequently projected that revenues would exceed $20 million by the end of the third quarter.

FormFactor's third-quarter profitability is expected to have benefited from improved manufacturing yields, shorter production cycle times and disciplined operating spending. The company has strengthened its cost structure while increasing output from existing facilities. FORM also anticipated approximately $7-$9 million of tariff refunds during the third quarter, providing a temporary benefit of roughly 300 basis points to gross margin. However, unfavorable DRAM product mix could have partially offset these gains in the to-be-reported quarter. FormFactor continues to face manufacturing capacity constraints as demand accelerates across advanced semiconductor testing applications.

Story Continues

FORM Shares Beat Sector, Valuation Stretched

FormFactor shares have appreciated 76.6% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 14%.

FORM has underperformed Cohu COHU but outperformed Teradyne TER and KLA KLAC, YTD. While Cohu shares have jumped 106.1%, Teradyne and KLA shares have appreciated 59.5% and 19.8%, respectively, over the same time frame.

FORM Stock's Price Performance

FORM stock is overvalued, as suggested by the Value Score of F. In terms of the forward 12-month price-to-sales (P/S), the company is trading at 6.54X compared with the broader sector's 5.47X. Shares of Cohu, Teradyne and KLA trade at 3.84X, 10.86X and 15.71X, respectively.

FORM Stock's Valuation

AI Infrastructure & Advanced Packaging Aids FORM's Prospects

FormFactor is benefiting from increasing investments in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging. The adoption of chiplet architectures in GPUs, CPUs and custom accelerators is significantly increasing semiconductor testing requirements. Each chiplet must undergo extensive testing before integration into advanced packages, creating additional demand for high-performance probe cards. The company's differentiated microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology enables testing at higher speeds, currents and temperatures.

Growing adoption of HBM4 and future HBM generations in AI accelerators is a tailwind. FORM's SmartMatrix full-wafer contactor technology enables simultaneous high-speed testing of hundreds of HBM stacks, improving throughput and manufacturing efficiency. The company is well-positioned to capitalize on increasing adoption of custom AI accelerators and next-generation GPUs. Rising power consumption, operating temperatures and testing complexity are encouraging customers to transition from conventional wire-based probe cards to advanced MEMS technologies. FormFactor has indicated that custom ASIC adoption of advanced MEMS probe cards is expected to accelerate from 2027.

FormFactor's manufacturing expansion in Farmers Branch, TX, is expected to strengthen its long-term growth prospects by increasing production capacity and improving manufacturing efficiency. The facility is scheduled to begin production late in the fourth quarter of 2026, with capacity ramping throughout 2027. The expansion will support growing demand for advanced MEMS probe cards used in GPUs, custom ASICs and next-generation memory products. The company's growing presence in strengthens its position in the global advanced semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.

Conclusion

FormFactor's strong exposure to AI infrastructure, advanced packaging and growing demand for semiconductor testing solutions bodes well for its long-term prospects. However, manufacturing capacity constraints, unfavorable DRAM product mix and elevated operating expenses remain concerns. Moreover, FORM's stretched valuation and significant YTD share price appreciation limit near-term upside potential. Investors may consider holding the stock ahead of third-quarter earnings, awaiting greater clarity on sustainable margin expansion and capacity improvements.

FORM currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

Fiscal 2026 was a strong year, with revenue up 26.0% to $23.2 billion, net income up 35.6% to $7.3 billion, and gross margin improving to 50.5%. Even so, the stock trades at about 51.8 times trailing earnings and 31.5 times forward earnings, which means investors are already paying a high price for that growth.

The bullish view is that AI is making chip manufacturing harder, and harder chips need more advanced equipment. AI chips require more sophisticated deposition and etch steps, which helps Lam Research Corporation as chipmakers expand capacity for AI, high-performance computing, and high-bandwidth memory. The results so far support this view, as revenue has grown steadily from $14.9 billion in fiscal 2024 to $18.4 billion in fiscal 2025, before rising again in fiscal 2026. The company also generated $4.9 billion in free cash flow, the cash left over after running and investing in the business.

Story Continues

Profitability adds to the case. The company keeps a 35.3% operating margin, meaning a healthy share of every sales dollar turns into profit, and it holds about $1.9 billion more in cash than debt. If chipmakers keep investing in advanced manufacturing capacity, bulls expect several more years of earnings growth, which is why investors are willing to pay a premium price for the stock.

Analysts are also positive. Shares of Lam Research Corporation trade at about $298.22, while the average analyst price target is $373.13, which suggests roughly 25% upside. Targets range widely from $290 to $500, reflecting different views on AI growth, the chip recovery, and geopolitical uncertainty. Analysts also expect earnings per share to rise from $5.76 over the past year to $9.47 over the next, a sign they see growth continuing as chip spending improves.

The main risk is a slowdown in chip capital spending. If AI demand stays strong, investors would expect higher profits, but the stock already trades at a demanding price, slightly above the peer median of 50.7 times trailing earnings, so there is little room for disappointment. Tighter U.S.-China export rules could also limit equipment sales to China, while Chinese equipment makers keep trying to replace foreign suppliers.

Another risk for the stock is that supply constraints could prevent Lam from meeting strong demand. Its equipment relies on specialized components, some sourced from a single supplier or a limited group of suppliers. Lam warns that disruptions could delay deliveries, raise costs, and hurt financial results. Finding and approving replacement suppliers can take time because components must meet demanding technical standards. Holding extra inventory offers protection but also ties up cash and creates potential losses if customer requirements change. This means rising AI orders do not automatically translate into timely revenue and cash flow. In our opinion, delivery bottlenecks could pressure Lam's margins and valuation even if chipmakers continue investing heavily.

Hedge fund positioning shows a strong signal for Lam Research Corporation. (see why Barometer Capital Management is bullish on LRCX ) As per our database, 139 hedge fund portfolios held the stock at the end of the second quarter, up from 123 in the previous quarter. That is a sizeable jump, showing institutional investors are adding to their positions at a steady pace. Among peers, Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) was held by 137 hedge funds, down from 138, while KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) was held by 81 hedge funds, up from 71, and Onto Innovation (NYSE:ONTO) was held by 75 hedge funds, up from 67. The divergence suggests institutional investors showed the strongest increase in conviction toward Lam Research Corporation, while Applied Materials remained relatively stable with only a marginal dip in ownership, and KLA Corporation and Onto Innovation gained investor attention as funds adjusted semiconductor equipment exposure based on growth expectations, restructuring opportunities, and valuation differences.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture across the semiconductor equipment space. Short interest in Lam Research Corporation stands at 2.07% of float, compared with 1.71% for Applied Materials, Inc., 1.86% for KLA Corporation, and 7.68% for Onto Innovation Inc. The low readings for Lam Research Corporation, Applied Materials, Inc., and KLA Corporation suggest few investors are betting against them, while the higher figure for Onto Innovation Inc. points to more caution around its valuation or near-term outlook.

Valuation Analysis

LRCX's forward P/E is 24.88x. KLA Corporation, Onto Innovation Inc., and Applied Materials, Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 26.95x, 16.84x, and 21.14x, respectively. LRCX's own forward P/E was 34.97x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 29% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about memory spending cycles, U.S.-China export restrictions, and whether AI-driven demand can sustain strong equipment sales. However, the historical discount appears encouraging given Lam's continued profitability and growth, although its premiums to Applied Materials and Onto Innovation mean the shares are not uniformly cheap against peers. Lam Research's fiscal 2026 revenue increased 26% to $23.2 billion, while net income rose approximately 36% to $7.3 billion and free cash flow reached roughly $4.9 billion. We believe the current valuation can be justified if earnings continue expanding at a healthy pace, without requiring the latest growth rate to persist, but a slowdown accompanied by a lower multiple would weaken returns. If Lam can maintain its technology leadership and convert high-bandwidth memory investment and increasing chip complexity into sustained earnings growth, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite its exposure to cyclical customer spending.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Lam Research Corporation (LRCX) by The Antifragile Investor in May 2025, which highlighted its semiconductor equipment moat, recurring services revenue, switching costs, and long-term positioning across advanced chip manufacturing. LRCX's stock price has appreciated by approximately 177.93% since our coverage. We believe LRCX could be a good long-term investment, as its current valuation offers an attractive entry point if AI and memory investment support sustained earnings growth through the semiconductor cycle.

Lam Research Corporation is on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds .
