Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the quarter, Silicon Motion unveiled its MonTitan SSD Reference Design Kit, targeting AI infrastructure with high-performance, scalable storage solutions. The kit helps accelerate SSD development, enabling faster data processing, improved efficiency and optimized storage performance for demanding AI workloads, data centers and next-generation computing systems.

The company is expected to benefit from growing demand for enterprise storage solutions, AI infrastructure and automotive applications in the third quarter of 2026. Management expects revenues to increase 15-20% sequentially, supported primarily by its Ferri automotive storage products, enterprise boot drive solutions and MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers. The ongoing commercial ramp of MonTitan, coupled with healthy customer order patterns across storage solutions, is expected to support the company's near-term performance.

SIMO's embedded storage business is another potential growth driver. The company continues to gain market share in eMMC and UFS controllers as NAND suppliers focus more resources on higher-priority memory products. However, rising NAND and DRAM prices remain a potential headwind. Higher component costs are making smartphones and PCs less affordable, particularly in lower-priced segments

Story Continues

Price Performance

Over the past year, SIMO has surged 81.9% compared with the industry's growth of 97.6%. It has underperformed peers like Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL and Western Digital Corporation WDC over this period. While Marvell has gained 157.5%, WDC has jumped 171.3%.

Key Valuation Metric

From a valuation standpoint, Silicon Motion appears to be trading at a premium relative to the industry and above its mean. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 12.17 forward earnings, higher than 9.6 for the industry but lower than the stock's mean of 22.81.

Investment Considerations

SIMO's expanding exposure to enterprise storage, automotive applications and AI infrastructure strengthens its long-term growth opportunity. The company's controller technology, established relationships with NAND manufacturers, and growing presence in higher-value storage solutions could help it capture demand as computing workloads become more storage-intensive. The increasing contribution of MonTitan and enterprise boot drive products also offers an opportunity to reduce dependence on consumer-oriented markets over time.

Profitability is another factor worth monitoring. Management expects the third quarter to benefit from a more favorable product mix, particularly the rising contribution of MonTitan and PCIe Gen5 controllers.

However, SIMO is exposed to volatility in the consumer market. Weak smartphone and PC demand, elevated memory prices, intense competition and uncertainty surrounding component availability could limit growth in established product categories.

End Note

Expanding enterprise storage operations, market-share gains in embedded controllers and increasing demand for automotive and AI-related storage solutions are major tailwinds as SIMO is set to release third-quarter results. Nevertheless, higher memory costs, weakness in consumer markets and the pace of enterprise product adoption remain key variables. SIMO's diversification strategy boosts prospects for the long run, but in the near term, the company demonstrates a balanced outlook. Long-term investors should hold on to the stock, but new investors should wait for a better entry point.

On October 23, 2026, Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS) closed at $83.43, with a $19.62 billion market capitalization. Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS) posted an 31.35% YTD gain, trading within a 52-week range of $51.93 to $92.80.

Vulcan Value Partners stated the following regarding Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"During the quarter, we sold Qorvo and used that capital to purchase shares of Skyworks Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ:SWKS). Both companies design and manufacture radio frequency (RF) semiconductors that enable wireless connectivity across mobile devices, industrial equipment, autos, broadband infrastructure, WiFi devices, and aerospace & defense systems. Apple is a major customer for both Skyworks and Qorvo. The two companies benefit from increasing complexity in RF semiconductors driven by increasing bandwidth, higher levels of data throughput, lower latency, and increasingly smaller form factors. In October 2025, Skyworks announced that it intended to acquire Qorvo, which it completed on October 5, 2026. We think this acquisition makes a lot of sense. Management is targeting over $500 million of cost synergies on approximately $8 billion of combined revenue. These synergies will come from consolidating underutilized fabs and R&D capacity, as well as from SG&A redundancies. The acquisition price included both Skyworks stock as well as a cash component. Because both businesses were discounted and Qorvo shareholders would receive cash, we found it more advantageous to own Skyworks and have 100% exposure to upside in the equity value. We therefore sold our stake in Qorvo and purchased Skyworks. Skyworks' price increased meaningfully in the third quarter. The stock benefitted from increasing certainty around the regulatory approval of the acquisition. Additionally, Skyworks reported a solid third quarter and its iPhone 17 content came in better than anticipated. We continue to like Skyworks and believe its acquisition of Qorvo will unlock meaningful value for shareholders."

news.Title: Down 22.5% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why You Should You Buy the Dip in KLA (KLAC)
news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) has been on a downward spiral lately with significant selling pressure. After declining 22.5% over the past four weeks, the stock looks well positioned for a trend reversal as it is now in oversold territory and there is strong agreement among Wall Street analysts that the company will report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.

RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

Why a Trend Reversal is Due for KLAC

The RSI reading of 23.08 for KLAC is an indication that the heavy selling could be in the process of exhausting itself, so the stock could bounce back in a quest for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

The RSI value is not the only factor that indicates a potential turnaround for the stock in the near term. On the fundamental side, there has been strong agreement among the sell-side analysts covering the stock in raising earnings estimates for the current year. Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for KLAC has increased 0.4%. And an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

Moreover, KLAC currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. news.Title: Don't Overlook Texas Instruments (TXN) International Revenue Trends While Assessing the Stock
news.Content:
Have you assessed how the international operations of Texas Instruments (TXN) performed in the quarter ended September 2026? For this chipmaker, possessing an expansive global footprint, parsing the trends of international revenues could be critical to gauge its financial resilience and growth prospects.

In today's increasingly interconnected global economy, a company's ability to tap into international markets can be a pivotal factor in shaping its overall financial health and growth trajectory. For investors, understanding a company's reliance on overseas markets has become increasingly crucial, as it offers insights into the company's sustainability of earnings, ability to tap into diverse economic cycles and overall growth potential.

Being present in foreign markets serves as protection against local economic declines and helps benefit from more rapidly expanding economies. Yet, such expansion also introduces challenges related to currency fluctuations, geopolitical uncertainties and varied market behaviors.

While delving into TXN's performance for the past quarter, we observed some fascinating trends in the revenue from its foreign segments that are commonly modeled and observed by analysts on Wall Street.

The recent quarter saw the company's total revenue reaching $6.06 billion, marking an improvement of 27.7% from the prior-year quarter. Next, we'll examine the breakdown of TXN's revenue from abroad to comprehend the significance of its international presence.

A Look into TXN's International Revenue Streams

Of the total revenue, $104 million came from Rest of World during the last fiscal quarter, accounting for 1.7%. This represented a surprise of -5.62% as analysts had expected the region to contribute $110.19 million to the total revenue. In comparison, the region contributed $98 million, or 1.8%, and $74 million, or 1.6%, to total revenue in the previous and year-ago quarters, respectively.

During the quarter, Europe, Middle East and Africa contributed $1.21 billion in revenue, making up 19.9% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $1.24 billion, this meant a surprise of -2.52%. Looking back, Europe, Middle East and Africa contributed $1.08 billion, or 19.7%, in the previous quarter, and $972 million, or 20.5%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Japan generated $369 million in revenues for the company in the last quarter, constituting 6.1% of the total. This represented a surprise of -0.87% compared to the $372.23 million projected by Wall Street analysts. Comparatively, in the previous quarter, Japan accounted for $330 million (6%), and in the year-ago quarter, it contributed $313 million (6.6%) to the total revenue.

Story Continues

Rest of Asia accounted for 10.5% of the company's total revenue during the quarter, translating to $635 million. Revenues from this region represented a surprise of -1.4%, with Wall Street analysts collectively expecting $644 million. When compared to the preceding quarter and the same quarter in the previous year, Rest of Asia contributed $606 million (11.1%) and $505 million (10.7%) to the total revenue, respectively.

During the quarter, China contributed $1.39 billion in revenue, making up 23% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $1.28 billion, this meant a surprise of +8.77%. Looking back, China contributed $1.22 billion, or 22.4%, in the previous quarter, and $1.02 billion, or 21.5%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Projected Revenues in Foreign Markets

It is projected by analysts on Wall Street that Texas Instruments will post revenues of $6.09 billion for the ongoing fiscal quarter, an increase of 37.7% from the year-ago quarter. The expected contributions from Rest of World, Europe, Middle East and Africa, Japan, Rest of Asia and China to this revenue are 1.6%, 17.8%, 5.3%, 9.3%, and 18.4%, translating into $100.02 million, $1.09 billion, $320.74 million, $564.85 million, and $1.12 billion, respectively.

For the full year, a total revenue of $22.26 billion is expected for the company, reflecting an increase of 25.9% from the year before. The revenues from Rest of World, Europe, Middle East and Africa, Japan, Rest of Asia and China are expected to make up 1.8%, 20.1%, 5.9%, 10.6%, and 20.9% of this total, corresponding to $399.21 million, $4.47 billion, $1.31 billion, $2.37 billion, and $4.65 billion, respectively.

In Conclusion

Relying on global markets for revenues presents both prospects and challenges for Texas Instruments. Therefore, scrutinizing its international revenue trends is key to effectively forecasting the company's future outlook.

With the increasing intricacies of global interdependence and geopolitical strife, Wall Street analysts meticulously observe these patterns, especially for companies with an international footprint, to tweak their forecasts of earnings. Importantly, several additional factors, such as a company's domestic market status, also impact these earnings forecasts.

Emphasizing a company's shifting earnings prospects is a key aspect of our approach at Zacks, especially since research has proven its substantial influence on a stock's price in the short run. This correlation is positively aligned, meaning that improved earnings projections tend to boost the stock's price.

The Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool, comes with an externally validated impressive track record. It effectively utilizes shifts in earnings projections to act as a dependable barometer for forecasting short-term stock price trends.

Texas Instruments currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), indicating that it could outperform the broader market in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Reviewing Texas Instruments' Recent Stock Price Trends

Over the preceding four weeks, the stock's value has appreciated by 2.4%, against a downturn of 1.2% in the Zacks S&P 500 composite. In parallel, the Zacks Computer and Technology sector, which counts Texas Instruments among its entities, has depreciated by 7.7%. Over the past three months, the company's shares have seen an increase of 3.3% versus the S&P 500's 2.5% increase. The sector overall has witnessed an increase of 0.3% over the same period.

news.Content:

ETFs sold $11.5 million in NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) stock last Thursday, a net selling figure that came despite more funds trading the other way: 35 ETFs bought shares while 14 sold, though in smaller amounts. The move snapped a run of net buying, with inflows of $45.4 million on Oct. 21, $94.1 million on Oct. 20, $62.6 million on Oct. 19 and $8.3 million on Oct. 16. ETF activity left 121 funds holding the stock unchanged. The selling streak stands at one day.

What does NXPI do?

NXP Semiconductors NV is a Dutch-American semiconductor company that designs and manufactures high-performance mixed-signal and analog chips. Its largest segment is automotive, where it supplies microcontrollers, processors, analog and interface devices, and secure connectivity for powertrains, infotainment, radar, and vehicle networking.

NXP reported trailing-12-month revenue of $13.19 billion, up 9.6% year over year, with gross margin of 55.1% and net margin of 22.9%.
